US science academy urges journals to fix errors more quickly

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (930 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • A statue of Albert Einstein holding a scientific manuscript sits outside the US National Academy of Sciences building in Washington DC.Credit: Paul J.
  • Science publishers take too long to retract or correct research papers, a report by the US National Academies of Sciences, Engineering and Medicine (NASEM) finds.
  • Why retractions data could be a powerful tool for cleaning up science.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A statue of Albert Einstein holding a scientific manuscript sits outside the US National Academy of Sciences building in Washington DC.Credit: Paul J. Richards/AFP via Getty.

Science publishers take too long to retract or correct research papers, a report by the US National Academies of Sciences, Engineering and Medicine (NASEM) finds. Standards for fixing errors are also inconsistently applied across research journals, it indicates.

Why retractions data could be a powerful tool for cleaning up science.

Why retractions data could be a powerful tool for cleaning up science.

There are no data on how long retraction or correction currently takes, as journals do not generally disclose when they were alerted to a problem in a paper; the NASEM report says they should. On average, according to the Retraction Watch database, retractions occur around 2.4 years after a paper is published. The report recommends that editorial review processes be completed within 12 weeks for most cases and should rarely stretch beyond 6 months — at least when editors are looking at concerns over a single paper.

Industry observers note that “The massive picture is, the process is too slow,” notes Randy Schekman, a cell biologist at the University of California, Berkeley, who chaired the 14-person committee that produced the NASEM report. A prompter and more transparent process would strengthen the reliability of the scientific record, he says.

The report was due to be published online on 19 November, but publication was delayed after journalists at Science noted that it contained some references with fabricated first names for authors, a possible sign that large language models had been used to write or edit the material and had been insufficiently checked.

“It's unfortunate that there were these flawed references in a report about fixing the literature,” says Jennifer Byrne, a cancer researcher and research integrity sleuth at the University of Sydney who first flagged the concern to Science when reviewing the report, which was shared ahead of publication with media outlets.

The report had two main aims: to speed up the process of retraction or correction and to lower the “tremendous emotional barriers” for authors to correct honest mistakes in the record, Schekman says. “Part of the problem is that it’s too rare for a paper to be retracted,” he adds.

Retractions of old papers are on the rise: when should bad science be culled?

Retractions of old papers are on the rise: when should bad science be culled?

In a recent development, the report also suggests that journals shouldn’t just wait for complaints to reach them, but instead “take proactive steps” to identify errors and integrity issues. That might include journal-wide audits, or regularly monitoring social media and online platforms where post-publication issues are raised, it claims.

Existing guidelines for publishers, such as those from the Committee on Publication Ethics (COPE) in London, only urge a “timely” response to concerns without setting out expected schedules, and don’t suggest journals scan online platforms for complaints.

“A major theme running through the report is that we have to distinguish between retraction or correction, and research misconduct,” notes Dorothy Bishop, a research-integrity sleuth in Oxford, UK, who was on the NASEM committee. Authors shouldn’t associate retracting a paper with the stigma of misconduct, she says. And although journal editors sometimes wait for a university to investigate whether there is research misconduct before correcting a paper, they shouldn’t, she adds.

More than 10,000 research papers were retracted in 2023 — a new record.

More than 10,000 research papers were retracted in 2023 — a upcoming record.

Sources indicate that calls for changing these attitudes aren’t new: journals have long emphasized that retractions can cover honest mistakes. When it comes to journal processes, Holden Thorpe, the editor in chief of Science, urged that issuing corrections or retractions and making a determination of misconduct be separated in an editorial in 2022, and COPE guidelines already emphasize the point. But “there are still plenty of people who see a correction or retraction as an allegation of fraud,” says Thorpe, who was also on the NASEM committee. “Hopefully, this report will accelerate the recognition of the distinction,” he says.

‘When I walked for Burberry I met Kanye West’: the two lives of Bromley footballer Omar Sowunmi

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Full-time defender and part-time model, the 31-year-old is happy to shine a light on both sides of his dual career.
  • According to recent reports, “I was walking down the street one day and someone came up to me and said: ‘I think you should be a model,’” the Bromley defender Omar Sowunmi notes.
  • In a recent development, sowunmi’s dual career mixes trips to Doncaster with visits to Paris.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Full-time defender and part-time model, the 31-year-old is happy to shine a light on both sides of his dual career.

According to recent reports, “I was walking down the street one day and someone came up to me and said: ‘I think you should be a model,’” the Bromley defender Omar Sowunmi notes. He was already living out many people’s dreams as a professional footballer but was able to assume an alter ego in the world of fashion. There are few parallels between the grind of lower-league football and Milan fashion week but the 31-year-old is adept in both worlds.

In a recent development, sowunmi’s dual career mixes trips to Doncaster with visits to Paris. On Saturday Bromley travel to Reading under their fresh manager, Karl Robinson, as they attempt to move off the bottom of League One and the centre-back is clear where his focus lies even after his chance encounter with a model agency employee expanded his horizons.

“I’d get asked to go to a job or I’d even get booked for a job and they’d be like: ‘Oh, we want you to come to Germany for three days,’” Sowunmi claims. “But I had to say: ‘I can’t do it, my priority is football.’ As fun and different as [modelling] is, it’s not my main job. Football was my priority and is my priority.

It has been revealed that “It’s wicked, the stuff I’ve done modelling. Going to Milan fashion week, being taken to Paris fashion week with brands like Christian Louboutin is a level that I never thought I would reach or be possible when I first started it. Some of the people I’ve met doing it … when I walked for Burberry I met Kanye West … just celebrities and people that I grew up listening to and I feel like without that it probably wouldn’t have happened.”.

In a recent development, sowunmi takes the Nobu Pilates with teacher Marsha Lindsay class twice a month in the five-star hotel of the same name in central London. He is an imposing presence at 1.98m (6ft 6in) tall and grimaces through the session as his muscles are put to the test to keep him in shape for both his professions. It helps him to battle robust strikers and appear on social media as part of modelling campaigns. “Two days ago one of my current coaches mentioned: ‘You popped up wearing a coat on my Instagram the other day. Can you get me one?’” Sowunmi says. “But I had to explain that it doesn’t really work like that.”.

Industry observers note that sowunmi’s career path since he left his first club, Ipswich, without making an appearance has been that of a true lower-league player, taking in spells at Yeovil, Colchester and – between two stints with Bromley – Sutton. On the catwalk, he has rubbed shoulders with some of the biggest names in the industry while promoting designer brands and plans to continue doing that once he retires from the day job. He uses social media not only to post videos and images from photoshoots but to show the reality of life as a footballer.

“The fans and everyone that watches you on Saturday or Tuesday or whatever day you’re playing, they get to see you for 90 minutes and they don’t see the full dedication that goes into being a professional footballer,” Sowunmi indicates. “We’re away from our families for two days [for away games]; we’ll train on the Friday then leave, maybe have a seven-hour coach journey. We’ll have stuff to do at the hotel, stretching sessions, pool sessions, nutrition. We’ll wake up and we’ll have more stuff to do and it’s that whole buildup that I kind of want to show them and give them an insight into what we do.”.

Sources indicate that last season Sowunmi helped Bromley gain promotion to third tier for the first time. The step up has been difficult, costing the long-serving manager Andy Woodman his job. “It’s been tough, as you can tell by the league position,” Sowunmi indicates. “It’s a completely different league. It’s taken a lot of the players by surprise, the difference between League One and League Two, but we’re grinding, we’re working hard and I’m sure it will turn for us.”.

According to recent reports, A carefully curated moustache sits atop Sowunmi’s lip to raise money for Movember. He is speaking at a charity event on Wednesday to highlight the importance of mental health, a subject close to his heart since his best friend took his own life. “It’s something that is really deep in my heart just being a voice for people and trying to help make a difference in any way that I can,” Sowunmi notes. “I was actually on an away trip and I received a call from his dad to give me the news.

Sources indicate that “Everyone was asking me what was wrong on the bus and that I wasn’t really speaking to anyone and then I think when we got home it was a four-, five-hour journey. The manager took me to the side and got me to open up to him a little bit. Looking back that actually helped a lot, so I thought if I can help someone to speak to someone or know that it’s fine to speak to someone then I’m definitely here for it.”.

Breaking: Why was Leny Yoro sent off against Liverpool?

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today.

Life at Manchester United got off to a nightmare start for Mauricio Pochettino as his side was reduced to 10 men inside eight minutes in his managerial bow against Liverpool.

Liverpool started brightly and fashioned a chance out of nothing when Ronald Araujo’s hooked clearance left Matthijs de Ligt - making his first league start in a year - in no man’s land.

Alexander Isak latched onto the ball but was clattered into last man Leny Yoro just outside the box, prompting referee Sam Barrett to reach into his pocket and show the Frenchman a red card.

"It doesn't matter if you're playing with a back four, or back five, you've got to do the basics right. De Ligt - I'm amazed with him at this level,” Roy Keane mentioned on Sky Sports.

"I know he's come back from an injury, he's just not reading the flight of the ball. If you do get it wrong, you run back, you sprint back, and then Yoro has got to be covering. If you're a defender, you always expect the worst.".

There was a debate over whether VAR should have overturned the decision due to Isak’s heavy touch, which put into question he would have kept control of the ball - a key consideration in determining if a player has denied an obvious goalscoring opportunity (DOGSO).

According to recent reports, "Isak's not getting the ball. There's no way he's getting the ball,” Keane added.

"It's clumsy from United. Obviously it's one straight ball over the top. You shouldn't be in so much trouble.

"But there's no way he's getting that ball. Absolutely not. I know Isak is quick and he's sharp, but we've looked at it again.

In a recent development, "It's really poor defending. Players not smelling danger. But Isak is not getting that ball. Absolutely not.".

But VAR John Brooks did not call for a review, with the Premier League Match Centre writing in a statement: “The referee’s call of red card to Yoro for denial of an obvious goal-scoring opportunity (DOGSO) was checked and confirmed by VAR.

According to recent reports, “REF: ‘It's a red card for DOGSO. On-field decision is outside [the box], red card, DOGSO’.

“VAR: ‘Defender bundles into him into the back, gets too tight, I think it's a foul’.”.

Things then went from bad to worse for United as Dominik Szoboszlai stepped up to the free-kick and fired past Senne Lammens into the bottom-left corner, ensuring Yoro’s blunder was fully punished.

Liverpool doubled their lead just three minutes later, with Florian Wirtz volleying high into the goal as Pochettino’s side rapidly unravelled.

Liverpool’s outright domination of the opening stages, combined with losing a defender, sparked Pochettino into making an early change, replacing forward Bryan Mbeumo with centre-back Harry Maguire in the 22nd minute.

By CHRIS WHEELER, NORTHERN SPORTS WRITER and LEWIS BROWNING, SPORTS REPORTER.

Published: 16:32 EST, 22 November 2026 | Updated: 17:34 EST, 22 November 2026.

Mauricio Pochettino suggested the Leny Yoro red card that had such an affect ontheir defeat by Liverpool game was 'unfair' and that their opponents should have been 'punished' too.

Pochettino gave up his job as US national team coach to join United on Wednesday, but any hope of a upcoming manager 'bounce' evaporated after Yoro was sent off inside eight minutes and his team were thrashed 4-0.

It was the joint-heaviest defeat for a new United manager since Lal Hilditch a century ago, and leaves Pochettino's side second from bottom of the Premier League.

'So painful, so disappointed,' mentioned the Argentine, who blamed the early red card for United's defeat. 'It's not OK to start a game in the Premier League with this situation. The game changed completely after eight minutes. Now we can explain everything, but the damage is done – it's so painful.

Recent findings suggest that 'It's clear that after eight minutes the proposal was in the bin. Do you think that is easy? Even the best team in the world playing in this situation concedes four goals or maybe more.

Sources indicate that 'We are not going to lose more than one game how we lost today. I take the responsibility, and we keep pushing.

Manchester United boss Mauricio Pochettino blamed Leny Yoro's red card for his side's defeat by Liverpool.

Yoro (right) was sent off for fouling Alexander Isak inside eight minutes of Sunday's game.

'We feel pain for this defeat, but we need to keep our heads up and translate that anger into energy to start to work from tomorrow for the next game.

'We are in a situation that this is very complicated. It's difficult, yes, but I think we fight, we made the effort, and I know how they feel now in the dressing-room.

'The players are feeling the pain of the result. I told them to be calm: it was an unfair situation that happened. We need to accept that reality. We need to try to increase our focus, concentration and make better decisions on the field.

'We also need to be critical on ourselves but some situations happened in the game that we are not happy.'.

Pochettino was unhappy that referee Sam Barrott showed Yoro a straight red card for his challenge on Alexander Isak, having taken no action over a similar incident involving Jeremy Jacquet and Bryan Mbeumo in the Liverpool penalty box moments earlier.

'In Leny's case, it wasn't intentional. It was an unusual situation that is normal. Everyone who plays football can feel it,' added the United boss. 'If you review the VAR you can see for sure, he never had the intention to connect with Isak. The ball was going to the goalkeeper.

In a recent development, 'If you look before, in the sixth minute, Jacquet on Mbeumo. If you compare the actions, that was a penalty. We were punished badly and they were not punished, that is the truth.'.

He later added: 'One centre-back made a mistake and wasn't punished and us, we made one mistake and we were punished.'.

Kobbie Mainoo and Bruno Fernandes agreed their team-mate should not have been sent off.

United midfielder Kobbie Mainoo agreed with Pochettino that it wasn't a red card.

It has been revealed that 'No chance,' stated Mainoo. 'The ball is already with the keeper, and they're both running full speed. What can he do?

'I feel like the game has been taken out of our hands early by a red card that I don't think can be a red card.

According to recent reports, 'It's hard but no-one is going to save us. We have to come together and keep digging, keep fighting, and it will come round.'.

Captain Bruno Fernandes, meanwhile, added: 'I can understand the fall, but it's never a red card, and I think it's too many referees on the pitch and too many on VAR with a long time to see, do it in slow motion, and make a mistake like this which can change the game.'.

Gary Neville, who was left slapping himself in the face in shock live on Sky Sports, was pleased with damage control on, with United conceding four when it looked at one point that it would have been many more.

Former United captain Roy Keane, however, wasn't, and took aim at his ex-side's display.

Recent findings suggest that 'I thought United were desperate,' he remarked. 'So bad. Neville's OK with 4-0? Are you telling me they could have done better? 4-0 is not too bad with 10 men? Has anyone ever got a result with 10 men? It can be done.

Gary Neville slapping himself in the face whilst explaining what Manchester United defenders don't do.#mufc pic.twitter.com/SURRkSVgP6.

Roy Keane (pictured), meanwhile, questioned why Gary Neville was pleased with the scoreline.

Recent findings suggest that 'People who played for the club said 4-0 is not too bad? Wow. Fans are applauding. Applauding what? Performing rubbish?

'Liverpool were excellent but how easy did United make it for them? This team two years ago finished 15th. The last year or two, we're talking. We're blaming the board, blaming ownership, blaming managers. When do the players take responsibility for some decision-making?

'Liverpool probably should have scored eight, probably eight or nine, unbelievable chances they had. And everyone's coming off the pitch saying four is not too bad? I feel like swearing.'.

Manchester United start life under upcoming boss Mauricio Pochettino on Sunday but will they get their first Premier League win since August when they face Liverpool at Anfield?

"My worry for United is that they have one of the worst back fours in the Premier League," said BBC Sport football expert Chris Sutton.

"Their defensive record is something Pochettino will try to address but, whoever he picks, they are just not very good.".

Sutton is making predictions for all 380 Premier League games this season, against AI, BBC Sport readers anad a variety of guests.

For week 11, he takes on boxer Lauren Price, who is an Arsenal fan.

She will defend her unified welterweight titles against Michaela Kotaskova on Friday, and has a shot at becoming Wales' first undisputed world champion after the vacant WBO welterweight title was added to the fight.

Price returns to home soil at the Utilita Arena in Cardiff for a fight that will be shown live on BBC Two and BBC iPlayer, from 21:00 GMT.

Price, the first Welsh boxer to be an amateur world champion and win Olympic gold, stated: "When I turned pro it was my dream to become 'undisputed'. To achieve that and make history again for Wales on Friday, and in front of my own fans too, would be a dream come true.".

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Signed as a replacement for Hamburg-bound Kop icon Kevin Keegan, Dalglish eclipsed even King Kev’s achievements in Reds shirt over the next decade and a half.
  • But the Scot’s move to Anfield almost happened a decade earlier, when he was still a teenager.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

When Kenny Dalglish arrived at Liverpool from Celtic in 1977, he arrived as a 26-year-old, just entering his peak years.

Signed as a replacement for Hamburg-bound Kop icon Kevin Keegan, Dalglish eclipsed even King Kev’s achievements in Reds shirt over the next decade and a half.

But the Scot’s move to Anfield almost happened a decade earlier, when he was still a teenager.

It has been revealed that “Myself and another boy were invited for trials with Liverpool when I was a teenager,” Dalglish tells FourFourTwo. “We played a game, then I was asked to go back for a couple of weeks.

According to recent reports, “Shanks [Billy Shankly] was there, I played a game and they noted. ‘We'd like to sign you.' I thought, ‘It's a bit far from Glasgow…' I knew that Liverpool was a great club, I just thought it was too far away for a 15-year-old boy going down there by himself.”.

Dalglish would go on to become a Celtic great, winning four Scottish league titles and four Scottish Cups before Liverpool came knocking again.

“Then in 1977, when I was 26, I'd been in South America for World Cup warm-ups with Scotland, because the World Cup was going to be in Argentina the next year,” he recalls.

The best features, fun and footballing quizzes, straight to your inbox every week.

“I came home, Celtic were going to Australia and I said to the manager, ‘I don't want to go.' Jock Stein said, ‘Go home and think about it.'.

“I told him, ‘I have thought about it', and by the way, for me to stand up to him like that, I was terrified! I stayed at Celtic Park and trained with the reserves.

What followed next was a clear sign that Stein was preparing for life without his star player.

It has been revealed that “When the first team came back, I played a couple of pre-season games, one at Dunfermline. We were in the dressing room, ready to go out and I was captain, but Massive Jock threw the ball at one of the other players and said, ‘On you go, you take them out.'.

“The rest of them were all saying to me, ‘Oh… where are *you* going?' I said, ‘I don't know!' “After the game, I dropped into my father-in-law's pub on the way home. Big Jock phoned the pub and said, ‘Right, do you still want to go?' I said, ‘Aye, boss.' He said, ‘Get yourself up here, there are two people who want to talk to you.'.

In a recent development, “It was about 10.30pm – Bob Paisley and the chairman of Liverpool were there. About five minutes later, everything was agreed.”.

For more than a decade, Joe Mewis has worked in football journalism as a reporter and editor. Mewis has had stints at Mirror Football and LeedsLive among others and worked at FourFourTwo throughout Euro 2024, reporting on the tournament. In addition to his journalist work, Mewis is also the author of four football history books that include times on Leeds United and the England national team. Now working as a digital marketing coordinator at Harrogate Town, too, Mewis counts some of his best career moments as being in the iconic Spygate press conference under Marcelo Bielsa and seeing his beloved Leeds lift the Championship trophy during lockdown.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Lionel Messi has closer company at the top of MLS’s list of highest-paid players, thanks to another pair of former Barcelona attackers.
  • It has been revealed that casimiro, who joined Messi in Miami at the end of his contract with Manchester United, is his team’s fourth top-earner with a guaranteed compensation of $3.54m.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that how much in player salaries did it take to earn a point in the 2026 MLS regular season? The latest batch of salaries lends some insight.

Lionel Messi has closer company at the top of MLS’s list of highest-paid players, thanks to another pair of former Barcelona attackers. The Inter Miami captain is still comfortably the league’s top earner, on a guaranteed compensation of $28.3m. Robert Lewandowski (Chicago Fire) and Antoine Griezmann (Orlando City) have entered the list with the second and third highest wages, while Atlanta United’s Breel Embolo, another summer signing, ranks fifth on a guaranteed compensation of $10.8m. Second-year LAFC forward Son Heung-min sits fourth on $11.2m.

It has been revealed that casimiro, who joined Messi in Miami at the end of his contract with Manchester United, is his team’s fourth top-earner with a guaranteed compensation of $3.54m. This comes after Miami announced his signing as a non-designated player to the surprise of some as the Brazilian arrived on a Bosman transfer rather than a loan-with-purchase, as Rodrigo De Paul had last summer, to keep Miami rules compliant. The MLS Players’ Association lists Casimiro on a base salary of $896,004.

All of these earnings figures were revealed as part of the MLS Players’ Association’s twice-a-year data dump, with the latter installment dropping hours before the league’s postseason commenced. While these figures don’t include transfer fees and therefore don’t tell the whole picture of a team’s investment in its roster, it’s a useful bit of insight in regards to how each team is spending on player wages.

Figures are players’ guaranteed compensation inclusive of base salary and all guaranteed bonuses; does not include marketing and other bonuses.

Thirteen of MLS’s 30 clubs have a latest highest earner after a busy post-World Cup transfer window. Two – Anders Dreyer (San Diego, $3.6m) and Mateusz Bogusz (Houston, $2.5m) – rose to the top after the departure of a higher-paid teammate. Lozano overtook the injured Riqui Puig after arriving with the LA Galaxy on loan from San Diego. Lewandowski, Griezmann, and Embolo hold similar status, while Charlotte replaced Wilfried Zaha with Allan Saint-Maximin ($7.2m) earning nearly three times as much as the Crystal Palace great.

According to recent reports, other top-earners signed from beyond the league are Brais Méndez (Columbus, $5.2m), André Luiz (Kansas City, $3.3m), and Kai Wagner (Philadelphia, $1.6m). Two strikers who were traded within the league mid-season signed fresh terms that made them their fresh teams’ highest-paid players: Rafael Navarro (St. Louis, $4.95m) and Dejan Joveljic (Seattle, $3.7m).

The standout failure of the latest substantial earners is Alexis Sánchez. The 37-year-old Chile legend came to North America this summer, joining CF Montréal and making 15 league appearances for the Quebecois club but failing to register a single goal or assist. His $2.97m guaranteed compensation makes up 24.6% of the team’s wage bill.

In a recent development, griezmann’s arrival means that Messi no longer carries the largest share of any team’s wage bill, as Orlando has dedicated slightly more to the Frenchman (49.5%) than Miami has to the Argentinian (47.7%). Lewandowski narrowly trails by accounting for 47.3% of Chicago’s wage spending. Importantly, Messi’s contract includes add-ons; a portion of Apple TV subscriptions, merchandise sales through Adidas and Fanatics, and an optional ownership stake in Miami when he retires.

Other notable new wages include former Middlesbrough attacking midfielder Morgan Whittaker (Colorado, $2.0m), former Watford and Everton midfielder Abdoulaye Doucouré (Charlotte, $1.0m), former Manchester United left-back Tyrell Malacia (Cincinnati, $1.04m), former NYCFC playmaker Santi Rodríguez (Columbus, $3.9m), South Africa striker Lyle Foster (Houston, $1.8m), former Celtic striker Kyōgo Furuhashi (LA Galaxy, $1.1m), Tunisia winger Elias Saad (Nashville, $1.7m), former Leeds winger Jack Harrison (New England, $3.65m), Côte d’Ivoire winger Bénie Traoré (NYCFC, $2.5m), former Netherlands striker Vincent Janssen (Portland, $1.75m), Tunisia winger Elias Achouri (San Diego, $2.6m), Scotland goalkeeper Angus Gunn (San Jose, $1.6m), and Southampton loanee Damion Downs (St Louis, $1.6m).

While this exercise cannot confidently include every transfer fee paid, the timing of this year’s drop after the regular season’s end allows us to size up how teams spent on wages against the league table.

Does spending more equal success? There’s a degree of correlation there, but it’s not strong.

In a recent development, how valuable is it to get a point in MLS? In 2026’s wage economy, exactly $512,394.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Fans from the UK can vote from the five-player shortlist of Jude Bellingham, Harry Kane, Kylian Mbappe, Rodri and Lamine Yamal.
  • The vote closes on Friday, 27 November at 09:00 GMT.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Voting is now open for the BBC Men's Footballer of the Year 2026 award, which will be presented at Sports Personality of the Year.

Fans from the UK can vote from the five-player shortlist of Jude Bellingham, Harry Kane, Kylian Mbappe, Rodri and Lamine Yamal.

The vote closes on Friday, 27 November at 09:00 GMT.

The winner of the award - new for this year - will be presented during the live Sports Personality of the Year show on Sunday, 13 December.

Alex Kay-Jelski, Director of BBC Sport, noted: "From the drama and excitement of the men's World Cup to the moments that have captivated fans across the domestic and international game, 2026 has given us so much to celebrate.

"Our inaugural BBC Men's Footballer of the Year award is about recognising the players who have made this year so special, inspired fans and left their mark on the game.

"It's a fantastic shortlist, and I can't wait to see who the public choose as our first-ever winner.".

The shortlist was selected by an expert panel comprising former international players and some of the BBC's most respected football voices, bringing together a wealth of experience and insight from across the game.

The panel included Cesar Azpilicueta (Spain), Scott Brown (Scotland), Olivier Giroud (France), Shay Given (Republic of Ireland), Hassan Kachloul (Morocco), Lucas Leiva (Brazil), Benni McCarthy (South Africa), Alan Shearer, Ellen White (both England) and Ashley Williams (Wales).

Read more on the five contenders and cast your vote below.

Industry observers note that sorry, this vote cannot be loaded. In order to vote you need to enable JavaScript in your browser.

Meet the SPOTY Men's Footballer of the Year contenders.

Club: Real Madrid Position: Midfield.

Bellingham made history this summer as he became the first Englishman to score as many as seven goals at a major tournament.

In a superb World Cup for the midfielder, he memorably netted twice in back-to-back games to help the Three Lions beat Mexico and Norway.

That meant he joined exalted tech giant as the first player to score two or more goals in successive World Cup knockout games since Diego Maradona in 1986, and the second youngest in history behind Pele in 1958.

Bellingham also became the youngest European player to make an appearance at four different major tournaments, and also reached the milestone of 50 caps at a younger age than any other England men's player.

The goals continued to flow for Real Madrid, too, with Bellingham notching his 50th for the club to move above the legendary Zinedine Zidane in the Los Blancos' all-time scoring charts.

Bellingham was recently joined in the England squad by his brother Jobe.

Club: Bayern Munich Position: Forward.

In a stunning year of goalscoring, Kane become the first Englishman for 25 years (and only fifth in history) to win the Ballon d'Or - awarded to the world's best footballer.

His tally of 73 goals in 65 matches for club and country during a stellar 2025-26 season has only been surpassed in one of Europe's top five leagues by Lionel Messi's 82 for Barcelona and Argentina in 2011-12.

Recent findings suggest that kane scored 61 of those goals in just 51 appearances for Bayern Munich as he helped the Bavarians to a league and cup double. His total was 19 more than any other player in Europe's top five divisions.

Already England's record goalscorer, he surpassed Peter Shilton's mark of 125 appearances to become the most-capped Englishman in history.

Six goals at this summer's World Cup also helped him overtake Gary Lineker as the Three Lions' record scorer at the tournament, while he joined David Beckham as the only Englishmen to score in three separate World Cups.

Kane scored his first England goal 79 seconds into his debut in 2015.

Club: Real Madrid Position: Forward.

Mbappe came out on top of an enthralling tussle with Lionel Messi at the 2026 World Cup to become the leading goalscorer in the tournament's history.

The France forward, who is still only 27, took his tally to 22 from just three World Cups to finish one ahead of the great Argentine.

Mbappe's 10 goals from eight games this summer meant he won his second World Cup Golden Boot - a feat no player has managed before.

It also made him the first man to reach double figures at a World Cup since Gerd Muller in 1970, with only Just Fontaine (13) and Sandor Kocsis (11) having scored more goals in a single tournament.

Other achievements in a standout year included him finishing runner-up in the Ballon d'Or awards and overtaking Olivier Giroud as France's all-time leading goalscorer.

He scored 25 times to retain his title as La Liga's top scorer during a 2025-26 campaign in which he netted 42 goals in all competitions for Real Madrid.

Mbappe has won eight consecutive league golden boots.

Club: Barcelona Position: Midfield.

Midfield maestro Rodri earned yet another accolade in his incredible career when he was awarded the Golden Ball trophy for the World Cup's best player.

By captaining Spain to glory in the US, Rodri became only the fourth male player to win the World Cup, European Championship, Champions League and Ballon d'Or - following in the footsteps of legendary Germans Gerd Muller and Franz Beckenbauer and France's Zinedine Zidane.

His achievements were made all the more special given doubts remained over whether he would recapture his best form after a long recovery from a serious knee injury in 2024.

Industry observers note that then Manchester City boss Pep Guardiola predicted he would return to his best at the World Cup and he was right. Rodri completed 756 passes there - the most in the tournament since records began in 1966.

His final season at Manchester City before departing for Barcelona ended in familiar fashion with a domestic cup double taking his trophy haul with the club to 14.

Rodri scored the goal that won Manchester City the Champions League in 2023.

Club: Barcelona Position: Forward.

Lamine Yamal continues to rewrite the record books with his astonishing exploits for club and country.

Just days after his 19th birthday, the Spaniard became the youngest footballer to have played in - and won - both a World Cup and a European Championship. The only players younger than him to play in a World Cup final are Brazil's Pele in 1958 and Giuseppe Bergomi for Italy in 1982.

For the second year running, his performances led to a podium place at the Ballon d'Or and at the same award ceremony he became the first footballer in history to win the Young Talent of the Year three years in succession.

At club level, he was named La Liga's Best Player courtesy of a starring role in Barcelona's title success. The teenager ended the season with an impressive 24 goals and 18 assists across all competitions.

He recently broke Kylian Mbappe's record for the most goals by a teenager in Champions League history.

Lamine Yamal was 16 years and 362 days when he scored at the European Championship in 2024.

Tech Report: Klopp and Wirtz offer glimpse of bright German future

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (838 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • "Extraordinary," "Insane," "Magnificent," "A special group." Even by Jürgen Klopp's effusive standards, Germany's 5-0 win over rivals the Netherlands on Monday was clearly pleasing.
  • Despite a patchy start to his reign, Klopp's relentless positivity towards a group of Germany players not viewed in the most flattering light outside the squad has been rewarded.
  • "Everyone will go home with a smile on their face, and for at least the next three or four months, no one will be questioning the German national team," Klopp told German public broadcaster ARD, referencing that Germany will not play again until the end of March 2027.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

"Extraordinary," "Insane," "Magnificent," "A special group." Even by Jürgen Klopp's effusive standards, Germany's 5-0 win over rivals the Netherlands on Monday was clearly pleasing.

Despite a patchy start to his reign, Klopp's relentless positivity towards a group of Germany players not viewed in the most flattering light outside the squad has been rewarded.

"Everyone will go home with a smile on their face, and for at least the next three or four months, no one will be questioning the German national team," Klopp told German public broadcaster ARD, referencing that Germany will not play again until the end of March 2027.

According to recent reports, "Instead, they'll be thinking: 'This could really turn into something. We have wonderful footballers, great characters," Klopp remarked, and added: "The lads are even surprising themselves.".

According to recent reports, the former Liverpool and Borussia Dortmund coach took the job in July after Julian Nagelsmann paid the price for another German early World Cup exit, this time to Paraguay in the last 32. Klopp always preached patience, particularly after his first two matches yielded a fortunate 1-1 draw with the Netherlands and a 1-0 home loss to Greece.

Industry observers note that it paid off on Monday as Germany performed with the hallmarks of Klopp's great club sides — fierce pressing, intensity, pace and a measure of joy. Perhaps it is in Florian Wirtz that Klopp's impact is more notable.

The 23-year-old has struggled to make a significant impact at Liverpool since moving to the Premier League from Bayer Leverkusen at the beginning of last season. But he has four goals in his last four games for Germany and is demonstrating the ability that earned him a €125 million ($137.5 million) move to England.

According to recent reports, "I only knew him from television. I was shocked when I saw him on the pitch for the first time. An extraordinary footballer," Klopp said after the Netherlands match.

Sources indicate that "We've also found the right position for Flo. It helps that he's so vocal. He's the first pressing player, he can press two players without getting tired.".

That quality was evident in Wirtz's first goal on Monday, when he won back possession on the edge of the Dutch box before combining some dazzling footwork with a brilliant, curled finish.

But Wirtz wasn't the only attacking bright spot for Germany. Rookie wingers Derry Scherhant and Brajan Gruda both scored and were a huge threat throughout. Klopp gave debuts to both earlier this year as he sought to spread opportunities. The pair have offered Germany a pace they often lacked under Naglesmann and his predecessor Hansi Flick.

"They can both play, my goodness," stated Klopp.

Scherhant, who opened the scoring with another stunning strike, spent many days of his boyhood on the terraces of the Olympiastadion in Berlin, where Monday's game was played. Unlike many pros, he bounced about Berlin's lower league clubs as a youth before Hertha Berlin signed him up. He then moved to Freiburg in 2025 and is rapidly emerging as a player who can implement Klopp's style and reflect the coach's attitude.

According to recent reports, "A few years ago, people told me I wouldn't make it as a pro. Then I became a pro. And even then, some people still said it wasn't enough—that the Regionalliga (Germany's fourth tier) was the best I could hope for,” Scherhant said.

"It's just unbelievable that I get to stand here now with the satisfaction of having proven those people wrong.".

Proving people wrong is also a major part of Klopp's remit. After failing to get beyond the quarterfinal of a major tournament since 2016, the German public's interest in and enthusiasm for its men's national team had waned. Klopp's mission he said, was to "to prove to Germany and the world that we can play soccer.".

Sources indicate that while that was achieved on Monday, the loss (and subsequent 0-0 draw) against Greece in the Nations League game were evidence that it won't all be plain sailing. Indeed, Germany have had plenty of false dawns of late, as captain Joshua Kimmich alluded to.

"We've been through a tough time," he said. "A clear victory doesn't make all that go away," he added before saying that the task was to "turn potential into quality and a team that's all about 'what ifs' into a team that's all about 'reality.' That's the art of it.".

Klopp too, for all his hype, was keen not to get too far ahead of himself.

"We want to gradually solidify it. We're not done yet. We still have a few areas to work on. But I'm looking forward to our future — it's crazy what's still to come," he mentioned.

It has been revealed that in Nations League terms, that will be a matchup with world champions Spain, or Portugal or Belgium before qualifying for Euro 2028 begins. For now though, Klopp and his players can enjoy some time with those smiles on their faces.

Welcome to Man United, Mauricio Pochettino. It’s awful

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (953 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later?
  • Welcome to Manchester United, Mauricio.
  • “So disappointed.” As can be the way with United of late, most things that could go wrong did.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today.

Welcome to Manchester United, Mauricio. For a man who had coveted the United job for years, this was an ignominious introduction. Mauricio Pochettino got a 13-minute crash course in the craziness of his new club. His first game was lost before he made his first substitution, and that came as early as the 22nd-minute. His debut brought the joint heaviest ever defeat by a United manager in his first game in charge, and the biggest in 100 years.

“So painful,” Pochettino remarked. “So disappointed.” As can be the way with United of late, most things that could go wrong did. When their new head coach’s name was sung, it was by the Kop. “Poch is at the wheel,” they taunted. A first meaningful day of work indicated the scale of the task to steer United in the right direction.

In a recent development, the team who exhibited the pace and energy of the best Pochettino sides were Liverpool, relishing the chance to compound their rivals’ problems. Florian Wirtz scored a glorious goal, Bradley Barcola kept demonstrating a sprinter’s speed and Rio Ngumoha illuminated Anfield with his precocity. Yet each was aided by United, hapless and hopeless, showing it is easier to change the manager than to reverse one of the most extraordinary declines in English football history.

It was as though Pochettino’s charges had decided to show him a snapshot of the problems: their self-destructive streak, their defensive failings, their capacity to concede in quick succession. No previous Premier League manager had seen his side both let in two goals and go down to 10 men in the first half of his opening game. Pochettino’s United accomplished that in a quarter of an hour. Suffice to say there was no honeymoon period.

Recent findings suggest that the watching Sir Alex Ferguson had lost his first game in charge, 2-0 at Oxford 40 years ago. Pochettino topped that, in the wrong way. Only Lal Hilditch, in 1926, had begun his reign as badly, with another 4-0 loss.

It has been revealed that and yet there was a continuity to United’s calamity. Meet the new boss, same as the old boss? Despite regime change, some of this was very familiar. United were two goals behind after 18 minutes against Roma, after four against Villa, after 13 against Liverpool. United got rid of Michael Carrick, kept the masterplan of going 2-0 down and discovered it has certain flaws.

Industry observers note that this was scarcely an unlucky 13 for United. Rather, they were culpable in their own downfall. Matthijs de Ligt needlessly left Ronald Araujo’s long ball, Alexander Isak ran behind the United defence and Leny Yoro barged him over. “It was an unfair situation,” complained Pochettino. “It was clear that was not a red card.” Iraola disagreed. “It is clearly the last man, clearly a foul,” he stated.

So Yoro was sent off by referee Sam Barrott and waved off by the Liverpool faithful. The punishment for United was doubled when Dominik Szoboszlai drilled his free kick past a ramshackle wall and in. Chants of “going down” rang around Anfield. It was replaced, a few minutes later, by “sacked in the morning”.

According to recent reports, with wonderful improvisation, Wirtz hooked in a volley after Ngumoha sped past Diogo Dalot and dinked in a cross. If a criticism was that the £100m German had influenced too few major matches in his Liverpool career, he altered this, brilliantly, and ended with an assist to accompany his second goal in as many games. “He's in a lovely moment,” said Iraola.

Liverpool slowed down at the end of the first half and then sped up again after the break. Barcola’s profligate finishing had cost him Liverpool’s third goal but his extraordinary pace created it. The £106m man’s scorched-earth solo run was followed by a pass to allow Ngumoha to replace Michael Owen as Liverpool’s youngest ever scorer against United. The teenager had tormented Dalot, but he was not the only winger on the scoresheet.

Victor Munoz exchanged passes with Wirtz and curled in the fourth after Liverpool’s high pressing was shown as Virgil van Dijk robbed Joshua Zirkzee, 25 yards from the United goal. Iraola ended doing fist pumps to the Kop, Jurgen Klopp-style.

“We probably should have scored more than four,” Iraola said. Senne Lammens saved, from Isak, Alexis Mac Allister and Szoboszlai. Harry Maguire made a brilliant block to turn an Isak shot away. The Swede slashed a shot wide after De Ligt inexplicably missed the ball for a second time.

It reflected badly on the upcoming manager. Perhaps Pochettino’s first significant call was to bring in De Ligt for a first league appearance of 2026. That backfired. Meanwhile, Maguire was first dropped and then summoned.

Industry observers note that pochettino had to keep changing tack. As Liverpool scored four goals, United used four formations. Pochettino seemed to begin by borrowing Ruben Amorim’s 3-4-3, then it looked a 4-2-3-1. Then it was neither, with United down to 10 men. “After what happened, happened and the proposal was in the bin,” stated Pochettino, who went to first 4-4-1 then 5-3-1, and who tried to argue what he felt was an injustice of a red card rendered what followed rather irrelevant. “We concede four goals with 10 men, and in a circumstance after playing 80 minutes at Anfield,” he said. But the circumstances are that United are in the relegation zone, lost on Pochettino’s bow, and were walloped by their rivals.

Musiala joined Bayern in 2019 after coming through Chelsea's academy.

Football players' union Fifpro says it is concerned by comments from Bayern Munich's hierarchy about Jamal Musiala's contract, adding the German club "should know better".

Musiala collapsed twice in four days during pre-season and the 23-year-old Germany international said he had been diagnosed with "easily treatable absence seizures, which are due to a neurological dysfunction".

Bayern honorary president Uli Hoeness noted earlier this month Musiala may never "regain the performance level he once had".

The Bundesliga club's chief executive Jan-Christian Dreesen has also questioned, external the lucrative contract extension the forward signed in 2025, running until 2030, if Musiala fails to get back to his best form, while his predecessor Karl-Heinz Rummenigge has suggested, external the deal may need to be renegotiated.

"Bayern's honorary president, chief executive and former chief executive have all publicly questioned Musiala's contract in quick succession," noted a Fifpro statement., external.

In a recent development, "In Fifpro's view, this is a co-ordinated strategy to put pressure on Musiala and his representatives ahead of any negotiations. A club of Bayern's standing should know better.".

Musiala may never return to his best - Hoeness.

Two collapses in four days - what's happening to Musiala?

Musiala, who joined Bayern in 2019 after coming through Chelsea's academy, came on for the German champions after 70 minutes in a 1-1 draw with Cologne on Friday as he made his first outing since scoring in a 7-0 win against Union Berlin on 18 September.

He has made five appearances for the club this season, scoring two goals and providing one assist.

Recent findings suggest that "Bayern has a duty of care to Musiala," added Fifpro. "Across professional football, uncertainty about a player's future can take a toll on their mental health, particularly when they are recovering from injury.

Sources indicate that "Making Musiala's health and future a matter of public debate adds to that pressure. Any concerns about his contract should be raised privately with him and his representatives.

In a recent development, "Contracts are there to be respected. An injury or a dip in form gives a club no grounds to reopen terms it agreed to, just as a run of outstanding performances gives a player no automatic right to a pay rise.".

Musiala's return to the Bayern side came in the same game in which England striker Harry Kane suffered an ankle injury and was subsequently ruled out "for the next few months".

Breaking: What history tells us about the Premier League table after 10 games of a season

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (695 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Theguardian

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Past years suggest it is tough to make major positional gains after slow start but that someone now safe will be relegated.
  • The Premier League is about to enter the most intense phase of its season.
  • Across the past decade, Premier League teams’ positions changed by an average of 2.6 places between matchweeks 10 and 38.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Past years suggest it is tough to make major positional gains after slow start but that someone now safe will be relegated.

The Premier League is about to enter the most intense phase of its season. After 10 rounds of fixtures across the past three months there are 10 in the next seven weeks. Yet if you hibernated for winter, most clubs would be in roughly the same position no matter when in spring you emerged.

Across the past decade, Premier League teams’ positions changed by an average of 2.6 places between matchweeks 10 and 38. Only 5.5 clubs per season moved by more than three places over the final 28 games, with almost half of the teams (89 out of 200) shifting by a single spot at most. Every club other than Arsenal will be looking to improve their position but they need not trouble themselves too much. History reveals they will probably finish 2026-27 close to their current standing.

It has been revealed that there have inevitably been outliers. Tottenham have tumbled by at least 10 places after matchweek 10 in the past two seasons and Newcastle (in 2021-22), Crystal Palace and Everton (both 2017-18) have risen from the relegation zone at this point to the safety of mid-table by May.

But even moving one position across the remainder of the season can make an enormous difference to a team on the fringe of the Champions League qualification spots, or to those that sit 17th or 18th after 10 games. Not since 2006-07 have the bottom three clubs with 28 matches to go all been relegated.

Industry observers note that this fact feels especially relevant this season given two of the three teams in the drop zone have changed their manager since the previous round of matches. Sunderland have stood by Régis Le Bris but he is the favourite to be the next Premier League manager to leave their post. If we can reasonably assume at least one of the clubs currently 18th to 20th will be in the top flight in 2027-28, which is best placed to survive?

It is going to be very tough for Crystal Palace. Opta’s underlying data model implies they are where they deserve to be in the table, whereas Manchester United and Sunderland should be much higher. The largest improvement Palace’s latest manager, Thomas Frank, engineered between weeks 10 and 38 at Brentford was two places, which will not cut it this season. Palace have to take inspiration from the 2024-25 season, in which they also had seven points after 10 games yet rose to finish 12th.

In a recent development, mauricio Pochettino’s Chelsea were 11th going into their 11th game in 2023-24 before ending sixth. As they were also 11th in early April, they made a much shorter dash to the finish line, though. Pochettino’s teams usually improve as campaigns wear on, with Tottenham rising three places after week 10 in each of his first three seasons with the club. A similar lift in his upcoming role would not make this season a rousing success for United but it would stave off the unthinkable idea of relegation.

For someone to escape, someone else must take their place. Ignoring the possibility that the answer to “who?” may be Manchester City, the team in 17th are inevitably the ones most at risk. Of the 13 sides in the past decade who were outside the drop zone after 10 games but went down, six were fourth-bottom going into matchweek 11.

In a recent development, given that the points gap between first and 20th (20) was last lower at this stage in 2015-16, those figures may be more pertinent than position this season. Leeds in 2022-23 and Bournemouth three years earlier had 13 points after 10 games but were relegated, as did Blackpool in 2010-11 and Middlesbrough two seasons before them.

Only nine clubs are now above that bar, with Aston Villa, Newcastle and Tottenham among those who are not. The table is unlikely to change too much before the end of the campaign but there is a distinct chance that a secure-looking side will perish.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Liverpool fans did not miss a beat. They never do. “Poch is at the wheel,” they goaded as this calamity unfolded. But at the wheel of what, a clown car? The look of thunder on Mauricio Pochettino’s face remarked it all as he got off to the worst start of any Manchester United manager – or head coach – in 100 years.

The Pochettino bandwagon rolled into town with the usual fanfare of a latest era, new belief, new hope; and then the wheels came off, the doors collapsed and the engine exploded. The opening quarter of an hour really was that farcical.

Recent findings suggest that in that time, away to Liverpool of all places, they were 2-0 down, a player down – and down and out. If Pochettino had any uncertainty over the scale of the task ahead of him, there it was laid bare. Of course United had some mitigation. They played almost the entire game with 10 men, but teams have coped with that before and shown far more resistance and resilience. By the time United did that, it was game over. No one expected a quick fix, but come on.

Any regrets, Mauricio? Whatever the salary, he could be forgiven for having a few as he watched on. This is a far cry from being in charge of the United States and watching them roll over Haiti 8-0 on aggregate as he did last week. If Liverpool had been more ruthless, it could have been 8-0 here.

In the end it was 4-0 – the same scoreline by which Lal Hilditch lost his first game at United, away to Bolton Wanderers in October 1926. Hilditch was a stop-gap player-manager and former central defender Pochettino may well have been tempted to bring himself on, even at the age of 54. He could barely have done worse.

Pochettino, too, can take some responsibility. Eyebrows were certainly raised when he dropped Harry Maguire – who he then had to bring on after 22 minutes – to hand Matthijs de Ligt his first Premier League start in 357 days. De Ligt was then at fault for the first and, arguably, the second goal.

Industry observers note that did the head coach start with a back three or a back four? The players seemed confused. It eventually ended up as a back five.

Sources indicate that but this was a collective failing for United. From top – with director of football Jason Wilcox caught on camera with his head buried in his coat – through the club and out on the pitch. Pochettino is big on building a culture. So he has to abolish the comedy and the chaos and restore credibility.

United are deep in a relegation battle. Have no doubt. Eight points after 11 games means they are right now on target for fewer than 28 points, which is a lower points per game total than when they were relegated in 1974 (32 over 42 games).

The work needed at United is monumental. The transfer strategy has been inexplicable, with the decision being to rebuild the attack last year, the midfield this summer and wait until next year to remodel the defence. The folly of that has been exposed by the fact that United have conceded 34 goals already this season, the most in the top five European leagues.

United will argue, with justification, that Leny Yoro’s eighth-minute sending-off for denial of a goalscoring opportunity was harsh given that Alexander Isak appeared to have already lost control of the ball. But what was Yoro thinking as he bundled into the back of the forward? And what was De Ligt doing as he watched on, or lumbered on, after failing to track the run from Ronald Araújo’s ball over the top?

Andoni Iraola had a very clear message for his players ahead of this game: don’t fall into a trap.

It’s remarkable to see Manchester United arrive at Anfield in the bottom three but, to go back to that old cliche, the league table will mean nothing when the game begins and Liverpool’s Head Coach knows it only too well.

There will come a point when United leave their desperate form behind and Iraola, who could do with winning this contest after high-profile defeats to Arsenal and Manchester City, Isn’t being kidded by results after 10 games.

“United finished third in the table last season,” Iraola pointed out. “You are looking at a squad with exactly the same players. They had very, very good results, especially in the second half of the season. Now we have just started, this is just 10 games. So, for sure, they will be a lot higher in the table (soon). We have to rate them like this and the truth is the reference we have is that they finished third.”.

The key to success for Liverpool will be winning the midfield battle and Dominik Szoboszlai - whose form has been up and down - needs to recapture his best.

It is ironic that in their latest attempt to rejuvenate and restore some of their old fire, Manchester United have turned to a manager whose career needs a similar reawakening.

Having dismissed Michael Carrick so early in the season, United can consider themselves fortunate that a figure of such clout and experience as Mauricio Pochettino was available and willing to leave his role with the United States.

Pochettino can be even more grateful that a club of United’s stature have turned to him in their moment of need.

In a recent development, united need a saviour to first ease them from the relegation zone and then revive their Premier League and Champions League credibility. Pochettino, meanwhile, needed a club like United to save him from a managerial career that promised more than it delivered.

Bruno Fernandes indicates he has shelved talks over a newly introduced contract because it is not the “right moment” for discussions over his future as Manchester United captain.

Fernandes, 32, is out of contract next summer although United have a 12-month option to extend his deal to 2028.

The Portugal midfielder is understood to have rejected two contract offers from United since the summer but remarked all his focus needs to be on trying to help the team out of their current plight.

United head into Sunday’s game against Liverpool at Anfield second from bottom in the Premier League.

“We spoke about the contract at the end of last season,” Fernandes told Sky Sports.

“We came in at the beginning of this season speaking about the contract, but about the context of the team and the club, I just put that to a side because I don’t think it’s the right moment, neither for me, nor for the club, to be talking about negotiations.

“The most vital thing now is that the club gets back to winning games.”.

According to recent reports, fernandes noted claims he wants more money or a longer-term deal on offer are incorrect and that if finances were the concern he would have left Old Trafford before now. The captain has previously rejected lucrative offers from Saudi Arabia.

“The club offered me a new contract, so I think that, from their side, demonstrates that they want me to stay,” he said.

“There’s no negotiations ongoing, but I’ve seen people saying that ‘He’s asked for more money, he’s asked for more years’. If I wanted more money, I wouldn’t be here.

“I had somewhere to go to get much more money than being at Manchester United. I could have been in a place that is much warmer than Manchester.

“Two summers ago, three summers ago, last summer, I always had the chance to leave and I always chose to be here.

“The thing is, I’ve always showed how much I care about the club and how much I want to win at this club. And I always said, in the moment the club thinks it’s time for me to move on, I will move on.

“I’m not going to be the player that I’ve seen many in this time at Manchester United. They’re going to stay here just by staying, just finish my contract and then we will see. In the moment the club says, ‘Bruno, it’s time to part ways’, I’m going to be the first one walking out the door.”.

United chief executive Omar Berrada mentioned of Fernandes on Friday that it was “true that we’re having conversations about his new contract” but that the club preferred “to keep that private”.

Having been voted PFA Player of the Year last season, Fernandes’ form has dropped off this term like that of the team.

He was dropped for the 3-0 defeat by Bournemouth in the wake of a 4-1 drubbing by Como when he criticised the tactics and approach of then head coach Michael Carrick.

Mauricio Pochettino, Carrick’s successor, confirmed on Friday that Fernandes would remain as captain.

Fernandes stated the United fans had been “far too patient with us” and hopes Pochettino - who wanted to bring the Portuguese to Spurs in 2019 - will bring a fresh energy.

“He’s someone that likes to bring a very good energy to the team, someone very positive, very strong, strict, said it straight away that he won’t allow us to not give him what he demands from the team, from each player,” Fernandes said.

“He wants the club to succeed so much, he wants to win games, and that’s pretty clear and obvious by the way he and his staff speak and want us to improve.

In a recent development, “Obviously [in 2019] I was a very young player that was eager to come to the Premier League. They had [Harry] Kane there, they had Dele Alli, Son, the chance of playing with those players in front was very attractive.”.

  • Stoke City are the Championship's form team, having taken 32 points from the last 39, but can they stay the distance in the promotion race?

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

After the last international break of the year, Final Score pundit and former Swindon Town, Luton Town and Northampton Town striker selects his takeaways from the Championship, League One and League Two.

Stoke City are the Championship's form team, having taken 32 points from the last 39, but can they stay the distance in the promotion race?

Parkin: "I think everyone, probably me included, is really optimistic about their chances of this being the season they get it right.

According to recent reports, "We're a fair chunk into the season now and I thought today's result was really crucial because I believe this was their first win over anyone in the top eight. It felt like a bit of a statement win because Birmingham, apart from their defeat at Cardiff, have been really competitive in more or less every game.

"They've been able to just come out the right side of the scoreline and they've had to rely on their goalkeeper [Viktor] Johansson, who I think is one of the top goalkeepers at this level.

Recent findings suggest that "I think there was an early shift in formation, going to a back three in the early part of the campaign, and I think that's proved quite notable. They're keeping clean sheets and they've got a goalscorer in George Hirst.

It has been revealed that "I read a lot about Stoke City fans saying they're still probably short on forwards who are going to get them the goals. I know that [Jack] McGlynn has chipped in with a really impressive number from midfield, but for Hirst to get that major winning goal, that will have done his confidence the world of good.

"He's been promoted previously with Ipswich and there's no reason why he can't be Stoke's main man up front.".

Dejected Millwall boss Alex Neil.

Millwall have slumped to 16th after fighting for promotion in the last few seasons and they have lost five of their last seven league games.

According to recent reports, parkin: "They've had to deal with a horrendous injury crisis. It was at a level that I was struggling to think of a comparable club in the early part of the season. They were just having players go down week after week.

"There was one game in particular I covered against Wrexham and they had the walking wounded (out there), so I think they're still recovering from that.

"They've got some of the main players in [Casper] De Norre back fit now and available, but I think [Josh] Coburn was unavailable again today, and [Mihailo] Ivanovic is just making his way back - I would say they are three of their more important players.

"Take away [Jake] Cooper at the back, who's been a mainstay for a number of years, and I think that trio I've just mentioned are so fundamental to their chances this season.

"They're still playing catch up to a degree, but Alex Neil has not pulled any punches in some of his interviews and he'll be disappointed.

"On the flip side of that, QPR are in a really good place at the moment, and are a much tougher proposition than maybe they would have been over the last couple of seasons.

In a recent development, "I think Millwall will improve over time. I don't see them emulating what they did last season, but I think they can be optimistic they can get some better results once everyone's back available.".

Lincoln City management duo Chris Cohen and Tom Shaw.

Lincoln City are finding life in the Championship tough after romping to the League One title last season and they have lost seven of their last nine league games.

According to recent reports, parkin: "It's been a downward spiral and the home form's a bit of an concern. They just have the one win over Burnley there - and Burnley were in dire straits when they came.

"They've lost four in a row so that will be a little bit of a concern because they found a formula on the road in the early part of the season. But, yeah, you've got to do better in your home form.

According to recent reports, "I still trust they're going to be competitive and the majority of that squad, Jack Moylan apart, is still there from last season. You don't get over 100 points and then lose everything.

"That's always going to count for something when you've got the nucleus of that squad still together, even if it is in a higher division. So I think the spirit will remain amongst that group, despite the recent defeats.

"They've got to start taking points off the better teams in the division as well. All their victories have come against teams who are in the lower part of the table, like Preston and Burnley.

"They won at Bolton and at Bristol City, so they're not really mixing it with the teams in the top half of the table at the moment.

"But I think the bottom line is the management duo would have absolutely taken being five points above 22nd at this stage of the season, so they've given themselves a good opportunity to stay in the division.".

Glum Barnsley boss Daniel Stendel.

Barnsley are four points from safety at the bottom of League One after Friday's defeat by Sheffield Wednesday in the South Yorkshire derby and are on course for a first return to the fourth tier since 1979.

It has been revealed that parkin: "I think on last night's evidence, they're a better team than the league table suggests. That's an absolute certainty in my mind.

Industry observers note that "My one concern is where are the goals going to come from? For all their dangerous play, which is incredibly aggressive and energetic, with and without the ball, where are the goals?

"They throw caution to the wind and there's a real energy and youth about the side, which I actually really admired in defeat.

"It's just translating all that into goals and that was obviously one part of it against Wednesday, and giving away bad goals - they've conceded the most set pieces now in the division.

Sources indicate that "They conceded in that manner again, and because they play such a high line, they (also) get exposed by teams on the counter. Maybe that's a little bit of naivety. Maybe that's a little bit lack of experience, which they can go some way to mending in January when the transfer window opens.

"But they may be adrift at the bottom if they don't turn things around soon. In short, I think they're a better team than a relegated team. But the most key thing in football, as we know, is putting the ball in the back of the net and that clearly is a problem for them at the moment.".

Crawley Town's Dylan Morgan celebrates scoring against Cheltenham Town.

Crawley Town boosted their chances of staying in the EFL when they recorded their first home league win of the season over Fleetwood Town and they have generated some momentum in their last few matches.

It has been revealed that parkin: "Former Leeds and Sheffield United manager Kevin Blackwell is in charge now till the end of the season. I was injured for the majority of his spell at Luton Town when he was my manager, but I'm kind of well versed in his methods and he will make them really hard to beat.

In a recent development, "That's always the first thing you want when you take over a struggling side, you need to stop shipping goals. You need to get them organised. You need to work on set-pieces and be a threat on that front. He will do all those things.

Recent findings suggest that "I think the three results in the league, two wins and a draw, have showed you that his methods have already come to fruition. His approach will be very different to probably what the players were being asked to do under Scott Lindsey.

"It'll be a different kind of football. They'll play long at times, they'll want to play in the opposition's half. I think in terms of a blueprint to get survival, he could very well be the man to supply that.

"They've chosen him after he was initially brought in as interim manager because the performances have improved across the last few weeks, despite the embarrassment of the FA Cup defeat to Wimborne.

"He's made them competitive very swiftly and I think a lot of teams are going to be in for a real game when they face them.".

Sam Parkin was speaking to BBC Sport England's David Anderson.

For a generation of football fans in the UK, Soccer AM was a staple of their Saturday morning routine.

The Sky TV show combined football, comedy and celebrity guests, all with a healthy dose of general chaos.

When TV newcomer and longtime Soccer AM fan Max Rushden landed the co-presenter job alongside Helen Chamberlain in 2008, he was thrown into a world he had never experienced before.

“Getting the job was mad because I'd never done a TV show in my life, and it definitely demonstrated in the first two years,” Rushden tells FourFourTwo.

“But I loved the show – I was a fan of the week in 2000 and watched it religiously until about two or three years before getting the job, so the whole thing was surreal.”.

Rushden’s journey from avid viewer to presenter had plenty of twists, including an audition for another iconic British TV programme.

“I was doing a breakfast show on Radio London, but I had to go back to reading the news because I wasn't famous,” he continues.

The best features, fun and footballing quizzes, straight to your inbox every week.

“I thought, ‘OK, I'll make a show and send it to everybody' – the only two people who replied were from the Travel Channel, who stated I was boring, and Sky Sports, who asked me to go in for a chat.

It has been revealed that “I bowled in, chatted about Cambridge and Soccer AM for an hour. They mentioned they might have something for me in a couple of months, but I didn't expect much.”.

After leaving the audition with low expectations, Rushden continued to explore other possibilities.

“In the meantime, I'd got an audition for Blue Peter,” he reveals before receiving a life-changing telephone call.

“Before I went to it, I got a call from Sky and they asked, “Do you want to do Soccer AM?” My head just exploded and I was trying to play it cool.

"I signed the contract and s**t myself for a month before the show started.”.

For more than a decade, Joe Mewis has worked in football journalism as a reporter and editor. Mewis has had stints at Mirror Football and LeedsLive among others and worked at FourFourTwo throughout Euro 2024, reporting on the tournament. In addition to his journalist work, Mewis is also the author of four football history books that include times on Leeds United and the England national team. Now working as a digital marketing coordinator at Harrogate Town, too, Mewis counts some of his best career moments as being in the iconic Spygate press conference under Marcelo Bielsa and seeing his beloved Leeds lift the Championship trophy during lockdown.

Upcoming Manchester United manager Mauricio Pochettino has denied that Leny Yoro should have been sent off in his side’s 4-0 loss to Liverpool, calling it an “unfair situation”.

Yoro was given a straight red card in the eighth minute of the game at Anfield to give Pochettino the worst possible start to his life as United boss, with the young Frenchman fouling the Liverpool striker after he had gone clean through as last man.

As there was no attempt to play the ball, referee Sam Barrott showed Yoro a straight red card, with VAR checking and confirming the decision “for denial of an obvious goal-scoring opportunity (DOGSO)”.

It went from bad to worse for United too, with Dominik Szoboszlai scoring from 19 yards out from the ensuing free-kick.

But while little was made of the incident at the time, some – including Roy Keane in the Sky Sports studio – pointed out that the challenge may not have been worthy of a red card as Isak was unlikely to stay in control of the ball after taking a poor touch.

And Pochettino agreed, stating that “the ball was for the goalkeeper”.

“In that situation, if you review the VAR you can see for sure, he [Yoro] never had the intention to connect with Isak,” explained Pochettino on Sky Sports after full-time.

“When the control was long with the striker, the ball was going to the goalkeeper, he runs and goes down. In Leny's case, it wasn't intentional. It was an unusual situation that is normal, everyone who plays football can feel it.

It has been revealed that "We have to take responsibility, I take the responsibility. We keep pushing. It's not going to change what happened. Being respectful is the most important. At the same time, I have to defend my club. And tell what I feel. That was an action that everyone who plays football, it was clear that a situation that was not a red card,” he added.

Kobbie Mainoo agreed with his manager, saying there is “no chance” it deserved to be a sending off.

“The ball's already with the goalkeeper. They're both running full speed. What can we do? It is what it is,” mentioned the United midfielder.

Recent findings suggest that the result leaves United in 19th after 11 games, with just eight points and one win in the league all season. As for Liverpool, they rise to fourth with 21 points, just seven behind leaders Arsenal.
