📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Spain Under-21 striker admits the pace of the Premier League has surprised him but says he must stay calm over goal drought at Fulham.

In a recent development, the first thing Rita Hayworth’s great nephew indicates when he walks in is: “Sorry I’m late.” Gonzalo García is not late, but it’s very like him: he is impeccably polite, accommodating, and there’s an almost gentle quality to him, a calm that’s not common but can help, especially in moments when the pressure builds. There’s a reason one of the coaches standing in the rain by the pitch where Spain’s under‑21s have just finished training says everyone here loves García. The Fulham striker shakes hands, introduces himself and ducks into the dressing room to change; then a few minutes later he’s back, apologising for a wait that wasn’t one.

In a recent development, time to talk, so let’s start with Tinseltown, the family tale. García laughs. His great-aunt, born Margarita Carmen Cansino, was among the biggest stars in Hollywood, although he’s not sure he’s seen any of her films. His grandfather was a surgeon and others in the family followed. His uncles played rugby for Spain, but that wasn’t his thing. As for him, he enrolled in a degree in business management and analytics, and reckons he might have liked law, yet even that wasn’t his chosen field.

According to recent reports, hayworth’s family was from Seville province. “I know she was a great actress but I’m afraid I have to admit I’m not one for old films,” García concedes in an even tone. “My uncles played rugby for Ciencias and practically all of them were in the national team together. They tried to get me to play with my cousins, but I was always more into football.” He was good at it too: another Spain international, the Club World Cup’s top scorer, playing for Real Madrid.

In a recent development, then this summer, with opportunities limited, he joined Fulham, his introductory interview conducted in impeccable English. Having joined Madrid aged 10, he was leaving home for the first time, as Fulham’s record signing, at 22. He had the language and intelligence to embrace it. As for being uprooted, he was used to that, growing up in Argentina and Chile as well as Spain.

According to recent reports, “From very little my parents impressed upon me the importance of study, learning languages,” García states. “I’m at Villanueva university [in Madrid]. I started with dual honours business and analytics, although that became difficult with my profession. Now it’s just business, and I’m trying to arrange with the university how best to handle it [from London]. My parents considered it fundamental to speak English and I was always at international schools.

In a recent development, “Every two or three years we would change city. Obviously, there would be phases when I felt: ‘Pfff, again?!’ Having to move home because of my parents’ work. But I look back and feel grateful because, seen with perspective, it gives you opportunities to meet newly introduced people, see new places, learn. I’ve always had foreign friends with whom I spoke English.”.

García has been joined at Fulham by César Palacios and Manuel Ángel from Madrid’s academy. Three 22-year-olds, like your very own Erasmus course. “Nah,” García says, laughing. “I wouldn’t call it an Erasmus because we’re talking about a massive, ambitious career step. We’re grateful for the trust placed in us. I’ve been pleasantly surprised by London, a huge city with people from all nationalities and cultures and Fulham fit the situation I was in, the desire to grow.

It has been revealed that “Álvaro Arbeloa explained the project, convinced me. I’d worked with him in Madrid. He knows me perfectly, how far he can push me. Equally, I know what he wants of me. That helps … [Arbeloa] told me it was a project that it will take time but that he needed me. I’m very, very happy. It’s one of the world’s best leagues, if not the best.”.

And the toughest? Is English football as wild as it looks? “Yes!” García replies. “They had told me it was demanding, hard, but …” He cracks up. “I have to admit it still surprised me. That first game against Chelsea, I finished really, really tired. It was box to box, intense, a lot of running. Bit by bit I’m adapting. The intensity and pace is very different.

“Spain is more tactical, a bit more technical. English football is pace. You can’t lose concentration for a second, not a second. Anything can happen any moment. How many Premier League games are decided late? Suddenly there’s a goal in the 90th minute and again on 93. It’s your corner and their chance. The level of concentration, that constant transition, is what most sets the Premier League apart.”.

Despite defeat on that opening day against Chelsea, García scored. A superb goal followed against AFC Wimbledon in the Carabao Cup. “It was super special to do it at Craven Cottage. I love how close the fans are – they can reach out and touch you. But I don’t consider myself someone who’s easily satisfied. I’m not like that. I always want more, more, more.”.

It has been revealed that garcía hasn’t scored since and Fulham went five league games without a win, pressure building. Which is where the calmness comes in. By the time they faced Hull, Arbeloa appeared on the edge of the sack, questions asked about his signings, García especially. Were three Madrid academy kids really what Fulham needed? Was the coach’s relationship with them not such a good thing after all?

No player is impermeable to what is mentioned, García admits, but he insists: “We treat that as outside noise. And we all knew that the beginning wouldn’t be easy. There’s a change of cycle: the coach goes, a fresh coach comes, there are signings, a different system, idea. Everyone has to adapt: those already at the club and those of us who are new. We’re young too. Results weren’t going our way but we had good intentions: to play good football, build, apply the manager’s ideas bit by bit. We had to remain calm.”.

Sources indicate that fulham go into Saturday’s game at Manchester City unbeaten in four in the league, the sense of them shifting towards something more pragmatic not shared by García. “I don’t think we changed anything against Hull,” he says of a game Fulham won 1-0. “We didn’t do anything we weren’t already doing. Nothing. Maybe we controlled the small details that hurt us but the idea was the same. The players were very clear what the manager asked, very firm: it was just a question of time. You have to be patient. If you watch Fulham, you see the manager’s idea: have the ball, construct attacks well, show maximum intensity constantly with and without the ball. Aggressive, ambitious.”.

It has been revealed that chances are coming for García but goals aren’t. He has started every league game but not scored or assisted since the opening day. Yet if there is a sense of a man feeling the pressure, that’s not repeated here; instead there’s an evenness, an ease. And a smile when another, more welcome, stat is raised: he has made more off‑the‑ball runs into the area than anyone. Something to hold on to, perhaps, a process that will pay off. “Really?” he indicates. “Well, I’m happy for people to see that a striker can help the team without the ball. In the end, it’s about following the manager’s instructions.”.

In a recent development, in the end, though, teams will be judged on results and strikers on goals, price too. He knows: this is what he does, the path he chose. “Pressure depends on how you look at it, really,” García says. “Football is [very psychological]. It happens fast: it doesn’t give you time to enjoy good moments or linger on bad ones. It’s a rollercoaster – up there, down here. It’s not flat, but you maintain balance, work daily, improve: go in, focus, repeat.

According to recent reports, “It’s not that I don’t ‘care’ about the price, it’s that the market is the market; it doesn’t depend on me. Calmness always, perspective … I know strikers are measured by goals but, well, the days I don’t score I’m completely sure I will be able to walk off the pitch and say that, no matter what happened, I helped my team, doing a load of other things. It is what it is.”.

It is also time. A head peers around the door, the bus is going. García holds out a hand, apologises again. “It’s been a pleasure,” he says.

Nine wins in a row - Bournemouth & Evanilson continue to make history

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1212 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Evanilson strikes again as Bournemouth see off Forest.
  • That is how Bournemouth manager Marco Rose responded after his side had dropped into the Premier League relegation zone with a 5-1 defeat by Chelsea.
  • The Cherries are up to fourth in the top flight, having clinched a club record ninth successive win in all competitions - with five in the league.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Evanilson strikes again as Bournemouth see off Forest.

"We have to stick together and face reality.".

That is how Bournemouth manager Marco Rose responded after his side had dropped into the Premier League relegation zone with a 5-1 defeat by Chelsea.

Six weeks on, it is an entirely different story.

The Cherries are up to fourth in the top flight, having clinched a club record ninth successive win in all competitions - with five in the league.

It is a far cry from that thumping defeat at Stamford Bridge, which left Rose without a victory in his first six Premier League matches in charge.

Bournemouth earned just three points from those six games (draws against Everton, Newcastle and Brentford - when the Cherries squandered winning positions) and fans may have been fearing the worst.

From the outside looking in, it seemed as though the appointment of Rose might not deliver the fortunes that had been expected.

The 50-year-old, who accepted the unenviable task of succeeding Andoni Iraola, called for his side to take "responsibility" after the defeat by Chelsea.

Industry observers note that "Three points after six games, we need a reaction. Everyone has to take responsibility to do better," noted Rose at the time.

Recent findings suggest that "We knew it was going to be a demanding season. We have to stick together and face reality. The reality is we have three points after six games.".

The Cherries have not only responded to Rose's rallying cry, they have exceeded all expectations.

Those nine straight wins include five in the league - and his side are now only four points behind second-placed Brighton.

After easing to a 2-0 victory against Nottingham Forest on Saturday, Rose noted: "We don't think about records, we just think about the next game.

"We took the right approach. We knew it would be tough and we would have to stay patient, and that's what we did. It was a top performance and a deserved win.".

Bournemouth's nine-game winning streak is a club record - beating two separate runs of eight in 1998-99 and 2012-13.

Since arriving in England in July, Rose has come across as a composed presence, regardless of Bournemouth's results.

However, the former Borussia Dortmund and RB Leipzig manager was unable to hide his delight at his side's record-breaking victory against Forest.

Shortly after the full-time whistle sounded at the Vitality Stadium, Rose unleashed a series of celebratory fist pumps in front of the delighted home fans.

It was arguably the first time Rose had let down his guard since arriving on the South Coast four months ago - and who could blame him, given the significance of the result?

It is the first time in the club's history they have won five consecutive Premier League matches.

The prospect of securing European football for a second consecutive season is growing by the week.

In addition to wins over Sunderland, Manchester United, Leeds, Ipswich and Nottingham Forest in the Premier League, Bournemouth have beaten AC Milan in the Europa League and Aston Villa in the League Cup.

Their remarkable run of nine wins across all competitions surpasses their previous record of eight, achieved in both the 1998-99 and 2012-13 seasons.

Bournemouth are at the moment also second in the Europa League league phase and are one of only three teams to have won all four of their matches so far.

"Tonight I will smile, but not just because of the table - because we win," Rose told Match of the Day.

Meanwhile, Justin Kluivert - who scored Bournemouth's second goal against Forest - urged his team-mates to remain "humble" and "not settle for less" before upcoming matches against Celta Vigo and Fulham.

'I'll call him' - Justin Kluivert happy he's scored same week as dad Patrick.

One of the main reasons behind Bournemouth's upturn in form has been the hot streak forward Evanilson is at the moment enjoying.

After failing to find the back of the net in his first five appearances of the season, the Brazilian became the first player in club history to score in six consecutive Premier League matches when he broke the deadlock against Forest.

Since joining the Cherries in a club record deal from Porto in August 2024, the 27-year-old has struggled for consistency.

In his first season in England, Evanilson managed 10 goals and five assists in 31 league appearances.

Last season, though, was less productive for the forward, who managed only six goals and three assists in 36 top-flight appearances.

By scoring against Forest, Evanilson has already matched his return from the previous campaign.

In a recent development, "He is lovely, he works hard and his quality does the rest," said Kluivert. "I am happy he has been scoring, and working hard for the team.".

In a recent development, it is not only goals that Evanilson is providing for his side this season. He has also proven that he is able to drop between the lines - and out wide - to allow Bournemouth to be a fluid side in transition.

That was evident for the Cherries' second goal against Forest, when Evanilson pulled out to the left touchline and threaded the ball down the line for Marcus Tavernier to cross for the unmarked Kluivert in the centre.

Sources indicate that "The way he works for us out of possession, works as a link player and goes deep," added Rose. "The way he scores is quite impressive.".

The season has not even reached the halfway point, so no-one at Bournemouth will be getting carried away just yet.

What is possible for the Cherries this term will largely depend on what happens - or, perhaps more importantly, what does not happen - in January.

Bournemouth's impressive recent form - and that of certain individuals - is likely to attract attention from some of the biggest clubs in the Premier League when the transfer window opens in January.

Players such as Evanilson, Rayan, Alex Scott and Junior Kroupi, in particular, are likely to be the subject of interest from elsewhere.

So what should Bournemouth do if some of the Premier League's 'bigger' clubs come knocking for their crown jewels?

Should they resist the premium prices the mid-season market is likely to bring and keep hold of their star quality to preserve their own aspirations this season?

Former Manchester City and England goalkeeper Joe Hart believes the Cherries should try to keep hold of their stars to bolster their own hopes this term - insisting the "sky is the limit" for Rose's side.

"Rather than setting a specific target, like Champions League qualification, they should just enjoy what they are doing," Hart told BBC Sport.

"It is crucial they keep everyone fit and firing, given they have the extra demands of playing in Europe plus the busy Christmas period to come.

"Junior Kroupi and Alex Scott came off the bench today, and that kind of squad depth could be massive for them.

"It is all about keeping themselves in the running because a lot of teams are stumbling right now, whereas Bournemouth are really in a rich vein of form.".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Leeds dominate Chelsea for first Stamford Bridge win since 1999.

Chelsea manager Xabi Alonso is already in firefighting mode.

His team were booed by their own supporters at several points during a dominant 4-1 Leeds victory at Stamford Bridge, their first win there since 1999.

Industry observers note that the first negative reaction came at half-time while the score was still 1-1. The ground then began to empty after the third and fourth Leeds goals, and the fans remaining voiced their dissent once more at the final whistle.

Although there were mitigating circumstances, including a potentially harsh penalty decision against them and the loss of midfielder Moises Caicedo to injury, joining a five-strong list of players on the treatment table, the defeat was thoroughly deserved.

It leaves Chelsea with three losses in their past four Premier League matches and they have slipped from fifth place to eighth, already 14 points behind league leaders Arsenal.

In October, Tottenham won at Stamford Bridge for only the second time in the Premier League era, while the 1-0 defeat at bottom club Sunderland before the international break was another alarm bell.

It is the first time in 67 years that Chelsea have lost at home to both Leeds and Spurs in the same season.

"We need to find solutions, for sure, because there will be setbacks during any game," Alonso said after the match.

"To be able to go through that and to know that it's still so long to play, it's something mandatory in this competition and today I felt that probably we are in a fragile moment mentally.

"When we received a punch we didn't recover that strongly.".

Okafor double delivers rare win for Leeds at Chelsea.

'Officials can't use common sense' - was Rogers handball correct?

Indeed, even when Chelsea have been winning matches, they have often looked unconvincing.

Yet Blues supporters chanted their newly introduced manager's name and seemed optimistic after the summer transfer business - despite a disappointing 10th-place finish last season.

Club record Â£117m signing Morgan Rogers was joined by the experienced trio of Emiliano Martinez, Danny Welbeck and Jordan Henderson.

It was the clinical finishing of Rogers, along with Cole Palmer and Joao Pedro earlier in the season, that masked the underlying fragility of Alonso's team.

Before this weekend, the Blues ranked 14th for expected goal difference and were joint 12th in Opta's expected points table.

After their latest setback, ex-England forward and BBC Match of the Day pundit Alan Shearer said: "Chelsea were all over the place. Once Moises Caicedo went off injured early on, there was no physicality and they looked weak.

"They hardly created anything going forward and the back four didn't look comfortable. There was no desire, cohesion or fight from the home side, but we shouldn't take anything away from Leeds.

"Two weeks ago Chelsea were bullied by Sunderland centre-forward Brian Brobbey and they let Dominic Calvert-Lewin do the same today, which is alarming.

Sources indicate that "It's fair to say Xabi Alonso's honeymoon period is over. He needs to tell his players this simply isn't good enough. They are miles off it and have to do better in every department.".

Xabi Alonso post-match interview - Chelsea v Leeds United.

Xabi Alonso was appointed Chelsea manager on a four-year deal in May.

In Alonso's defence, Chelsea had problems before his arrival.

They finished 10th last season, having been outrun in 37 of their 38 matches, and had three managers during a chaotic campaign.

Remarkably, Chelsea have seven more points from corresponding fixtures this season and last, but it mostly serves to show how low the bar was set.

Champions League qualification was again the club's pre-season target and Alonso's appointment was designed to bring stability and authority.

The former Real Madrid and Liverpool midfielder had an impressive playing career and earned much early admiration as a manager, guiding Bayer Leverkusen to a league and cup double in 2024.

However, the Spaniard, who was sacked by Real Madrid last season, has yet to establish any real consistency - beyond his defence leaking goals regularly.

Only Crystal Palace, Coventry City and Ipswich Town have conceded more goals than Chelsea this season.

According to recent reports, chelsea are also now averaging fewer than a goal per game since Joao Pedro suffered a thigh injury in training. Alongside Pedro and now Caicedo, Jorrel Hato, Maxence Lacroix, Reece James and Jamie Gittens are also injured.

It highlights how they have gained little benefit of having a season without European football.

Alonso is also beginning to face criticism from sections of the fanbase for both his team selections and substitutions.

Chief among the reasons is the constant chopping and changing of the starting XI, having now made 28 line-up changes (behind only Tottenham) while also switching between back-four and back-three systems.

In addition, Alonso is being criticised for his use of personnel, having deployed Pedro Neto as a striker on two occasions and, some would argue, not made enough use of exciting young winger Estevao.

Chelsea have shown 'no progression' under Alonso - Shearer.

Against Leeds he gave striker Emmanuel Emegha his first start alongside Estevao and, although the Dutch striker scored, the pair were the first players he substituted while Chelsea were chasing the game at 3-1 down.

Similarly, his late in-game interventions are under scrutiny, including the decision to bring on striker Welbeck only in the 90th minute of the defeat by Spurs.

Industry observers note that he took until the 64th minute to make changes against Leeds when Chelsea were already 3-1 down. Only three clubs had made more substitutions in the last 15 minutes than Chelsea in the league this season.

Given Leeds' strengths, Chelsea should have been better prepared for what was coming. Before kick-off, Leeds had applied more high-intensity pressures in the opposition half than any other team in the Premier League.

They had also generated the most expected goals from set-pieces and won the most duels. Leeds maintained those trends at Stamford Bridge against a Chelsea side often accused of being soft.

Chelsea have had problems in recent seasons, but this was still their worst home defeat since a 4-1 loss to Brentford in 2022.

Likewise, it is almost uncharted territory in Alonso's managerial career, having only previously lost at home by a three-goal margin once.

The stadium emptied and supporters again left early.

Players displayed negative body language and argued with one another both during the match and after the final whistle.

As a result, Alonso has gone from needing to fix defensive complications to dealing with problems that appear to be spreading throughout the squad.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Latest hire will depend on fresh faces and time to bed in at Old Trafford where the dugout churn is hardest to budge.
  • A title challenge becomes clinging on for the last Champions League spot becomes mid-table.
  • The media wonder whether the spark has gone.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Latest hire will depend on fresh faces and time to bed in at Old Trafford where the dugout churn is hardest to budge.

Everybody knows the pattern. Performances fade. Results falter. A title challenge becomes clinging on for the last Champions League spot becomes mid-table. Or a promising start becomes a troubling dip, becomes a full-on battle against relegation.

Fans begin to grumble. The media wonder whether the spark has gone. Players look disaffected. A dressing room, once lost, is seldom rediscovered, and few managers are given the opportunity to find it again. A crisis in football, once acknowledged, is only ever resolved in one way: by the sacking of the manager.

Industry observers note that with hindsight, Michael Carrick’s dismissal was probably inevitable from the moment Manchester United lost at Hull on the opening weekend, just as Ruben Amorim was doomed from the moment cameras picked him up fiddling with magnetic counters on a tactics board in the rain at Grimsby. The message for Mauricio Pochettino is clear: don’t go playing badly on the east coast.

It’s generally acknowledged that Carrick, while he may not have been the ideal manager for United, was a long way down the list of the biggest problems at the club. So what was the point of sacking him? As Pochettino begins his United career at Anfield on Sunday, what realistically can any manager hope to achieve?

Recent findings suggest that sackings have become almost ritualistic. Football demands blood sacrifice. How else can the harvest be guaranteed but by the torching of the wicker man? How else can Crystal Palace stay up but by the sacking of Pierre Sage? Once, when the manager defined the club, bought the players, decided the tactics, set the mood, that perhaps made sense. When managers were messiahs, it requires only a slight tweak to the underlying theology to see a logic in sacrificing them.

In a recent development, but managers now, at least at the majority of Premier League clubs, are part of a wider structure. In one of his meltdowns at Spurs, Antonio Conte made the point that it made little sense for him to be answering questions about the broader future of the club when he had so little power compared with the tiers of executives. Why sack the manager rather than the head of recruitment or the sporting director or the chair?

Industry observers note that the answer to that perhaps goes back to the emergence of the English idea of the manager, which began in the 1930s and blossomed in the post-war golden age of Matt Busby, Bill Shankly, Don Revie and Brian Clough. As Barney Ronay argues in The Manager, at least part of the reason he became a figure of such pre-eminence was that it was useful for the board to have a hapless ashen-faced figure standing out on the touchline to take the blame. A handful of geniuses aside, the manager was essentially a convenient scapegoat.

Recent findings suggest that but does the sacrifice work? It was one of the shibboleths of football’s early data wonks that the new manager bounce was a myth. What was being witnessed when form improved after a sacking was nothing more than regression to the mean. Which sounds sensible: squads make games and are determined by finance. There is a wealth of evidence that the biggest single factor in determining league position is the wage bill.

In a recent development, and yet there is also evidence that fresh manager bounce does exist. A lot of early data analysis in football ignored the fact that those involved are human and respond emotionally to circumstance. More recent studies, though, suggest that, while around a quarter of clubs experience no improvement, the first five matches under a new manager show a 41% improvement in points per game, although the impact wears off after around 10 games.

Recent findings suggest that that feels intuitively true and is readily explicable. A manager under pressure can become embattled, lashing out at enemies real and imagined, their capacity to make lucid decisions impaired as confidence ebbs, creating a doom spiral. Replacing him breaks that pattern and permits a psychological reset.

It has been revealed that in a world where everything is studied endlessly, a upcoming manager should make a team less predictable. It’s possible, of course, that as those early analyses suggested, performances would have turned anyway as part of a regression to the mean, but it is curious how often the uptick in form coincides with the replacement of the manager.

Industry observers note that anthropologists are yet to determine precisely why United sacrifice managers so frequently, although there does appear to be some sense of deflecting blame. There is also a sense that it has become routine, that reasons that once probably did exist have been forgotten over time.

Sacking the manager is just what the club do a few months into the season, the ritual now as divorced from its original purpose as modern Hallowe’en customs are from their origins in the Christian commemoration of All Hallows’ Eve.

It has been revealed that will the arrival of Pochettino help? He is a far more ebullient and charismatic figure than Carrick, whose status as a dead man walking for most of this season perhaps meant players did not take him as seriously as they might have an incumbent who appeared to be there for the long term, or had them beginning to ponder moves away from United.

Sources indicate that but this remains a mismatched hotchpotch of a squad assembled over six previous managers. If there is some style of play that would suit most of them it has yet to reveal itself.

According to recent reports, it will take time for Pochettino to instil in a side that are habitually outrun the levels of conditioning that characterised his Tottenham, and perhaps even longer to get them playing in a coherent pattern. There will probably have to be five or six newly introduced signings (and at least as many departures). Probably most difficult of all, there is the entire culture of the club to overhaul, which may not be possible without a change of ownership.

Given United came back from two goals behind three times in their final two games under Carrick, these are not usual circumstances: beleaguered managers rarely inspire such defiance, and the fans never turned against him. In that sense, there will not be the immediate benefit that comes when toxicity is removed.

Some sort of bounce, though, is probable under Pochettino, if only because a negative pattern has been broken. The question is how long it can be maintained.

Mauricio Pochettino endured the worst possible start to life as Manchester United manager as his side were thrashed 4-0 by fierce rivals Liverpool.

United set the tone for a disastrous afternoon early as they went a man down inside eight minutes, with Leny Yoro bundling into Alexander Isak as the last man to be shown a straight red card.

Dominik Szoboszlai fired in from the resulting free-kick to ensure Yoro’s blunder was fully punished, and Liverpool doubled their lead three minutes later when Florian Wirtz excellently improvised a volley to score.

Rio Ngumoha got a deserved goal after the break to put the game to bed, converting from Bradley Barcola’s cross, before Victor Munoz put the cherry on a ruthless performance for the hosts late on.

Mauricio Pochettino got a 13-minute crash course in the craziness of his newly introduced club. His first game was lost before he made his first substitution, and that came as early as the 22nd-minute. His debut brought the joint heaviest ever defeat by a United manager in his first game in charge, and the biggest in 100 years.

Recent findings suggest that “So painful,” Pochettino said. “So disappointed.” As can be the way with United of late, most things that could go wrong did. A first meaningful day of work revealed the scale of the task to steer United in the right direction.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • The Students' List candidates officially took their seats in the inaugural parliamentary session as the first step for the youth-backed party toward forming Serbia's new government.
  • The movement holds 140 seats in the 250-member parliament while Vucic's right-wing Serbian Progressive Party (SNS) holds 103.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Representatives of Serbia's student-led movement were sworn in as lawmakers on Tuesday, just over four weeks after they ended Serbia's strongman leader Aleksandar Vucic's 14 years of rule.

The Students' List candidates officially took their seats in the inaugural parliamentary session as the first step for the youth-backed party toward forming Serbia's new government.

The movement holds 140 seats in the 250-member parliament while Vucic's right-wing Serbian Progressive Party (SNS) holds 103. The remaining seats belong to ethnic minority parties.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Hundreds gathered outside the parliament building in the capital Belgrade, to show their support for the student-backed lawmakers, most of whom are teachers, professors and other professionals with little or no political experience.

Meanwhile, SNS candidates were met with a negative reaction from the crowd. A woman in the crowd poured yogurt over an SNS member's head as she climbed the steps to the parliament entrance.

According to Serbian media, the newly elected lawmakers have been preparing for their first session for days. They will face veteran opposition politicians, including Aleksandar Vucic, who became the opposition leader after his defeat.

The Students' List will have 90 days to name a prime minister, present their programme and form a government, once the parliament is formed.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

The movement unites left- and right-wingers, pro-European and pro-Russian forces. It is focused on making changes in domestic politics and wants to advance European Union accession talks by implementing real reforms. The List opposes sanctions on Russia and the recognition of Kosovo — positions that almost the entire population of Serbia agrees with.

They pledged to improve healthcare, boost education and double the defense budget, along with many other reforms.

The election of a latest parliamentary speaker will also lead to the appointment of a new acting president. The speaker has held the role since Vucic resigned in September to run for prime minister.

A snap presidential election must be called by November 27 and held by December 27.

Both parties are expected to put forward presidential candidates, but Vucic cannot seek another term because the constitution limits presidents to two terms in office.

Steven Pressley: ‘I’m embarrassed … I apologise’.

Celtic 4-1 St Mirren; Rangers 2-1 Motherwell.

Wouter Vrancken remarked Hearts’ remarkable 8-0 demolition of 10-man Dundee was his team’s best performance since he took charge at Tynecastle.

In a recent development, sabah Kerjota and Pierre Landry Kaboré both scored twice with Claudio Braga, Sabri Guendouz, Stuart Findlay and a Ryan Finnigan own goal completing the rout. Vrancken was naturally delighted that his players had ended a run of three defeats in a row in such spectacular style.

“Our best performance? Of course,” he noted. “When you have the confidence of one moment and then you feel the score is getting bigger, you see the players with extra confidence. You see the dynamics there and it’s good they feel it works.

According to recent reports, “It was ruthless and I like to see it this way. That was the message at half-time – that and keeping the clean sheet. But it’s only the first step, only one game and we have to try to bring more.”.

Recent findings suggest that steven Pressley admitted he was embarrassed by the result and Dundee’s performance, saying: “It’s a night I need to own, a night where I can only apologise for the performance. I never expected that.

“I had a little sense we haven’t been quite on it over the last couple of weeks but I take ownership and I mean that. We talk about the culture and environment that we set and part of that is making sure we have a fully motivated team, a team which works hard and demonstrates grit. We didn’t show that tonight but that is on me and I mean that. I’m embarrassed by it and I accept it.”.

The recalled midfielders Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain and Luke McCowan both scored as Celtic beat St Mirren 4-1. The champions brushed off the loss of midfield pair Mika Baur and Benjamin Nygren to injury to consolidate their place at the top of the Premiership.

Recent findings suggest that the centre-forward Camilo Duran was also on target as Celtic killed the game late in the first half with three goals in nine minutes. Callum McGregor grabbed his first league goal of the season before Killian Phillips scored a consolation from the spot.

With Baur facing up to 10 weeks out with an ankle injury and Nygren nursing a heel problem, Martin O’Neill would have been delighted with how his midfield functioned.

Industry observers note that oxlade-Chamberlain made his fifth start of the season and McCowan his second. The pair had never started a game together before. O’Neill also introduced the former PSV Eindhoven midfielder Joël van den Berg for a debut in the second half and the 19-year-old highlighted some good touches.

Recent findings suggest that ryan Naderi hit a deflected 88th-minute winner at Fir Park as Rangers stayed four points behind Celtic by beating Motherwell 2-1. Naderi’s effort went in off the unfortunate Motherwell defender Martin Moorman as Rangers finally made the most of some late pressure to win.

The visitors looked as if they might be held to a third draw in four away games after Jake Girdwood-Reich had cancelled out an early opener from Rangers defender Emmanuel Fernandez. Rangers had 29 shots at goal but found Motherwell goalkeeper Alex Paulsen in top form and the Newly introduced Zealand international pulled off one of the saves of the season to deny Dujon Sterling with five minutes left.

However, they netted after a corner when Naderi’s shot from eight yards went in off Moorman after the Austrian had blocked a shot from Badredine Bouanani.

Recent findings suggest that mario Frick enjoyed a dream start to life as Aberdeen manager by edging a six-goal thriller with a 4-2 win at Kilmarnock. Kevin Nisbet’s double along with Brad Lyons and Findlay Marshall strikes secured three priceless points to leave the Rugby Park side rooted to the bottom.

The visitors climbed to eighth spot after a remarkable afternoon where the Pittodrie side hit a much-needed scoring streak. Aberdeen opted to dispense with the services of Stephen Robinson after a run of one win from seven which saw them sink to second bottom and Frick was appointed as his replacement last Sunday.

Industry observers note that dundee United recorded their biggest ever win at Easter Road with an impressive 4-0 thrashing of Hibernian. Zac Sapsford’s first-half double laid the foundations before Lyall Cameron and Jesse Randall found the net after the break.

The visitors were well worth the three points as they cemented their place in the top six and picked up their first win in Leith since 2021. It was a humbling afternoon for Hibs, who thought they had turned a corner under their new head coach, Marink Reedijk, after back-to-back victories before the international break.

Falkirk clung on to clock up six top-flight wins in a row for the first time since 1966 with a 2-1 home victory against St Johnstone. John McGlynn’s team scored early in each half to remain third.

Industry observers note that jacob Murrell’s eighth goal of a superb debut season sent Falkirk on their way inside six minutes. Finley Barbrook’s second goal in as many games on 48 minutes doubled the advantage. Josh Campbell nodded in a late reply to serve up a scare but the hosts held firm.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

When it comes to English football’s best atmospheres, few can match the noise and fury of a packed Elland Road.

Since joining Leeds United from Yorkshire rivals Sheffield United in 2024, Jayden Bogle has been able to experience this on a regular basis, with his defensive efforts and lung-busting runs forward bringing the cheers of the Elland Road faithful week-in, week-out.

This backing helped Bogle’s side win promotion back to the Premier League in the right-back’s first season in West Yorkshire, which was followed up by a respectable 14th-place finish back in the top flight last term.

Leeds’ return to the Premier League last season came against Everton, a match which left a lasting impression on Bogle.

“The first game of last season [a 1-0 win over Everton] was top, that atmosphere,” he tells FourFourTwo.

In a recent development, “You really feel the impact of what the fans and the stadium can do, especially when we're making chances or someone puts in a massive tackle or block. You can feel the energy instantly from the fans.”.

The Leeds fanbase has taken its fair share of knocks over the years, and while Bogle knows just how key building this authentic connection with the fans is, it has to be done in the right way.

The best features, fun and footballing quizzes, straight to your inbox every week.

Sources indicate that “As players, you work all year round to stay as professional as you can,” he continues. “You try to have that relationship with the fans, but you've got to stay professional at the same time.”.

Leeds’ promotion campaign, which saw them win the Championship title with virtually the last kick of the season, sparked huge celebrations in the city, climaxing in an estimated 150,000 fans lining the streets for an open top bus parade.

For Bogle, this was finally a chance to share in the moment with the club’s supporters.

"On that day, it was nice to be able to really bond with them, especially after the parade.

Recent findings suggest that “Everyone was on the same page, happy and enjoying it. When we got on the bus and headed towards the city centre, it was something I'd never seen before – flares going off, people everywhere.

“It's a day that I'll never forget.”.

Industry observers note that for more than a decade, Joe Mewis has worked in football journalism as a reporter and editor. Mewis has had stints at Mirror Football and LeedsLive among others and worked at FourFourTwo throughout Euro 2024, reporting on the tournament. In addition to his journalist work, Mewis is also the author of four football history books that include times on Leeds United and the England national team. Now working as a digital marketing coordinator at Harrogate Town, too, Mewis counts some of his best career moments as being in the iconic Spygate press conference under Marcelo Bielsa and seeing his beloved Leeds lift the Championship trophy during lockdown.

Sleuth finds ‘impossible proteins’ in hundreds of research papers

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (934 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Some studies show the expression of proteins such as caspase-3 (pictured), in cell lines that should not be able to produce them.
  • It has been revealed that A scientific sleuth has identified more than 220 research papers that describe impossible patterns of protein expression in genetically altered cell lines.
  • Journals are now taking action to clean up the literature by retracting or correcting the work, and researchers warn that there are probably many more affected studies.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Some studies show the expression of proteins such as caspase-3 (pictured), in cell lines that should not be able to produce them. Credit: Dr Mark J. Winter/Science Photo Library.

It has been revealed that A scientific sleuth has identified more than 220 research papers that describe impossible patterns of protein expression in genetically altered cell lines. In these studies, particular proteins show up in imaging experiments, even though the cells do not have the gene necessary to make them.

Journals are now taking action to clean up the literature by retracting or correcting the work, and researchers warn that there are probably many more affected studies.

It has been revealed that “This problem will not go away,” indicates Thierry Soussi, a cancer geneticist at Uppsala University in Sweden, who notes that there are several other examples of the issue in now-retracted papers that were not included in the sleuth’s analysis. “This is only the tip of a gigantic iceberg.”.

Cell lines are groups of cells derived from a single origin cell and cultured for use in experiments. Some cancer cell lines have been genetically modified with mutations and deletions — often to remove genes that usually control cell division. This means that the cultures continually divide and grow, giving researchers the chance to study tumour progression and test potential treatments.

Sources indicate that the MCF-7 cell line is one of these. It lacks the gene for caspase-3 protein, which is involved in cell death. In 2009, researchers warned1 that some studies that report working with MCF-7 have mysteriously observed caspase-3 expression in western blots, an imaging technique that identifies proteins based on their molecular weight.

Sleuth identifies dozens of studies that used the wrong antibody.

Sleuth identifies dozens of studies that used the wrong antibody.

In the most recent analysis, published as a preprint on 21 October to the data repository Zenodo2, Sholto David, a sleuth based in Arbroath, UK, finds that this problem persists and extends to other cell lines.

David compiled a list of 20 commonly used cell lines with genetic mutations or deletions that leave cells unable to express specific proteins. He then scoured the literature using Google text and image searches to identify examples of western-blot images that unexpectedly identify these proteins. He also searched a collection of 140,000 articles that he had previously downloaded and screened for image-integrity issues and other problems, most of which were biomedicine papers.

In a recent development, he found 230 reports of phantom proteins across 221 papers published since 2004. The most common errors were observations of caspase-3 expression in the MCF-7 cell line, affecting 49 papers; expression of the cell-death protein BAX in the Jurkat cell line in 47 papers; and expression of the signalling protein STAT3 in the PC-3 cell line in 35 papers.

In a recent development, david suggests several explanations for these impossible protein-expression patterns. They might be the result of honest errors: researchers could have misidentified the cell lines or contaminated them with others. Or the antibodies used to identify proteins in the western-blot experiments could have been non-specific and bound to another protein with the same molecular weight. In fact, David states that he stumbled across the anomalous proteins while working on a project that flagged hundreds of studies that used the wrong antibodies in experiments.

Another possibility is that some of the papers are the product of papermills, companies that fabricate and sell scientific manuscripts. David notes that some papers in the cache contain the hallmarks of being produced by such outfits, including duplicated images or text templates that are similar to other papers. The proportion of the papers that fall into this category is not clear, he says.

Nature has contacted several authors of papers containing anomalies to ask for comment, but none responded.

Science sleuths raise concerns about scores of bioengineering papers.

Doué went down after twisting awkwardly late in the first half as he tried to control the ball, shortly after scoring to put PSG 2-1 ahead. Dominik Szoboszlai put the hosts ahead with a fierce free-kick after defender Leny Yoro was sent off for denying a goalscoring opportunity inside just eight minutes, before Florian Wirtz’s smart finish promptly put Pochettino’s side further behind.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Nvidia on Tuesday said it had created a board-level national security and export-control committee.
  • This follows the scandal surrounding former CEO Jensen Huang, who resigned last week over extramarital affairs, including one with a woman suspected of spying for China and working to help ensure higher quality chips crucial to AI development made it to the Chinese market.
  • The events have heightened oversight of the US tech giant and its importance to national security, as well as wiping several hundred billion dollars off the stock market valuation of what investors treat as the world's most valuable company in the space of a month.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Nvidia on Tuesday said it had created a board-level national security and export-control committee.

This follows the scandal surrounding former CEO Jensen Huang, who resigned last week over extramarital affairs, including one with a woman suspected of spying for China and working to help ensure higher quality chips crucial to AI development made it to the Chinese market.

The events have heightened oversight of the US tech giant and its importance to national security, as well as wiping several hundred billion dollars off the stock market valuation of what investors treat as the world's most valuable company in the space of a month.

Since Huang's resignation, some investors — including Elon Musk and Donald Trump — have voiced concern that his departure could leave Nvidia and America's AI sector in peril and are now calling for his return. Huang on Tuesday, expressed regret for "serious mistakes" in his personal life before declaring he would be "honored" to return if the tech giant's board of directors thought that was "in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the company, and America.".

Nvidia is calling the new group its National Security and Export Control Oversight Committee.

Suzanne Nora Johnson, a former vice chair at Goldman Sachs, will chair the committee, joined by fellow directors Stephen Neal, a former CEO of a law firm, John Dabiri, a professor of aeronautics and mechanical engineering at the California Institute of Technology (Caltech).

The committee will meet at least once every quarter. It will also incorporate independent legal, national security and trade compliance experts.

Nvidia already has a lower-level National Security Team and Global Trade Compliance Team; these groups will report to the board-level committee.

"We are committed to working constructively with government and industry partners to help establish and advance a robust framework that uses every tool at our disposal to safeguard national security while supporting continued technological innovation," Board Chair Harvey Jones remarked in a statement.

The tech giant did not explicitly link the decision to November's developments and Huang's rapid fall from grace, but the timing seemed conspicuous.

The decision was announced hours ahead of Nvidia publishing its third-quarter results, with its still-stratospheric share price having fallen roughly 28% in the past month.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

US President Donald Trump, whom Huang was influential in persuading to allow the export of better-quality Nvidia chips to China than other US companies and officials deemed prudent, welcomed Nvidia's move on arrival in the Philippines on Tuesday.

"Yes, that's a good idea. It's a great tech giant," he said during a photo opportunity at a Manila meeting with the other "Quad" leaders from Australia, India and Japan. "It's a great idea.".

Trump reportedly owned Nvidia stock worth tens of millions of dollars before the share price fell. He also owns shares in other massive tech companies.

It has been revealed that huang resigned last week after admitting to extramarital affairs in a message to Nvidia employees. This followed widespread reports, seemingly based on US and other intelligence, that one of the affairs was with a woman who used to lead a Singapore-based cloud computing company.

That manufacturer, Megaspseed International, is a major Nvidia client and is suspected of diverting advanced chips to China in violation of US export controls. Intelligence officials also suspect Huang's partner of being an asset of Chinese intelligence services.

The reporting on the case also seems to show these suspicions had been known to US officials and other countries, including Singapore, for roughly a year.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Industry observers note that villa were too predictable, short of a spark, someone to unpick an organised back line.
  • Recent findings suggest that “I am trying to select the players I think that are ready to play and the selection is thinking for the best of the team,” noted Emery, who was again reluctant to blame the empty North Stand as a factor behind their disappointing home form, a sharp contrast to their 11-game winning run here last season.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

For Aston Villa, a painful stalemate at home to Sunderland, but for Régis Le Bris and his players, this was another triumph of sorts. The raw numbers spoke volumes of Villa’s struggles against a defence that backed themselves to keep Unai Emery’s side at bay. All but one of Villa’s seven shots on target came from outside the visitors’ box and the one inside it, courtesy of Ian Maatsen, was forgettable. Owing to a summer of change, injuries and Emery resting John McGinn with Tuesday’s game at Galatasaray in mind, Maatsen, incredibly, was the sole survivor in the Villa starting XI from when these sides played out a 4-3 classic seven months ago.

Industry observers note that villa were too predictable, short of a spark, someone to unpick an organised back line. Johan Manzambi, Emi Buendía and Alysson all flattered to deceive on an afternoon when Ibrahim Mbaye and McGinn arrived from the bench. Alejandro Garnacho, however, was not involved in Villa’s matchday squad for the second successive match and the Chelsea loanee has played just 38 minutes in the Premier League this campaign. Tammy Abraham, the match-winner in April, was also left out and a January move looks likely.

Recent findings suggest that “I am trying to select the players I think that are ready to play and the selection is thinking for the best of the team,” noted Emery, who was again reluctant to blame the empty North Stand as a factor behind their disappointing home form, a sharp contrast to their 11-game winning run here last season. “In my experiences here and in Spain, when they [stadiums] are in works like we are in now, it’s a small sacrifice, but it’s not an excuse,” Villa’s manager added. “We have to play with this situation and next year it will be better.”.

Villa’s frustration was underlined by a moment on the verge of half-time, when Emery gave Sunderland’s kit man, Luke Purcell, a gentle shove on the sidelines in an attempt to speed up a Villa restart. “We have increased our demands a lot, our level, but still there are favourites in front of us, to reach the top six, top four,” Emery said. “We are now again in a new construction with some new players who are sharing their qualities and we are trying to mix different players, young players to build our structure as fast as possible.”.

With 90 minutes and 25 seconds showing on the massive screens, Chemsdine Talbi almost snatched victory for Sunderland, the Moroccan winger shaving the upright of Zion Suzuki’s goal with a spell-bending strike. Talbi did almost everything right, bursting past Aaron Wan-Bissaka, comfortably eliminating the defender, before using Boubacar Kamara as a mannequin to get his bearings, but his curling right-foot shot was ultimately a few inches too close to the post. For Villa, a first clean sheet in the league here since March, but this draw extended their winless run to five matches in all competitions.

For Sunderland, this may not have been the dopamine hit of beating Chelsea, but it was was another gutsy showing, and without two key players in Granit Xhaka and Brian Brobbey, both of whom were absent through injury. It was a big team performance, another feather in the cap of Jules Ahoka, the 20-year-old midfielder who shone on his first Premier League start. Ahoka started last season playing on sandy pitches in the Democratic Republic of Congo’s second division. “He is getting better game after game,” Le Bris noted.

Sunderland were happy to soak up the Villa pressure. Emery introduced the 17-year-old Brian Madjo, who trained with England under-21s during the international break, but in place of Nicolas Jackson rather than to join him in attack. By which point Mbaye had entered and combined with McGinn to fashion another nearly moment. Disbelief reigned in the stands, but had Talbi located the top corner, things could have felt a lot worse at the final whistle.

Space is filling up with junk. Could laser-reflecting mirrors help humanity clean things up?

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (608 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Space

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • A British startup thinks it can help humanity deal with its space junk problem.
  • Recent findings suggest that millions of pieces of space debris circle Earth at the moment, according to the European Space Agency (ESA).
  • According to recent reports, experts have proposed a range of measures to deal with this junk.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A British startup thinks it can help humanity deal with its space junk problem.

Recent findings suggest that millions of pieces of space debris circle Earth at the moment, according to the European Space Agency (ESA). Even the smallest fragments are potentially dangerous, given how fast stuff travels in orbit.

According to recent reports, experts have proposed a range of measures to deal with this junk. The smallest bits, for example, may require significant space nets, or lasering the stuff down to Earth. Large satellites are increasingly being deliberately deorbited these days, and a few have even been refueled to keep them operating in orbit — something that will likely start happening more and more over the coming years.

Now, the British startup Foundational has another idea to throw into the mix: retroreflectors. The company argues that its tech can help fight the space-junk problem — and it just proved out a demo version in an orbital test.

London-based Foundational recently tested its Retro-2 laser retroreflector system, which it developed in collaboration with ESA. The early-stage test was designed to ensure that Foundational's retroreflectors can return laser-ranging signals from a satellite, at altitudes between about 600 kilometers and 870 kilometers (about 370 to 540 miles), with a usable range distance of 300 to 1,400 km (186 to 870 miles).

The long-term aim is to create a sort of tracking device for spacecraft, so they can be monitored in orbit even after they fall silent.

According to recent reports, the tech, Foundational remarked in a statement today (Nov. 17), needs "no electronics, power or commands from its host spacecraft" and allows ground stations to keep tabs on the orbiting spacecraft.

Industry observers note that the demo mission released this past July on SpaceX's Transporter-17 rideshare flight. It attached Retro-2 — a mini device with seven reflectors — to a small satellite that was integrated into an ION carrier craft operated by the Italian company D-Orbit.

Retro-2 worked as advertised, successfully returning 6,111 laser shots beamed from the from the ground across five passes in low Earth orbit.

According to recent reports, "Our tests have shown that a device weighing just 50 grams [1.8 ounces] can deliver millimeter-level ranging precision," Dave Gooding, Foundational's co-founder and chief technical officer, said in today's statement. "As space becomes increasingly crowded, keeping satellites trackable throughout their lifetime and beyond is critical to managing collision risks.".

It has been revealed that foundational is in its early stages — it was founded in 2025 and just emerged from stealth last month. Nevertheless the organization has already raised £8.2 million ($10.9 million) in pre-seed funding.

Foundational is part of a range of companies involved in debris removal, satellite servicing or debris tracking that have raised funds in 2026. Others include Starfish Space (which raised more than $100 million in a Series B), Katalyst Space ($12 million in funding) and international companies like India's Cosmoserve Space.

She was contributing writer for Space.com for 10 years from 2012 to 2024. Elizabeth's reporting includes multiple exclusives with the White House, leading world coverage about a lost-and-found space tomato on the International Space Station, witnessing five human spaceflight introduces on two continents, flying parabolic, working inside a spacesuit, and participating in a simulated Mars mission. Her latest book, "Why Am I Taller?" (ECW Press, 2022) is co-written with astronaut Dave Williams.

#116670. NASA's Voyager 1 debuted second, so how did it beat Voyager 2 to a light-day by nearly a decade?

📅 17 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (930 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Space ↗ Open Full Page

NASA's Voyager 1 debuted second, so how did it beat Voyager 2 to a light-day by nearly a decade?

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (930 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Space

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that voyager 1 is about to reach a light-day of distance in space, but Voyager 2 won't hit the mark until about 2035.
  • 18, Voyager 1 will be so far away from Earth that it will take a full light-day (24 hours) to send a signal to the distant spacecraft, at 16,094,799,096 miles (25,902,068,356 kilometers).
  • Industry observers note that but why will Voyager 2 take nearly a decade longer?
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that voyager 1 is about to reach a light-day of distance in space, but Voyager 2 won't hit the mark until about 2035. Why the big difference?

It has been revealed that on Nov. 18, Voyager 1 will be so far away from Earth that it will take a full light-day (24 hours) to send a signal to the distant spacecraft, at 16,094,799,096 miles (25,902,068,356 kilometers). Since light is essentially the maximum speed in the universe (absent using devices like wormholes, or quantum-physics puzzles), it's a big deal — so big that NASA will be celebrating the milestone by asking fans to shine Morse Code signals at the sky.

Industry observers note that but why will Voyager 2 take nearly a decade longer? It comes down to choices made for speed and science during the twin missions' nearly 50-year journey, specifically during the first bit when they were flying by planets. The result is Voyager 1 is zooming out at a speed of 3.5 Earth-sun distances (astronomical units a year), while Voyager 2 has a more stately speed of 3.1 Earth-sun distances, according to NASA.

It has been revealed that the original aim of both the spacecraft, which rolled out about two weeks apart in 1977 with Voyager 2 going first, was to look at Jupiter and Saturn. If funding persisted, which it did, the hope was to bring Voyager 2 past Uranus and Neptune, taking advantage of a rare planetary alignment. Voyager 1, by contrast, made a turn at Saturn to look at the planet's rings and the prebiotic (pre-life-chemistry) moon of Titan, before flying outside the plane of the solar system.

NASA had a range of trajectory options to consider when launching the spacecraft, and elected to bring Voyager 1 at a faster trajectory — as illustrated in this video by Britannica, where you can swiftly see the spacecraft overtaking Voyager 2 on its way to Jupiter even though Voyager 1. Voyager 1 arrived at Jupiter on March 5, 1979 while Voyager 2 got there four months later on July 9.

It has been revealed that each of the spacecraft then performed a "gravity assist"—a sort of slingshot around the planet in which they took a tiny bit of momentum from Jupiter to gain speed as the spacecraft flew to Saturn. This technique is used constantly, such as recently when the ESCAPADE Mars mission flew two spacecraft by Earth on the way to the Red Planet, as it allows spacecraft to gain speed while saving on fuel. The planets themselves don't slow down that much.

In a recent development, "Because the planet is so much more massive than the spacecraft, the transfer doesn't affect the planet to any measurable extent, but to the spacecraft it's a substantial deal," the Planetary Society wrote. "For example, we can calculate that during the Voyager encounters with Jupiter in 1979, Jupiter slowed down by roughly 10 to the -24th power kilometers per second — a change much too small to measure.".

"But each Voyager gained about 10 km/s [6.2 miles/s], a pretty substantial number," the society continued about the Jupiter encounter. This was "enough to put them on a fast path to Saturn — and in the case of Voyager 2, to Uranus and Neptune as well — and eventual escape from the solar system.".

In a recent development, with each flyby, the two spacecraft picked up speed with a single exception — during Voyager 2's encounter of Neptune. That's because the spacecraft made a turn to fly by Triton. The maneuver brought Voyager 2 over Neptune's north pole, before it turned and then was directed to begin "plunging down, out of the plane of the solar system," losing speed along the way.

Voyager 2, in fact, did not have enough speed to leave the solar system until it flew by Jupiter. "It gained about 10 km/s at Jupiter, about 5 km/s at Saturn, about 2 km/s at Uranus, and lost about 2 km/s at Neptune," the Planetary Society wrote of the speeds, which are 6.21 miles/s, 3.11 miles/s, 1.24 miles/s and a loss of 1.24 miles/s, respectively.

According to recent reports, at any rate, these fast speeds allowed both spacecraft not only to go fast, but to eventually reach interstellar space in 2012 (Voyager 1) and 2018 (Voyager 2), respectively. With the light-day milestone now reached by Voyager 1, it is anticipated the spacecraft could work into the 2030s, as long as their nuclear power sources can last.

NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory, which manages the mission, has been carefully turning off instruments as required, and recently did a "Massive Bang" procedure on both spacecraft to redistribute power supplies as best as possible. The idea is to maximize science return on both spacecraft, the only interstellar messengers we have, for as long as possible.

The European Court of Human Rights (ECHR) ruled against Turkey over the detention of human rights lawyer and elected lawmaker Can Atalay.

The ECHR published its decision on Tuesday, saying that Turkey must release Atalay and allow him to take up his seat in the Turkish parliament.

The court ruled that his continued detention had been intended to silence him and undermine political pluralism.

It ordered Turkey to pay him €32,500 (about $35,700) in compensation.

The judges stressed that Atalay's case should not be considered separately, but rather in the wider context of the detention of political opponents, human rights activists and journalists in Turkey.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

In a recent development, turkey was among the original signatories of the European Convention on Human Rights. Yet it has previously refused to comply with the court's decisions in the cases of rights activist Osman Kavala and prominent Kurdish politician Selahattin Demirtas.

As a lawyer, Atalay represented victims in numerous social and political cases in Turkey, as well as in freedom of speech cases involving journalists and writers.

He was also among the leading voices in the 2013 Gezi protests, which the government called an attempted coup.

Because of his involvement in the protests, Atalay, along with seven others, was sentenced to 18 years in prison in April 2022 for "aiding and abetting an attempted coup.".

Continuing his struggle from the infamous Silivri prison, Atalay ran as a candidate for the Workers' Party of Turkey (TIP) in the 2023 parliamentary elections.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

A candidate for the earthquake-hit province of Hatay, he won his seat but was denied release despite multiple rulings by the Constitutional Court, Turkey's top court.

In a recent development, his parliamentary status was revoked in 2024, a decision the Constitutional Court later overturned. President Recep Tayyip Erdogan's party stopped the opposition from formally reading the decision in parliament.

Although a year later an opposition lawmaker read the decision in parliament, Atalay remains in jail.

After the ECHR's ruling was published, TIP leader Erkan Bas took to social media to call for Atalay's release and the restoration of his parliamentary mandate.

Shania Twain is standing up for others in country music.

The legendary star in the genre used her acceptance speech for the Equal Play Award at Sunday’s CMT Awards to call for more equity and diversity in the country music industry.

“When I wrote the phrase ‘Man I feel like a woman’ I honestly had no idea at the time it would become an undercurrent of a decades-long career,” she said, referring to one of her biggest hits. “It’s amazing how one statement can empower so many.”.

The phrase, Twain mentioned, “has been adopted by an array of fantastic communities all around the world and become a genuine path of power…which brings me so much joy.”.

“I believe in an all-inclusive country music. We’re family,” Twain mentioned. “This is a genre of music with a rich history that raised and nurtured my own songwriting and performance and recording career from childhood. At the moment, the industry standard does a real disservice to this.”.

Twain, who was presented the award by rapper Megan Thee Stallion, shouted out some of the diverse acts she is spotlighting on her “Queen of Me” tour this year, including Lily Rose, Lindsay Ell, Hailey Whitters, Mickey Guyton and others.

“I will continue to do my best as a trailblazer,” Twain mentioned. “Together, let’s ensure all our fellow artists get equal play regardless of gender, age or race.”.

She also performed acappella with the African American singing group, The BoykinZ, while presenting an award onstage. Twain connected with the group, who are sisters and rising country stars, after Kelly Clarkson surprised them recently by bringing Twain out to meet them during an episode of Clarkson’s daytime talk show.

Ian Watson was in his first EFL managerial role at Rochdale.

Rochdale have sacked head coach Ian Watson after only five months in charge of the League Two club.

The former South Shields boss replaced promotion-winning manager Jimmy McNulty in June after he joined Stockport but leaves the club just two points clear of the relegation zone.

Watson took South Shields to the National League North play-off final last season where they were beaten by Kidderminster Harriers before taking up his first Football League role at Spotland.

After returning to the EFL by beating Boreham Wood in last season's National League promotion final, Rochdale have won only four of their 16 League Two matches so far this season.

He departs following Saturday's 3-2 defeat by Northampton Town which was their fourth successive loss and left them 22nd in the table.

"We would like to thank Ian for his hard work and commitment during his time at the Crown Oil Arena and wish him every success in the future," said a club statement., external.

"The process to appoint a successor is already underway, and the club will give a further revision in due course.".

Rochdale are next in action at home to Barnet on Saturday, 28 November (15:00 GMT).
