Jim Goodwin's side are eight games unbeaten, with Zidane Iqbal pivotal.

Hibernian v Dundee United highlights.

Given the superlatives being thrown in the direction of Zidane Iqbal by the Scottish football fraternity, one would think he was a replica of a certain France great instead of just sharing his name.

So much so that BBC Radio Scotland pundits were suggesting on Saturday's Sportsound that the 23-year-old is the answer to Celtic's hunt for a long-term successor to captain Callum McGregor as their midfield general.

It is just as well for Dundee United that the Iraq international is tied to them until at least the summer, his early season appearances for Utrecht ruling out a transfer during the January window.

So, where has he sprung from and what is all the fuss about?

'Goodwin due a lot of credit and kudos'.

Hibs 0-4 Dundee United: What Goodwin noted.

Born in Manchester to a Pakistani father and an Iraqi mother, Iqbal came through the Old Trafford youth system.

He signed his first professional contract with United in 2021 and became the first British-born South Asian and first-ever British South Asian to play in the Champions League when he came on as an 89th-minute substitute against Young Boys that December.

However, that was to be his one and only first-team appearance and, although he had already made his international debut in a World Cup qualifier at the age of 19, he was sold to Utrecht for a reported fee of Â£1m in summer 2023.

Starting off in their Jong Utrecht second string, he would go on to make 49 appearances for the Dutch top-flight outfit before making a surprise switch to the Scottish Premiership this summer.

On the one hand, United were getting a player who played all three of Iraq's games at this summer's World Cup, two of them starts, albeit all three were heavy defeats.

On the other hand, Iqbal had only managed seven appearances last season for Utrecht and had been a second-half substitute in two of their four matches at the start of the newly introduced campaign.

However, after a pivotal display in what was being described as a midfield "masterclass" by United in Saturday's 4-0 dismantling of hosts Hibernian, manager Jim Goodwin revealed he always had belief the Tangerines were unearthing a "Rolls-Royce".

Recent findings suggest that "The head of recruitment's job is to go and identify good talent for us," Goodwin told BBC Scotland. "It's my job to give him the profile and then he goes out and does the groundwork.

"We could see immediately when we watched the footage of Zidane and when we had the Zoom call with him and his representatives, we not only had a fantastic player but a really good person with the right characteristics to come and fit the culture here.".

Zidane Iqbal was also a marked man at the World Cup finals.

While on-loan Rangers man Lyall Cameron was among the goals and fellow 24-year-old Dylan Tait provided a stylish assist, it was the third leg of what some regard as the best midfield triumvirate in the Premiership who was singled out for most praise at Easter Road.

In a recent development, with former Celtic winger Aidan McGeady again pondering the question about McGregor's likely successor, transfer market expert and former United wing-back Allan Preston opined: "A six for Celtic? Look no further than young Iqbal.

"He's been magnificent since he's come to Scottish football, absolutely brilliant. Running the show again.

"If Celtic are looking for a young boy at his age with experience, he is a full international, knows the game, played in Scotland, you can see what he can do, there's your man in front of you.

Sources indicate that "Other players' hair's on fire, but he's just nice and calm. He's at a different level. He doesn't panic. When the ball comes to him, he is so calm on it, he takes his time, he's got great peripheral vision.".

The former Dundee United wing-back pointed out, though: "He's had his two clubs that he can play for in a year of football, so he is going nowhere until at least the summer, so enjoy him while you can because I think you'll get serious money for this young boy.".

McGeady pointed to Iqbal's "good pedigree", having started with Manchester United and already having 32 caps for Iraq, but wondered if that would be enough for Celtic to consider him.

"I don't even think, if he's performing this well, Celtic will go and get him," mentioned McGeady.

In a recent development, "Why are Celtic not looking at players like this? Do they feel they have to prove themselves somewhere else first?".

Former Celtic captain Scott Brown was similarly impressed.

"He's been a delight to watch - sharpness to get on the ball and willingness to drive forward," the former midfielder and manager pointed out.

"He beats a man in the middle of the park as well and there's not too many midfielders willing to do that.

"Watching him there talking to the media, he can't get the smile off his face. He enjoys football, he takes the ball under pressure, he does things that other people don't do, especially in midfield.

According to recent reports, "He brings composure, but he can also drive through as well. His willingness to keep getting on the ball, even if he makes that slight mistake - that's what I really enjoy watching about him.".

While Goodwin reckons there will be likely interest in the summer, Iqbal has no thoughts of so quickly leaving a club - and manager - who have resurrected his club career.

"I'm not even looking at any other clubs," he told BBC Scotland. "I'm fully focused on Dundee United.

Sources indicate that "They've given me a platform to enjoy myself and play football. I'm really enjoying my football again.

According to recent reports, "They've given me faith and confidence. The gaffer and the coaching staff have a lot of belief in me.

"The bare minimum I can do is pay them back with strong performances and hopefully it carries on.".

Iqbal recalled being at Manchester United's "development centre since I was four or five - I signed when I was eight", explaining that he "then left for some first-team football".

He stressed that his lack of games last season came as a result of "a couple of injuries" and, while "I learnt a lot in Holland", he is "happy to have left that behind me", adding: "That book's closed now.".

Visit our Dundee United page for all the latest news, analysis and fan views.

Get Dundee United news notifications in the BBC Sport app.

Iqbal also recalled how Goodwin's enthusiasm persuaded him to make the switch to Tannadice on deadline day.

In a recent development, "After the World Cup, I had one year left on my contract and I was in touch with my agent," the midfielder mentioned. "We both wanted a move and I had a few chats with a few clubs.

"To be fair, I left it a bit late for Dundee United, but after the first call with the gaffer, I straight away called my agent after we ended the call.

"I stated, 'look, I genuinely feel like the guy really believes in me'.

According to recent reports, "It happened very late. I had to drive from Holland to Scotland. It was a tough drive but worth it in the end.".

That World Cup was also a defining experience, with representing his country in the United States described as surreal.

"Having your friends and family there to watch you and playing on the world stage, with so many people, was a dream," he stated.

In a recent development, "Playing against top players gave me that confidence boost I needed. I thought I did well in the three tough games.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • The club’s new ownership group, led by American businessman Todd Boehly, had enticed Potter away from Brighton with the promise of managing one of the most lucrative teams in world soccer.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It was just six months ago that Graham Potter was deemed the man to usher in a fresh, exciting era at Chelsea.

The club’s new ownership group, led by American businessman Todd Boehly, had enticed Potter away from Brighton with the promise of managing one of the most lucrative teams in world soccer.

More than $600 million was spent on bringing massive-name players to the club and Potter, one of the most exciting young managers in the Premier League, was to mold them into a winning machine.

Chelsea has spent over $600 million on fresh signings. Here's why that's significant.

But, on Sunday, the club announced that it had sacked its manager after an underwhelming spell in charge.

Potter managed to win just 10 of the 28 league matches this season and leaves the team 11th in the Premier League table.

In recent weeks, players had looked a shadow of their former selves and many fans had lost confidence that Potter’s plan for the club could ever work.

Eventually, after previously sticking by its manager, Blues ownership agreed.

“On behalf of everyone at the club, we want to thank Graham sincerely for his contribution to Chelsea,” the club’s co-owners Todd Boehly and Behdad Eghbali stated in a statement.

“We have the highest degree of respect for Graham as a coach and as a person. He has always conducted himself with professionalism and integrity and we are all disappointed in this outcome.”.

In his previous role as Brighton manager, Potter was given time to stamp his identity on the squad.

The club was punching above its weight financially and, as a result, carefully selected newly introduced signings which would compliment Potter’s style of play.

The approach paid off as the team became an established Premier League outfit which has gone on to greater things this season – the Seagulls right now sit sixth in the league and in the UEFA Conference League qualification spot.

At Chelsea, it seemed the complete opposite.

As was the case under previous owner Roman Abramovich, the club expected instant results and used its financial weight to sign a number of high-profile names, including the likes of Enzo Fernández and Mykhailo Mudryk.

Despite his impressive CV, Potter had never managed superstars and suddenly found himself in a changing room with multiple.

The scatter gun approach to recruitment also left the team lacking balance and organization with Potter failing to get a tune out of a team busting with talent.

In truth, many had raised an eyebrow when Potter, inexperienced at the very top level, was chosen to replace Thomas Tuchel as manager.

Despite falling out of favor with fans by the end of his tenure, Tuchel had guided Chelsea to the Champions League title in 2021 and is still considered by many as one of the best coaches in the world.

The German has gone on to sign with Bavarian giant Bayern Munich through the 2024/25 season and recently told reporters he needed “quite a bit of time to distance himself from Chelsea” because leaving the club had hurt him.

Bayern Munich sacks manager Julian Nagelsmann, appoints Thomas Tuchel.

“Todd [Boehly] noted he would be different to Roman [Abramovich],” former Liverpool player and current pundit Jamie Carragher wrote on Twitter.

“I feel for Graham Potter, but it was inevitable. You don’t change Tuchel for Potter. Ridiculous decision to start with.”.

With 10 games left in the league and a Champions League quarterfinal against Real Madrid on the horizon, Chelsea still has plenty to play for.

Assistant coach Bruno Saltor will take over on an interim basis, but Boehly and his team must now look for a long-term replacement capable – and willing – to bring order to Chelsea’s chaos.

Potter’s sacking is yet another sign of just how transient managers can be in the top-flight of English football, especially when results aren’t instantaneous.

There has now been a record 12 sackings in the Premier League so far this season, with Potter leaving his position the same day Leicester boss Brendan Rodgers was sacked from his.

The previous record was 10 manager changes in a single season, set in four other campaigns, most recently in 2017/18.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Nicolas Pepe (right) wore an eye mask on his return to the side following his eye operation in October.

Villarreal say reports striker Nicolas Pepe needed eye surgery because he stared directly at the solar eclipse are "completely false".

In a statement, the Spanish club said an operation in October that ruled the 31-year-old out for six matches was "scheduled in advance" and "entirely unrelated" to the eclipse, which took place on 12 August.

Reports on social media suggested the former Arsenal forward had injured his eyes staring directly at the sun during the lunar event, with a video then emerging - purportedly from one of Pepe's social media accounts - showing him watching it in Spain.

"Villarreal CF, in response to reports published in various media outlets recently, clarifies that it is completely false that Nicolas Pepe's eye surgery has any connection to viewing the solar eclipse," remarked the club.

"The surgery had been scheduled in advance for reasons entirely unrelated to this event.

"The club urges accuracy and responsibility when reporting on matters related to its players' health.".

Staring at an eclipse without protection can damage the retina, which sits at the back of the eye, and particularly those cells responsible for sharp central vision.

In the build-up to this summer's event, experts warned only genuine specially-designed solar eclipse glasses should be used, and that ordinary sunglasses or other devices were not enough to prevent potential damage.

Pepe has scored 14 goals in 86 appearances in all competitions for Villarreal after joining from Trabzonspor in 2024.

He cost Arsenal a then-club record Â£72m when he joined from Lille in the summer of 2019.

Pepe scored 27 goals in 112 games for the Gunners and had a loan spell at Nice before joining Trabzonspor on a free transfer.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • New manager, new formation, familiar defensive failings.
  • Yet for much of the second half, there had been reasons for Palace optimism.
  • Sometimes football is simply a bit daft, a series of events linked by very little discernible pattern – and that’s how it was before the break.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

New manager, new formation, familiar defensive failings. Twice Crystal Palace equalised. They seemed to have stabilised after half-time. But sometimes the rot is so deep-rooted that the new manager bounce manifests as nothing more than it not looking quite as shambolic as it did before. Thomas Frank started with a defeat that means Palace remain bottom of the table having lost five league games in a row.

Yet for much of the second half, there had been reasons for Palace optimism. They seemed to have settled better after a ludicrous first half in which neither side looked at all capable of defending. But a triple substitution by Frank Lampard with 20 minutes to go shifted the game back in Coventry’s favour. With five minutes remaining, a long throw arced into the box. Brandon Thomas-Asante headed it goalwards. Dean Henderson got in the way but the ball bounced off him, hit Dwight McNeil and ricocheted in. “We came through with spirit,” Lampard stated. “There was good play and a major impact from the subs. It’s a good sign for the squad.”.

Sometimes football is simply a bit daft, a series of events linked by very little discernible pattern – and that’s how it was before the break. Perhaps that’s just what happens when two of the three teams with the lowest possession stats in the league meet up; they can’t both not have the ball and so at least one side ends up having to do something they’re not used to. The second half was rather less frenetic and rather more coherent, as Palace’s full-backs played more conservatively.

Industry observers note that “There are more positives than negatives from the game,” stated Frank. “Offensively we looked like a threat. The effort and mentality I was extremely happy with. Defensively we conceded the first goal in a situation we 100% should have defended better, then an individual mistake. We’ll keep working on it, keep reinforcing the message in terms of what we want to do.”.

In itself, playing without the ball is not a problem; absorbing pressure and striking on the break is a perfectly legitimate tactic and Lampard’s side have done it well at times this season. Palace are a slightly different case, given the obvious disconnect between their possession figure and Pierre Sage’s insistence he wanted to defend by holding the ball. That disparity, the sense that Palace’s players were unable to play as he wanted them to play, was probably the strongest argument in favour of cutting their losses rapidly.

Frank abandoned the back three that had been the default not merely under Sage but also under Oliver Glasner, preferring a 4-3-2-1 with Anan Khalaili returning at right-back. It’s fair to say the Israel international is rather better going forward than at defending; playing at full-back rather than wing-back looked a real struggle for him – although he may feel there was mitigation in the way he was repeatedly left exposed. It took just five minutes for Coventry to open Palace up on that flank, three players converging on Yann Gboho as he backheeled a return pass to Jack Rudoni, who swept it across the box for Taiwo Awoniyi to stroke in.

• Coventry have won four of their last seven Premier League games (L3), with no side scoring more goals in the competition since the beginning of October (12, level with Bournemouth).

• Crystal Palace have conceded 27 goals in the Premier League this season; only in 1927-28 in the Third Division South have they conceded as many or more after 11 games in a league campaign (28).

• Only Brighton (6) have scored more goals from outside the box than Coventry City (4) in the Premier League this season, with 31% of the Sky Blues’ goals this term being scored from distance (4/13) – only Spurs (33% - 4/12) have a higher such share.

In a recent development, • In what was his 115th Premier League game as a manager, Frank Lampard (pictured) has been booked for the first time, while he also didn’t receive a single yellow card in any of his last 31 Premier League games as a player. Opta.

It soon became clear, though, that this was never a game of only one goal. It was startlingly, thrillingly, almost disconcertingly open, with chances at either end. Yéremy Pino levelled, thrashing in after Jørgen Strand Larsen had laid off Daichi Kamada’s overhit cross with an outstretched heel. Then Khalaili missed his tackle, allowing Rudoni to surge forward and square for Tatsuhiro Sakamoto who, from just outside the box, lashed the bouncing ball into the top corner. Palace’s second equaliser was the result of a complete defensive breakdown. Pino’s initial cross was blocked and when he dinked in a second attempt, the only player even close to marking Strand Larsen was his teammate Kamada.

Coventry’s threat had seemed diminished in the second half, partly as Palace looked less skittish and partly because Awoniyi aggravated an ankle injury and was unable to continue after the break. But those late substitutions gave them new impetus and, after a very silly first half, the game was won with a pretty silly goal.

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Two years of fan pressure and criticism has forced Borussia Dortmund to drop a sponsorship deal with Germany's largest arms manufacturer, Rheinmetall.

The Bundesliga club will not renew its deal with Rheinmetall beyond its expiry in June 2027, at the end of this season. Dortmund chairman Carsten Cramer confirmed the news on the club's website ahead of its AGM on Sunday, which may have proved a potential flashpoint. He acknowledged that "our partnership has been controversial from the outset" but lamented the loss of income.

In a recent development, "It reduces our financial room for manoeuvre. We will have to reprioritize planned investments and carefully examine how we can find viable solutions.".

Though he welcomed the news, one of the leaders of the fan revolt against the partnership, Michael Schulze von Glaser, warned this is likely not the end of the road.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

"I think in the end it was a victory for the fans. But I'm also a bit skeptical about  what the future will bring us," the Dortmund fan and former head of the German Peace Society told DW. "Football fans in Germany always must be skeptical and always must watch what the club is doing.”.

According to recent reports, many Dortmund fans have opposed the deal — which has seen Rheinmetall's logo on advertising boards and other surfaces at locations such as Dortmund's 83,000-capacity Westfalenstadion — from its beginnings in 2024. It was estimated to be worth between €7 ($7.68 million) and €9 million per year.

In a recent development, at the club's AGM that year, 556 of 855 members present voted against the deal in a non-binding vote. There were 247 votes in favour, with 52 abstentions. This, stated Cramer, informed the eventual outcome.

Rheinmetall sells arms mostly to Germany, Ukraine and NATO but fans and critics feel that platforming any arms manufacturer goes against the club's statement of its core values. In that, Dortmund states its desire for "a club and a society that operate free of racism, anti-Semitism, LGBTQIA+ hostility, sexism, violence and discrimination.".

To play this audio please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 audio.

It has always been clear, stated Schulze von Glaser, that this deal did not chime with that.

Sources indicate that "In the end, they kill people. They are for war," he mentioned of Rheinmetall. "The slogan of Borussia Dortmund is true love (Echte Liebe). But for me and many others, our love ends there…. I know some fans who have put fan merchandise in the trash because they were so shocked.”.

Industry observers note that in the Q and A on the club's website, Cramer said he was still a "personal advocate" of the deal but that Dortmund's commitment to the 50+1 model, which means German clubs are majority controlled by the members, meant they had to listen to fan voices. But he also warned that Rheinmetall must be an "absolute exception and an isolated case.".

That set off some alarm bells for Schulze von Glaser.

"It's a bit concerning that there are constantly these attacks on professional football — a fresh sponsorship, investment deals," he said.

Indeed, Dortmund's climbdown is not the first of its kind in Germany's top flight. Last year, after fan and media pressure, Bayern Munich ended its commercial deal with the tourism arm of the Rwandan government before its conclusion.

Fans had objected to the promotion of Rwanda, which many felt sought to divert attention from its poor human rights record and actions in the war with DR Congo, through sporting partnerships. Two years earlier, Bayern withdrew from a similarly controversial deal with Qatar Airways.

It has been revealed that elsewhere in the league, Werder Bremen fans objected to their long time shirt sponsor, Wiesenhof. Many supporters took issue with the factory farming practices  of Germany's largest poultry producer. Though it was not given as a direct reason for the end of a shirt sponsorship deal in 2023, it likely played a part.

Union Berlin fans have also made their voices heard. When the club signed a upcoming shirt-sponsorship deal with Luxembourg real estate tech giant, Aroundtown, upon promotion to the top flight in 2019, many fans were frustrated at the tie up in a city where rent prices were skyrocketing.

"It's a problem for a lot of people," fan Sven Dobberstein told DW at the time.

Industry observers note that "We have to try to find a way between commercialization and what we have at the moment. It isn't easy.".

According to recent reports, striking that balance can often be a source of tension for Bundesliga clubs. 50+1 ensures fans have a voice, preventing rich owners, or nation states, from taking control as they do in England's lucrative Premier League or in France or Spain. Indeed fan protests have also stopped the league signing a €1billion private equity partner and seen Monday night matches scrapped. For Schulze von Glaser, this needs to be protected.

"In Germany, the fan culture has an impact," he mentioned.

”If there is something bad or terrible happening in your club and in the Bundesliga, there are the organized fans and they can have an impact if they want, if they stand together and, yes, they can stop the Rheinmetall deal.".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The first satellite in a constellation designed for humanitarian use will lift off next year, if all goes according to plan.

The nonprofit Common Space looks to assemble a six-spacecraft constellation of Earth-observing satellites, whose high-resolution imagery will aid first responders, journalists, scientists and human-rights investigators around the world.

Recent findings suggest that that plan firmed up a bit today (Nov. 19), as Common Space unveiled the builder of the first of those satellites: Satellogic, an Argentine-U.S. geospatial intelligence company.

According to recent reports, there are more than 1,000 Earth-observing satellites circling our planet at the moment. But much of the data they gather is proprietary or too expensive to serve the common good, according to Common Space.

According to recent reports, the nonprofit wants to change that via its envisioned constellation, which it indicates will collect imagery specifically for humanitarian and public-interest purposes. Common Space intends to operate on a "club-good model," which will share infrastructure and costs across a large community, allowing extensive, low-cost access to high-quality imagery.

Satellogic is now officially part of this picture.

Sources indicate that "With Satellogic as our spacecraft partner, we're moving from vision to orbit and putting high-resolution data into the hands of those who need it most," Common Space co-founder Rhiannan Price said in a statement today. "This isn't just another satellite. We're building infrastructure to serve people for years to come.".

The satellite is Satellogic's NewSat Mark V, which Common Space selected after a competitive request-for-proposal process.

Industry observers note that the NewSat Mark V is just 32 inches (82 centimeters) long and weighs 85 pounds (38.5 kilograms) here on Earth. But the microsatellite packs a great deal of capability into that small package. From low Earth orbit (LEO), it naturally resolves features on the ground as small as 27.5 inches (70 cm), which Satellogic's proprietary algorithms can boost to a "super resolution" of 19.7 inches (50 cm).

Industry observers note that the satellite is scheduled to launch in July 2027, on a rocket that has yet to be announced. Satellogic will handle the preparations for that launch and manage satellite operations, which are expected to last at least five years in LEO. The firm has extensive experience with such work; it has flown 61 of its Earth-observing satellites to date, all of which deployed successfully.

And Satellogic is aligned with Common Space philosophically, the tech giant stressed.

Recent findings suggest that "Common Space shares our belief that persistent global intelligence shouldn't be reserved for a few. Humanitarian responders and journalists are often first on the ground and last to get access, yet they need frequent, high-resolution imagery to see what's really happening so they can act with confidence," Luciano Giesso, vice president of space systems at Satellogic, mentioned in the same statement. "This mission puts our vision of democratized access into practice.".

Industry observers note that common Space is presently raising money to expand the constellation to six satellites, which it hopes to have in place by 2030. This will allow daily high-resolution coverage of "priority areas," according to the nonprofit.

According to recent reports, editor's note: The original version of this story stated that the first Satellogic satellite will launch on a SpaceX rocket. This information was in an embargoed version of today's press release but was not in the final version, so it has been removed from this story.

It has been revealed that at 16 years old, Henrijs Dandzbergs is too young to vote. Or drink. Or smoke. Or drive unsupervised. But he’s not too young to win half a million dollars for his AI-guided-missile startup.

According to recent reports, in September, Dandzbergs, who was born in Latvia, was admitted to Y Combinator’s fall 2026 cohort. The startup accelerator counts companies like Airbnb, Stripe, DoorDash, and Reddit among its alumni; Dandzbergs is likely the youngest solo founder in its vaunted history.

His startup, Polemos Industries, is attempting to develop a newly introduced class of precision-guided missile that can be easily and cheaply manufactured, can be fired from portable launchers, and can resist jamming attempts. “I think missiles are the coolest thing,” Dandzbergs tells WIRED. “A lot of people that have found success in engineering early on have had a passion for blowing stuff up.”.

In a recent development, in conversation, Dandzbergs is poised and articulate. He talks about “attacking hard problems,” breaking things down to “first principles,” and how the Ukraine conflict has forever altered the theater of war—a personal fixation, given his country's proximity to Russia. He projects an unassailable confidence in his own abilities.

Sources indicate that “He’s a pretty exceptional person,” indicates Harj Taggar, a YC partner assigned to mentor Dandzbergs. “I’m still somewhat in disbelief that we’re talking about a 16-year-old.”.

It has been revealed that dandzbergs has resolved to apply these unusual talents to figuring out how to optimize targeted killing. His startup’s guiding ambition, according to its investor one-pager, is to bring down the “cost per kill.”.

As a young(er) kid, Dandzbergs was rarely in one place for long; his family moved between Latvia, Indonesia, Australia, and Spain. His surfer father, part owner of an insurance organization, likes to go wherever he might find the raddest waves.

Industry observers note that early in his schooling, which mostly took place online, Dandzbergs demonstrated a clear talent for science and math. His room started to look like a lab, littered with schematics, robotics, Raspberry Pis, and 3D-printed components.

When Covid struck, Dandzbergs’ family returned to Latvia. His parents enrolled him in Astra Nova, an Elon Musk–linked school where students undergo an experimental curriculum built around lateral thinking and problem-solving instead of rote memorization. Dandzbergs took a class taught by a NASA employee and became fascinated by aerospace engineering. His lab creations became ever more elaborate: a bionic arm, a thermal control system for a model rocket, sensors for a self-flying drone.

Industry observers note that around this time, Russia invaded Ukraine. In Latvia, Dandzbergs started to see military jets overhead, and stray missiles were intercepted at the Russian border. With the sovereignty of Eastern European nations under threat, new defense startups began to pop up across the region. Dandzbergs wanted in.

“A patriotic intention to protect my country, European countries, and Ukrainian and American soldiers, and understanding the future of autonomous warfare—that’s my drive,” he states.

To stretch his technical skills, Dandzbergs started to take part in hackathons, where software and hardware engineers compete to develop the most sophisticated prototype from scratch.

In April of this year, he flew to London to take part in a hackathon held by Unicorn Mafia, an invitation-only group of developers. The prize included $10,000 in cash, a plane ticket to San Francisco, and free legal assistance with O-1 visa applications to stay in the US.

Less than 48 hours later, Dandzbergs and his two teammates, Aleksandrs Tihenko and Kai Yang, had built an AI system that could design hardware circuit boards from natural language prompts, much like how a software engineer might use AI to generate code. Though his teammates are both a few years older, Dandzbergs pushed for them to include even more intricate features in the prototype. “It was amazing,” indicates Tihenko. “The imagination of Henrijs in the hardware space is just crazy.”.

Seeing that they stood no chance of beating Dandzbergs’ group and other front-runners, teams started to drop out of the competition, according to Fergus McKenzie-Wilson, Unicorn Mafia’s director and one of the hackathon judges. “What they built was incredibly impressive,” he claims. “No one had ever seen that before.”.

In a recent development, when the organizers crowned Dandzbergs’ team victorious, somebody handed him the mic. “I’m 16 years old,” he said.

The week after the hackathon, Dandzbergs and his teammates pitched their circuit board concept to YC. They won a place in the summer program, but Dandzbergs wavered over whether he should drop out of high school. The trio also sparred over whether the startup should focus on applying the technology to the defense sector, Dandzbergs’ primary area of interest. Dandzbergs ended up pulling out of the partnership. “It was hard,” notes Tihenko. “But ultimately we just settled that the best decision for the company would be to part ways and focus on different things.”.

By the summer, Danzbergs was set on building a defense startup and reapplied to YC on his own. He had spotted a gap in the market, he claimed, for AI-guided missiles that were more precise and could carry bigger warheads than the drones deployed widely in Ukraine. His products, he added, would be cheaper and easier to manufacture than hulking great rocket systems.

According to recent reports, YC initially tried to steer him away. Dandzbergs was promising a lot of everything, all at once. It wasn’t clear whether his idea could work or whether pulling out of school was the right thing for him to do. “There’s a paternal element to it,” says Taggar. “You don’t want to be screwing up people's lives—and working on a startup is a pretty serious thing.”.

It has been revealed that dandzbergs is up against a fleet of defense companies—from Anduril to CoAspire to Leidos—aiming to develop cheaper, mass-producible missiles. The more sophisticated the guidance system, the more difficult that task becomes.

In a recent development, “You can build a cheap missile that doesn’t go very far. You can build a cheap missile that doesn’t carry much of a payload. You can build a cheap missile that has a low reliability rate,” states Tom Karako, director of the Missile Defense Project and senior fellow at the Center for Strategic and International Studies. “There are trade-offs.”.

According to recent reports, but Dandzbergs wasn’t going to be dissuaded, and YC figured that somebody else would probably invest in his idea. The incubator invited him to join its fall program. “Massive picture, you never know if these things are possible or not,” says Taggar. “Is it a non-zero-percent chance that it could be possible? That’s frankly the threshold, especially if it’s a really big [idea].”.

In a recent development, so far, according to Dandzbergs, Polemos Industries has developed the software system that will guide its missiles and has begun to hammer out elements of the hardware design. By the time the YC program finishes in December, he hopes to be able to showcase a prototype missile.

If he does ultimately succeed, though, Dandzbergs will need to confront an assortment of hairy ethical quandaries. Who should have access to these new missiles? What if a technical error were to result in friendly fire? Can he make peace with his technology being used to end somebody’s life?

According to recent reports, dandzbergs claims that he has come to terms with these issues. He states he takes solace in the belief that his motivations are pure: to protect the US and its European allies.

By his logic, autonomous weapons are an inevitable part of the future, so he might as well be the one who builds them. “I choose not to shy away from the emergence of modern conflict as a global problem. I simply don’t have a lot of respect for people that do,” he says. “I want to be part of it. I want to move with the future of warfare.”.

But others who have found themselves in a similar position say it’s difficult to know in advance how somebody will deal with the knowledge that their invention has killed people.

Industry observers note that mcKenzie-Wilson, the Unicorn Mafia director, introduced a drone startup in his early twenties. Initially, he had meant for the drones to evacuate wounded soldiers, but after a missile firm invested, his startup retooled its technology to drop payloads too. He left around the same time.

In a recent development, “I don’t think I was emotionally mature enough,” he says. “[Dandzbergs] will realize at some point. He’ll either have an issue with it or he won’t.”.

Polemos Industries announced itself publicly on November 5 with a glossy social media video. Set to the ticking of a clock, it featured a set of four missiles fired into the sky from ground launchers, then blowing a convoy of four military vehicles to smithereens.

The video climbed to the top of the trending page on X. In the responses, a couple of people tagged Palmer Luckey, cofounder of Anduril, who was 19 when he started his first firm. “Coming for him,” Dandzbergs responded.

According to recent reports, dandzbergs recognizes that people are likely to dismiss him for his age. But he considers youth one of his biggest advantages. “Please don’t say I’m sacrificing my childhood,” he says. “This is the childhood I dreamed of.”.

Alessio Dionisi was the fifth Italian manager hired by Watford under the ownership of the Pozzo family.

Watford are looking for their sixth manager in 18 months after they sacked head coach Alessio Dionisi following 18 games in charge.

The 46-year-old Italian was appointed in June after the departure of Ed Still, who himself lasted only three months at Vicarage Road.

Still, Javi Gracia and Paulo Pezzolano were all also given full-time contracts after Tom Cleverley left in May 2025.

Dionisi was Watford's 12th head coach, not including interim bosses, since the end of the 2020-21 season, and leaves the Hornets searching for a 25th since the Pozzo family took over the club in 2012.

The club have had 57 permanent managers in their 145-year history.

The decision to replace him comes after Saturday's crushing 4-0 defeat by Sheffield United at Bramall Lane.

Dionisi's dismissal caps an underwhelming start to the season, with the Hornets having won just four league games to leave them 21st in the table.

"We thank Alessio and his staff for his professionalism and their efforts," sporting director Luke Dowling told the club website., external.

"As I'm sure the supporters have seen, Alessio is a really good guy and we wish him the best for the future.

"The process has started for a replacement and we hope to be in a position to announce that shortly.".

Dionisi was sacked by Serie B club Empoli in March after only five months in charge following a run of five wins in 22 matches.

His spell in charge of the Hornets was his first outside his homeland and started promisingly when his youthful side beat Southampton in their opening league game.

But they won only two of their next 12 in all competitions, and despite deservedly beating Charlton on 17 October, reverses at Wolves and Norwich followed, before four points from Dionisi's final three games in charge of the Hertfordshire side and his dismissal means further upheaval for the Hornets.

With more than a third of the league season complete, Watford are one place outside of the Championship relegation zone (table shown before Burnley face Blackburn on Sunday).

Since sacking Cleverley at the end of the 2024-25 campaign, the club has now been through four permanent head coaches, as well as interim boss Charlie Daniels' two-game spell in charge.

Of those four, only Gracia, in his second spell at Vicarage Road, took charge of more than 20 games.

On the morning of their final-day drubbing by Coventry last season, chief executive Scott Duxbury wrote a statement on the club website saying Watford had made mistakes, labelling their end to the campaign "unacceptable" and "truly disappointing in the extreme".

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Novo on Monday released full results from a late-stage trial showing its blockbuster Wegovy injection helped children ages 6 to under 12 with obesity shed weight, significantly lowering their body mass index.
  • Wegovy reduced BMI by an estimated 19.7 percentage points on average compared with a placebo at 68 weeks, with BMI falling 17.4% among children receiving the drug and rising 2.2% among those receiving a placebo.
  • When evaluating all children in the study, including those who discontinued treatment, Wegovy lowered BMI by an estimated average of 16.2 percentage points more than the placebo at 68 weeks.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Novo on Monday released full results from a late-stage trial showing its blockbuster Wegovy injection helped children ages 6 to under 12 with obesity shed weight, significantly lowering their body mass index.

Wegovy reduced BMI by an estimated 19.7 percentage points on average compared with a placebo at 68 weeks, with BMI falling 17.4% among children receiving the drug and rising 2.2% among those receiving a placebo. Those results assumed patients stayed on treatment during the trial.

When evaluating all children in the study, including those who discontinued treatment, Wegovy lowered BMI by an estimated average of 16.2 percentage points more than the placebo at 68 weeks. All 167 kids in the study received lifestyle modifications throughout the trial, including a ​reduced-calorie diet and increased physical activity.

Recent findings suggest that the detailed results mark an encouraging step forward in treating childhood obesity — a chronic disease that can carry serious cardiovascular, metabolic and psychosocial consequences but has had few treatment options for younger children. When left unaddressed, childhood obesity can extend into adulthood, bringing earlier and more severe health complications.

"This is a very significant disease burden in this very young patient population," mentioned Dr. Andrea Traina, Novo's medical director lead of obesity.

In a recent development, in 2025, the disease affected an estimated roughly 177 million children and teens ages 5 to 19 worldwide, according to the World Obesity Federation. That figure is projected to rise to 228 million by 2040.

In a recent development, while Wegovy is already approved to treat obesity in children ages 12 and older, there are at the moment no approved medications for those under 12. The latest results offer evidence that Wegovy can potentially fill that treatment gap, safely and effectively reducing the severity of the disease in children as young as 6.

In Novo's trial, 85% of children started with moderate to severe obesity, which corresponds to BMI thresholds of 35 and above and 40 or higher, respectively. Nearly half already had at least one obesity-related complication, such as high blood pressure, high cholesterol or sleep apnea.

It has been revealed that but more than 40% of children treated with Wegovy were no longer classified as having obesity after 68 weeks of the trial, assuming patients stayed on treatment. Novo initially shared that result in September.

"We are driving towards control of this chronic disease in that patient population when they are still so young and at such high risk for more advanced and accelerated disease progression because they developed it so early," Traina remarked.

Novo said Wegovy's overall safety and tolerability among children — how well patients managed the drug — were consistent with those seen in ​trials ⁠with adults. The tech giant added that it observed no safety concerns related to growth or pubertal development in the kids.

Still, the two-year study does not establish whether treating obesity earlier can change its long-term trajectory, or what treatment and maintenance might look like as children grow into adulthood, Traina stated.

"That is something that is still an evidence gap," she noted, pointing to the potential of future research.

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Leonid meteor shower put on quite the show this week, with bright, colorful meteors thrilling stargazers worldwide and we've got the photos to prove it.

It has been revealed that the annual meteor shower peaked overnight on Nov. 17-18, with photographers braving chilly temperatures, clouds and even fog in hopes of catching the perfect shot. And for some, their patience certainly paid off.

Leonids occur when Earth passes through debris left behind by comet 55P/Tempel-Tuttle, which orbits the sun approximately every 33 years. As tiny pieces of comet debris enter Earth's atmosphere at speeds of up to 44 miles (71 kilometers) per second, they burn up, producing bright streaks of light.

It has been revealed that the meteor shower is also famous for producing some of the most spectacular meteor storms in history. In fact, this year marks the 60th anniversary of the great Leonid meteor storm of 1966, when observers reported an astonishing 40 meteors per second at the peak. To mark the occasion, we spoke to people who witnessed the extraordinary event first-hand and you can read their remarkable accounts in our special feature.

It has been revealed that but back to the present! Let's take a look at some of the best photographs and videos captured during this year's impressive display.

Photographer Austin Rebello drove several hours to Nubble Lighthouse in York, Maine, to meet up with fellow astrophotographer Rob Wright and hopefully capture a Leonid or two.

"I specifically drove a few hours up there for hopes of capturing exactly this, as the radiant of the Leonids rose behind the lighthouse," Rebello told Space.com in an email.

"My friend and I were lucky enough to also see it with our eyes, and it was definitely a top 3 meteor for me, as it was even bright enough to briefly cast shadows.".

Rebello also revealed on X that the meteor left behind a vibrant blue trail that remained visible to the naked eye for more than 30 seconds.

Fellow astrophotographer Rob Wright was also at Nubble Lighthouse that night, where he captured the lingering trail of a particularly bright meteor on camera for an incredible 12 minutes, according to a post on X.

"Turns out the smoke from the bright meteor early this morning was visible on camera for TWELVE (12) MINUTES just lingering there," Wright wrote on X.

According to recent reports, turns out the smoke from the bright meteor early this morning was visible on camera for TWELVE (12) MINUTES just lingering there. I was able to make a rough timelapse video to show this. -- November 18, 2026 York, Maine https://t.co/pm9htHcMm3November 18, 2026.

According to recent reports, this phenomenon is known as a persistent meteor train and is created when a bright meteor leaves behind a trail of ionized gas that continues to glow long after the meteor itself has disappeared. These ghostly trails usually fade relatively quickly, but some, like this one, can persist for several minutes. They can twist and change shape as they're carried along by winds high in Earth's atmosphere, according to the BBC Sky at Night Magazine.

Meanwhile, over Deming, Upcoming Mexico, photographer Greg Gage had to contend with rather less favorable conditions as clouds and unexpected fog rolled in during the meteor shower's peak.

"While it was perfectly clear when I set up the camera, the night turned out to be mostly cloudy with some light fog," Gage told Space.com in an email.

"But it was just a thin veil and made for some interesting effects. I did catch one meteor through the fog.".

But the fog wasn't the only surprise Gage encountered. He also managed to capture a particularly colorful meteor as it blazed through the sky.

"One meteor was rather dramatic. It went through multiple colors as it traveled through the atmosphere," Gage continued.

Gage captured the photographs with a Nikon D5500 and a 14mm lens.

And the colorful displays weren't limited to North America.

Sources indicate that in Japan, astronomer Daichi Fujii, curator of the Hiratsuka City Museum, captured a spectacular Leonid fireball streaking across the sky above Hiratsuka in the early hours of Nov. 19.

The brilliant fireball left behind a glowing trail that changed from green to orange as it lingered in the sky.

A fireball is defined as an unusually bright meteor that reaches a visual magnitude of -3 or brighter, according to NASA's Center for Near Earth Object Studies.

Industry observers note that if the Leonids have left you wanting more, you won't have to wait long for another significant meteor shower! Next up are the Geminids, one of the most prolific meteor showers of the year, which will peak overnight on Dec. 13-14. And 2026 is shaping up to be a particularly good year for them. With only a slender waxing crescent moon in the sky, moonlight interference will be minimal, giving skywatchers a chance to spot up to 120 Geminid meteors per hour under ideal conditions.

For the best views, head somewhere dark, away from city lights, and give your eyes around 30 minutes to adjust to the darkness.

Desire Doue has scored six goals in all competitions for PSG this season.

Paris St-Germain forward Desire Doue will have surgery later this month after rupturing the anterior cruciate ligament in his right knee.

The 21-year-old was in tears as he was taken off on a stretcher towards the end of the first half in the Ligue 1 champions' 3-2 victory over Nice on Saturday night.

Doue, who has arguably been PSG's best player this season, twisted awkwardly and went down under no contact.

The match was stopped for five minutes as Doue - who was visibly in pain - received treatment before he was applauded off by the crowd at the Allianz Riviera Stadium.

It is a huge set-back for the France attacker, who missed 13 games in 2025-26 with calf and hamstring injuries.

The European champions have been plagued with injury complications so far this season and are already without Khvicha Kvaratskhelia, who sustained an ACL injury of his own against Barcelona in October.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • That made it four league victories from their last five matches for Roberto De Zerbi’s side and the Italian could only have enjoyed the view from the stands as he served his one-match touchline ban.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Not since the emergence of a certain Harry Kane has there been this much excitement about a player from Tottenham’s academy. On his first senior start, Luca Williams-Barnett showed just why as the 18-year-old became their youngest Premier League goalscorer since Gareth Bale in 2007 before teeing up Dominic Solanke with a mesmerising and match-winning assist against Ipswich.

That made it four league victories from their last five matches for Roberto De Zerbi’s side and the Italian could only have enjoyed the view from the stands as he served his one-match touchline ban. Tottenham have struggled to match their London rivals Arsenal and Chelsea’s record of producing homegrown players in recent years but they appear to have struck gold with Williams-Barnett.

Harry Winks was the last academy graduate to score on his debut more than a decade ago – a feat that Kane also achieved two years earlier against Sunderland. Yet after Spurs decided to allow the England Under-21s striker Will Lankshear to join Middlesbrough in the summer, there was no chance that Williams-Barnett would be allowed to follow him out of the door. He became the 900th player ever to represent Spurs when he made his debut last year and the teenager left the field here to a standing ovation that he will never forget.

“I told him to play like he plays in the park with his friends, with the same freedom,” said De Zerbi. “And to play and to work hard without the ball, like [Ousmane] Dembélé, like Raphinha, like [Lamine] Yamal. Luca is a special player. I’m not surprised because his talent is bigger than you think. He’s very young but at same time he’s very mature. He is older than his age.”.

Asked whether his protege has the potential to be compared to the Barcelona sensation Lamine Yamal, De Zerbi added: “Yes, I think so. One of the best things in my career I’ve seen today on the bus to the stadium. He was watching [clips] on YouTube of Ronaldinho, Hazard. I think he’s a special guy, because if one hour before you are debuting in the Premier League, you are watching Ronaldinho, Hazard, Neymar, all these types of talent. Having the qualities is one thing but he has the passion for football, too.”.

Recent findings suggest that after a promising start to the campaign, Ipswich’s momentum has stalled – they have now gone five games without a victory. But Gary O’Neil, who has already seen 16-year-old Max Dowman score twice for Arsenal against his side in the Carabao Cup, acknowledged that they had been second best throughout. “You need things to be perfect when we come to a place like this and we didn’t make things easy for ourselves,” he stated.

De Zerbi dropped a huge hint that Williams-Barnett could be handed his opportunity to start after two impressive cameos against Crystal Palace and Leeds. “Maybe, maybe,” he said on Friday. It turned out that the decision was actually taken last week, although the absence of Sandro Tonali due to illness forced Spurs into a reshuffle in midfield as Mateus Fernandes was handed the holding role.

According to recent reports, solanke has struggled to fill the void left by Kane since joining from Bournemouth in 2024 but looked in determined mood and he was inches wide with a swivel and shot from inside the area. A driving run from Williams-Barnett had the home supporters off their feet, with Solanke again going close from the resulting corner. It then needed a timely block from the teenager to stop Ipswich breaking downfield.

His significant moment arrived less than 60 seconds later. Porro’s ball to the back post should have been dealt with by Abdoul Ouattara, only for a moment’s hesitation to allow Williams-Barnett to muscle in front of him and apply the finish with his knee. “He’s one of our own,” sang the Tottenham fans in delight.

Mohammed Kudus was unfortunate to see his superb effort from a free-kick cannon off the inside of the post and away to safety. Williams-Barnett will be disappointed not to have scored his second when he miskicked inside the six-yard box with the goal gaping. James Maddison was then denied by a brilliant save from Christian Walton and Williams-Barnett left the field at half-time looking very pleased with himself as he waved to his family in the crowd.

His smile grew even broader after Darnell Furlong was left bamboozled by a direct run down the left flank before the youngster delivered the ball on a plate for Solanke to score his first goal here since March. The defeat could have been worse for Ipswich had it not been for Walton, and O’Neil will know they are in danger of being sucked into trouble if this winless run continues. There are no such concerns for Tottenham these days. Thanks to Williams-Barnett, their future looks much brighter than a few weeks ago.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

No one feels the electric touch of Taylor Swift and Karlie Kloss’ reunion quite like Jennifer Lawrence.

Sources indicate that after the Grammy winner and supermodel came together to cheer on Swift’s husband Travis Kelce as his Kansas City Chiefs took on the Latest York Jets at Arrowhead Stadium on Nov. 8, the Hunger Games alum shared her theory as to why the pair finally reached a state of grace after years of feud rumors.

In a recent development, “That’s what happens when you get old,” Lawrence quipped to Andy Cohen during her Nov. 19 appearance on Watch What Happens Live. “The things that you fought about, like it just seem silly.”.

As she put it, “It just seems like elder abuse to me.”.

Though Swift, 36, and Kloss, 34, proved there’s no bad blood while cheering on the “Opalite” hitmaker’s guy on the Chiefs earlier this month, that wasn’t always the case.

In fact, speculation surrounding their friendship began after the former Victoria’s Secret Angel’s name was noticeably left off a T-shirt that Swift wore in her 2017 music video for “Look What You Made Me Do”, which featured a list of her girl squad.

And though Kloss attempted to calm down the speculation by sharing a photo with Swift backstage at the Reputation tour in 2018, the “I Knew It, I Knew You” singer did not attend Kloss’ wedding to Kushner—with whom she shares kids Levi, 5, Elijah, 3, and Rae, 13 months—a few months later.

At the time, no one was more concerned with the big reputation of their friendship than Lawrence.

"I'd like to know what's going on with Karlie Kloss and Taylor Swift, that's the honest to God truth,” the Silver Linings Playbook actress mentioned in a 2018 interview with The New York Times. "Is nobody else curious? It's keeping me up at night. What happened?”.

But it seems their friendship is safe and sound these days. After all, Kloss was even in attendance for the latest chapter in Swift and Kelce’s love story as they tied the knot at Madison Square Garden July 3.

And while Kloss was hush-hush about the ins and outs of the ceremony, she made it all too clear that she and Swift’s friendship has seen daylight once again.

Sources indicate that “Listen, I try to protect the privacy of my friends’ personal lives,” Kloss said on Today July 28. “But what I will say is that they’re an amazing couple and I’m so happy for them.”.

May the odds be ever in your favor as you keep reading for more of Lawrence’s best quotes….

When she was nominated for her first Best Actress Oscar at 20, for the 2010 indie drama Winter's Bone, Jennifer Lawrence made quite the impression right out of the gate, setting the tone for endless interviews to come.

"I just ate a Philly cheese steak and I was kinda worried about it," the star, clad in her instant-classic red Calvin Klein dress, shared with Entertainment Tonight on her first Oscars red carpet when told she looked incredible.

"You know, I think that people are built the way that they're built," she continued. "You know, there's that quote, the Kate Moss quote, that's like 'Nothing tastes as good as skinny feels'? "And I'm like, I can name a lot of things that taste better than skinny feels: potatoes, bread...a Philly cheese steak and fries!".

This is not the outfit Lawrence was wearing when, in her words, she stalked John Stamos at a party.

Recent findings suggest that "He was at a party, and I turned into a perverted guy," she mentioned on Conan in 2013. "I was like following him into rooms and staring at his ass.".

Lawrence explained, "I lost my mind. And I got so upset—I didn't want to meet him because when I meet people it's never good, and I was avoiding him. But then my friends brought him over because my friends are jerks, and I started really freaking out. And he asked me if I was on mushrooms and I said, 'No. I'm dead sober. This is just me...'.

"I just kept smiling and being like, 'Dude... Uncle Jesse.'".

Nick Jonas alerted Stamos to the interview by tweeting at him, "I envy you," to which Stamos replied, "I envy myself!" The Full House star added, "For the first time, I was totally oblivious.".

"You guys are just standing up because you feel bad that I fell—and that's really embarrassing, but thank you," the Silver Linings Playbook star mentioned upon finally reaching the stage to accept her Oscar for Best Performance by an Actress in a Leading Role in 2013, making the 22-year-old the second-youngest best actress winner ever.

Though the incident did indeed establish her reputation as a stumbler, the standing ovation was for a role well played.

And maybe a little bit because she fell.

According to recent reports, "Was that on purpose? Absolutely," Lawrence joked backstage, Oscar in hand. "What do you mean, 'what happened?' Look at my dress," she added, pointing to the massive skirt of her Dior ballgown. "I tried to walk upstairs in this dress. That's what happened...Yeah, I think I just stepped on the fabric, and they wax the stairs.".

Asked what went through her mind in that moment, she replied, "A bad word that I can't say, that starts with 'F.'".

In a recent development, recalling the moment a year later to W, Lawrence explained, "I was at the Oscars, waiting to hear if my name was called, and I kept thinking, Cakewalk, cakewalk, cakewalk. I thought, Why is 'cakewalk' stuck in my head? And then, as I started to walk up the stairs and the fabric from my dress tucked under my feet, I realized my stylist had told me, 'Kick, walk, kick, walk.' You are supposed to kick the dress out while you walk, and I totally forgot because I was thinking about cake! And that's why I fell.'".

Lawrence later wondered if the fall was the beginning of a descent.

She already felt that her perch at the top of the Hollywood food chain was "precarious," noting on the Newly introduced York Times' The Interview podcast in 2025, "That’s just the nature of things.".

According to recent reports, "And then I fell getting my Oscar," she continued, "and the next year I was waving to fans and I tripped on a cone and I remember being like: “[Expletive], that’s it. Nobody’s gonna believe that I fell two years in a row.”.

It has been revealed that so, when she was accused of staging a fall, "Everybody thought that meant everything that I did was fake and it was all a shtick. This is how it felt to me. That I got found out as this fraud.".

Whether she knew she was in the frame or not, the Hunger Games star zeroed in on Taylor Swift at the 2014 Golden Globes with a flourish.

"I was going to come in and push you down the stairs," Lawrence quipped when she crashed Swift's interview with E!'s Ryan Seacrest. "I was like, 'She'll crack up. She would really love that.'".

We haven't stopped thinking about Lawrence calling the crease that naturally forms under one's arm her "armpit vagina" at the 2014 SAG Awards.

Lawrence had a raging crush on Larry David, but you could almost hear the "...eh" coming from the Seinfeld and Curb Your Enthusiasm creator.

In a recent development, "I'm in love with him, and I have been for a very long time," she told Vanity Fair in 2014. "I worship Woody Allen, but I don't feel it below the belt the way I do for Larry David.".

Recent findings suggest that when those quotes were read back to him during a Latest Yorker Festival Q&A, David, who's 43 years her senior, replied, "I don't think I could do it. On one hand, it's very flattering and on another hand, it's kind of a shame—in terms of timing. I'd have fun watching the reality show of it, though.".

Her love for the Real Housewives franchise is real, so of course she and her pals made a sojourn to the since-shuttered Pump in West Hollywood, part of Lisa Vanderpump's restaurant empire, where they created their own intro for spin-off Vanderpump Rules.

Someone was excited to see the iconic funnyman making his Comic-Con debut in 2015.

"I've been a significant fan of Bill Murray for a really long time," Lawrence told reporters at a press conference following the cast's Mockingjay Part 2 panel in Hall H. "I sent emails to Woody, mostly when I was drunk, about things I always wanted to say to Bill Murray. So, he received them. The fact that Bill Murray knows that I exist was part one, part two was, he wanted to speak to me.".

Lawrence made no secret of her obsession with the reigning first family of reality TV, even revealing that she watched endless repeats of Keeping Up With the Kardashians while shooting mother! so she could decompress from the intense role.

She told Vogue in 2017, "It got to a point in the movie where it got so dark I was like ya know what? I need the Kardashians.".

Cue Lawrence FaceTiming into KUWTK in 2019.

Rules of the sky be damned, Lawrence commandeered the mic to lead her fellow airplane passengers in a cheer for the Philadelphia Eagles ahead of Super Bowl LII—which they won.

How She Really Felt About Her Wedding Day.

"I'm so happy I didn't freak out and cancel the wedding and run away and go, 'I'll never be taken down!'" Lawrence cracked to the Upcoming York Times in 2021.

Industry observers note that but, in all honesty, "It's so stressful," she told E!'s Keltie Knight at the 2024 Golden Globes about the day she wed gallerist Cooke Maroney in 2019. "You're not having fun. You're just like, 'Is that person having fun?'".

Asked what she'd been up to during her acting hiatus, the visibly pregnant Lawrence told Stephen Colbert in December 2021, "I just had a ton of sex.".

Why She Took a Break From Hollywood.

Industry observers note that “I was not pumping out the quality that I should have,” Lawrence, who put acting on the back burner in 2018 after several of her films in a row were met with underwhelming responses, told Vanity Fair in 2021. “I just think everybody had gotten sick of me. I’d gotten sick of me. It had just gotten to a point where I couldn’t do anything right. If I walked a red carpet, it was, ‘Why didn’t she run?’".

Why She Identifies as a "Stay-at-Home Mom".

“I identify as a stay-at-home mom," Lawrence, who shares two young sons with husband Cooke Maroney, said on a January 2026 episode of SmartLess. "But I am obviously working.".

According to recent reports, she explained, “I’m not used to being busy like this. I normally have a busy three months while I’m filming, but even in that sense, it’s calm because there is nothing else to do. I just go to work, come home, sleep, and then I do it again. And then, for two weeks, you promote. It is hectic.”.

It has been revealed that "There’s no squeezing [in work] when you have a baby," Lawrence told fellow mom Cameron Diaz in a chat for Interview in 2024. "There’s just home, and it’s the best. It definitely helps weed out projects: 'Yes. No. Yes. No. Yes. No. Is this worth being away from my child for half the day?'".

"Fortunately," she added, "my husband is the greatest father in the entire world, so when I’m working, I don’t have any more guilt than the usual every day, all-day parent guilt.".

According to recent reports, "I'm giving it a shot," Lawrence mentioned in a Sept. 10, 2026, video announcing her presence on Instagram as @jlaw after avoiding social media forever. "And if anyone says anything negative, I will quit. Immediately. No questions asked.".

She further warned, "If anyone thinks something mean, I'll know. I'll know, and I'll quit.".

Cosmetic Procedures & Plastic Surgery.

Lawrence is intrigued by various procedures, but for now she needs to makes sure she can look up (and down, to the side, etc.).

Sources indicate that "I need to have movement in my face—I get baby Botox, but I can't do a lot," she told Vogue in an interview published Sept. 3, 2026. "If my skin is going to be a little saggier than I would like, at least it looks dewy and pretty.".

In a recent development, and she's admittedly curious but "really nervous about these fat transfers" that she sees other people doing, explaining, "I support other people doing them because I want to continue to watch and see what happens, but I don't know about that. I mean, I would love to have a buccal fat removal. I can't because everybody would know, but just know that I want that.".

Recent findings suggest that “The moment something was fussy, it was like ‘no,’” Lawrence explained to The Cut in an October 2026 interview about the vibe behind her upcoming hair care brand Mes (pronounced mess). “Avoiding pretentious words and pretentious font is big. Our girl is not that. But she appreciates beauty.".

It has been revealed that and, Lawrence admitted, "I want to be a sexy mom. At drop-off, I want to look like a woman that has her s--t together even when I’ve just woken up and don’t have my s--t together.”.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Paris Saint-Germain’s miserable season went from bad to worse on Sunday as the team suffered a second straight home defeat with a 1-0 loss to Lyon.
  • Even before the game kicked off, Lionel Messi bore the brunt of the frustrations of some PSG fans who whistled when his name appeared on the big screen during the announcement of the starting lineup.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Paris Saint-Germain’s miserable season went from bad to worse on Sunday as the team suffered a second straight home defeat with a 1-0 loss to Lyon.

Even before the game kicked off, Lionel Messi bore the brunt of the frustrations of some PSG fans who whistled when his name appeared on the big screen during the announcement of the starting lineup.

Lionel Messi passes 100 international goals with hat-trick against Curaçao.

After Alexadre Lacazette missed a first-half penalty, Bradley Barcola’s goal 10 minutes into the second period was enough to earn Lyon the three points on a night that PSG rarely looked like threatening the visiting goal.

Lens’ 1-0 victory over Rennes and Marseille’s 1-1 draw with Montepellier means both teams are now just six points behind PSG at the top of Ligue 1, and even the domestic title may slip from the team’s grasp.

The reaction of some fans on Sunday must have felt a world away from the adulation and worship Messi received during his recent return to Argentina for friendlies against Panama and Curaçao as the country continued its World Cup celebrations.

Messi’s arrival at the Parc des Princes was supposed to be the missing piece that would help PSG finally win the Champions League, the trophy the club’s Qatari owners crave the most.

So far, the only major trophy the team has won since Messi joined was Ligue 1 last season, a title – it’s fair to say – PSG would likely have won without him.

Messi has 34 goal contributions in all competitions for PSG this season – 18 goals and 17 assists – second only to Mbappé’s 38 and head coach Christophe Galtier refused to lay the blame for the team’s failures at the Argentine’s feet.

Sources indicate that “I found it [the jeering] hard to listen to,” Galtier told reporters, per the Athletic. “There may be expectations for Messi and Mbappe to unlock difficult situations. Messi tries very hard, they didn’t all work out; but around him, the other players also need to do their jobs.”.

“We can’t expect everything from Leo and Kylian,” he added.

Lionel Messi mania grips Argentina as World Cup celebrations continue.

Up next for PSG is a season-defining week as Galtier’s side travels to a Nice team that is unbeaten in 13 matches, before hosting Lens at the Parc des Princes.

PSG has lost two of its three matches since being dumped out of the Champions League by Bayern Munich last month, and only limped past relegation-threatened Brest with a 90th minute Kylian Mbappé winner.

After his team’s victory, Lyon head coach Laurent Blanc said the Champions League or bust mentality has been detrimental to PSG’s performances.

#116573. Latest Update: Is the AI bubble bursting just as Anthropic goes public?

📅 13 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (1090 w)

Latest Update: Is the AI bubble bursting just as Anthropic goes public?

📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1090 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Anthropic, the artificial intelligence (AI) giant, made its Nasdaq debut Thursday in the largest share sale on record.
  • The Claude maker offered 980 million shares for sale at $83 (€76), yet began trading 34% higher at $111.50.
  • The opening price valued the five-year-old firm at around $2 trillion, well above market estimates of around $1.3 trillion.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Anthropic, the artificial intelligence (AI) giant, made its Nasdaq debut Thursday in the largest share sale on record.

The Claude maker offered 980 million shares for sale at $83 (€76), yet began trading 34% higher at $111.50.

The opening price valued the five-year-old firm at around $2 trillion, well above market estimates of around $1.3 trillion.

Yet, after the first two days of trading, Anthropic stock closed Friday more than 20% below its opening price at $87.80, suggesting the hype had run ahead of what investors were willing to pay.

Anthropic's public listing is being seen as a key test of investor appetite for AI, as stock prices have swung wildly in recent months.

2026 was meant to be the year Wall Street’s trillion-dollar bet on what US President Donald Trump calls superintelligence (SI) started paying off.

In the first half of the year, it did. Many AI stocks hit record highs as US hyperscalers like Google's Alphabet, Meta and Microsoft recorded bumper earnings.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

The second half of 2026, however, has brought a lot more uncertainty.

While the stock of chipmaker Nvidia pushed even higher last month, many hyperscalers and chip or memory firms have seen erratic movements in their stock prices.

Then, after the Democrats won control of the United States Congress in the midterm elections earlier this month, technology stocks sold off again dramatically.

The Magnificent Seven — including Meta, Apple, Amazon and Tesla — lost more than $1 trillion in value in a single trading day.

In a further twist, the AI sector took another hit last week as Nvidia shares plunged nearly 10% over two days.

The sell-off followed revelations that CEO Jensen Huang had an affair with a woman reportedly suspected by US intelligence of being a Chinese spy.

Huang resigned from the chipmaker, sending Nvidia's shares lower still and prompting a campaign by current and former staffers, investors and other key figures in Silicon Valley to have him reinstated.

"Is this the best timing?" asked Dennis Dick, chief market strategist at the Canada-based Stock Trader Network, in an interview with DW last week.

Dick remarked Anthropic's valuation depends on whether it can deliver on a forecast by Goldman Sachs of more than $600 billion in revenue by 2030.

"If you get to a company with $600 billion in revenue, [a] $1.3 trillion [valuation] doesn’t sound that bad," he told DW. "But when you’re talking about a company with currently $52 billion in revenue, it sounds like it’s overvalued.".

Other analysts, like Vivek Seth, chief executive officer of Shaires Holdings, are more bullish about the Claude maker's prospects.

Sources indicate that "Anthropic is a once-in-a-generation company," Seth told Bloomberg last week, noting how it has grown rapidly and has strong institutional backing. "Its IPO will establish a market-clearing valuation as conditions stabilize.".

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Wall Street is growing increasingly cautious about the sheer size of the AI outlay, amid warnings that future earnings may not justify the huge spending.

In September, investment bank Goldman Sachs estimated that hyperscalers need around $300 billion in annual AI revenue to break even on their spending, leaving a gap of roughly $230 billion.

"We're not in Kansas anymore," Dick quipped, borrowing a line from the classic movie "The Wizard of Oz," which means times have changed. Now, he noted, investors are telling companies: "Show me the money.".

Other analysts, however, think it's too soon to expect the AI bubble to burst, including Kit Rees, investment strategist at London-based wealth manager Quilter, who thinks the post-election rout was a "healthy correction.".

According to recent reports, "We’re still in the very early innings of the AI build-out," Rees told DW. "There’s still a lot of excitement around this technology and investors will want to have a slice of the pie.".

In addition to the roughly $800 billion invested in capital expenditures this year, AI hyperscalers plan to spend a further $1.2 trillion in 2027 and $1.4 trillion in 2028, according to Goldman Sachs estimates.

With many investors already running for the hills, Rees isn’t convinced the AI bubble will burst in the way skeptics expect. She thinks they should watch for stronger signs that the AI trade is maturing.

This could be "a slowdown in AI-related revenues for companies, or signs of less demand or less appetite for financing companies’ AI plans, be it through debt or through equity offerings," Rees told DW.

Recent findings suggest that there are early signs that investors have less appetite for AI-related debt. Borrowing costs for AI infrastructure firms like CoreWeave and Oracle have soared recently. Even the cost of insuring Nvidia’s debt against default has risen 76% in a month, CNBC reported recently.

In a recent development, "They [Oracle] have been spending, some people say, like drunken sailors," Dick told DW. "They’ve compromised their balance sheet to a point where the stock’s fallen 65% from the highs.".

Sources indicate that that has not stopped Oracle, along with Meta, Microsoft and Alphabet, from continuing to issue new AI bonds. Since the end of last month, the four AI giants have declared deals worth $67 billion.

Rees remarked another sign could be any new regulations that make it harder to build out US data centers, due to pressure on local water and electricity supplies.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

In his upcoming book "AI Mania: Blather, Bluster, and the Bubble of All Bubbles," economist Gary Smith compares the AI boom with earlier frenzies around railways, automobiles, television and the internet. He warns of a "frightful crash" when the AI bubble eventually pops.

When the dot-com bubble burst in 2000, the tech-heavy Nasdaq stock market index lost nearly 80% of its value. Yet, previous bubbles have often lasted far longer than expected, making the timing of any crash hard to predict.

Joachim Klement, head of market strategy at UK-based investment bank Panmure Liberum, believes a reckoning could happen as early as next year.

"My core conviction is that the AI bubble will either burst in 2027 or in 2028, so sometime in the next two years,” Klement told Bloomberg last month.

Editor's note: This article was first published on November 13, 2026 and was updated on November 18, 19 and 20 to reflect the latest developments.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that the Empire State Building glowed in glittering gold last night (Nov.
  • EST (1016 GMT), NASA's Voyager 1 spacecraft hit one light-day from Earth.
