📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that the Empire State Building glowed in glittering gold last night (Nov. 17) to celebrate NASA's Voyager 1 spacecraft hitting one light-day from Earth. And it isn't the only building celebrating this achievement with a sparkling display.

Today (Nov. 18) at 5:16 a.m. EST (1016 GMT), NASA's Voyager 1 spacecraft hit one light-day from Earth. About 16 billion miles (about 26 billion kilometers) away, this is the point at which it takes a full day (or 24 hours) for one light particle to get from us to the probe. So any signal we send to Voyager 1 or it sends back now takes a full day as the spacecraft continues to explore interstellar space.

To celebrate the major milestone for the farthest human-made object in history, the Empire State Building in Latest York City lit up in gold. This golden glow references the Golden Record onboard both the Voyager 1 and 2 spacecraft.

And the Empire State Building wasn't the only major landmark to celebrate the occasion. The Space Needle in Seattle, Washington, and both the Willis Tower and the Skydeck Chicago in Chicago, Illinois have all been illuminated gold to mark the milestone.

Sources indicate that the Golden Record that these gold glowing buildings are referencing serves as an inanimate ambassador for Earth, carrying information about humanity, our planet, the other species who live here, the languages we speak, the music we listen to and so much more. It even includes instructions for building a record player to play the record.

In a recent development, the Voyager mission has, and continues to, make incredible scientific discoveries and observations throughout our solar system and now in interstellar space. But this Golden Record provides an additional aspect to the mission that connects us here on Earth to whatever unknown life may exist out there.

If some sort of life forms out in the cosmos were to ever come across Voyager and its Golden Record at any point in the distant future, they might learn a little bit about our small blue dot.

Chelsea Gohd served as a Senior Writer for Space.com from 2018 to 2022 before returning in 2026, covering everything from climate change to planetary science and human spaceflight in both articles and on-camera in videos. With a M.S. in Biology, Chelsea has written and worked for institutions including NASA JPL, the American Museum of Natural History, Scientific American, Discover Magazine Blog, Astronomy Magazine, and Live Science. When not writing, editing or filming something space-y, Gohd is writing music and performing as Foxanne, even launching a song to space in 2021 with Inspiration4. 📖 Baca
General 📈 Bullish 🌐 Theguardian ↗ Open Full Page

Champion’s corner: KC Current win first NWSL Championship with 2-1 stunner over Spirit

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1014 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Theguardian

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Debinha, Trinity Rodman trade goals in stoppage time.
  • Washington Spirit lose third consecutive NWSL final.
  • It took five years, 90 minutes and a goal for the ages, but the Kansas City Current have their first-ever NWSL championship.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Current’s opener came direct from a corner kick.

Debinha, Trinity Rodman trade goals in stoppage time.

Washington Spirit lose third consecutive NWSL final.

Read Jeff Rueter’s minute-by-minute report.

It took five years, 90 minutes and a goal for the ages, but the Kansas City Current have their first-ever NWSL championship.

Riding a wave of momentum created by a 54th-minute Olimpico from midfielder Vanessa DiBernardo, and capping it off with an all-important breakaway winner from Debinha, the Current silenced the partisan, sellout crowd at the heavily-favored Washington Spirit’s home ground with a 2-1 victory on Saturday.

The Spirit, heartbroken at the final whistle, have now lost three consecutive NWSL Championships.

Recent findings suggest that “Obviously this one hates way worse than any of the other ones,” forward Trinity Rodman noted afterward. “I don’t even think you have words in this moment — it is too fresh.”.

DiBernardo’s goal was stunning, a driven, bent corner kick played to the far post that eluded Spirit goalkeeper Sandy MacIver, her defenders and Current forward Haley Hopkins, potentially DiBernardo’s intended target. The Spirit’s players and fans alike pleaded with center referee Joshua Encarnación, suggesting he examine the play on VAR for obstruction, as MacIver had potentially been screened. The review never came.

Industry observers note that whether played directly on goal intentionally or otherwise, the effort will go down as one of the most memorable in NWSL Championship history. At 34, DiBernardo becomes the oldest player in league history to score in a final, and was later named the match’s MVP.

Industry observers note that “I’ve been to the game a few times and haven’t won, but this one just felt a little lighter,” said DiBernardo, who gave birth to Charlie, her first child, in January and took time off before returning to the Current in March. “I think just having Charlie, it just brings a different perspective on life. I knew the game was big and it was a big moment, but just kinda having her, just spending the day with her, it just felt really special.”.

In a recent development, the game’s early phases were forgettable save for one incident which would go on to affect the remainder of the match: a bruising, high-speed tackle on Rodman by Current defender Laney Rouse in the fifth minute. The challenge sent Rodman flying and appeared to injure her left elbow; the Spirit forward, nearing tears, spent much of the first half in visible pain and seemingly never fully recovered. Rouse was not cautioned for the challenge.

Recent findings suggest that “[It helped set the tone] in the sense that it hurt really bad, yes,” Rodman noted. “As a team, you always want to put the first hit in. You’re taught to do that. Credit to them. I wish I was the one who put her on the ground. They did a really good job at setting the tone and controlling the first half.”.

Industry observers note that it was far from the game’s only physical moment. Neither team managed to settle into any meaningful rhythm during an opening 45 that felt at times more like a title fight than a title match. Encarnación, involved in his first NWSL final, called a very tight match and the near-constant stoppages in play were the defining characteristic of a sometimes ugly opening phase. In many ways it was not entirely his fault: the message-sending start from KC and the Spirit’s subsequent response often compelled him to act. The 19 combined first-half fouls between both sides were the most in any half of any NWSL title match in league history.

According to recent reports, “It felt like we couldn’t play more than two minutes without a whistle,” Rodman remarked. “We were fouling, they were true calls for sure — but I think you lose control of the game really quickly that way ... It definitely messed with our rhythm a little bit.”.

According to recent reports, paradoxically, though, the match was won with speed. Deep into second-half stoppage time, the Current found their eventual match-winner on a breakaway. After doggedly winning back possession after a Spirit free kick late on, Kansas City forward Debinha streaked upfield from just beyond the center stripe, looking off a wide-open Temwa Chawinga and rounding MacIver who looked on hopelessly as the Brazilian slotted it home.

In a recent development, moments later, Rodman – somehow still in the match after not only the early challenge but a later high-speed collision with Current goalkeeper Lorena – pulled one back for the Spirit. Falling away from goal 10 yards out, Rodman got her head on the end of a Tara Rudd cross, placing it perfectly over Lorena’s outstretched arms and into the far-side netting. The ensuing five minutes – the game ended in the 102nd – were chaotic but the Spirit couldn’t quite find the equalizer.

After a slow start, the Current were well-managed by former Major League Soccer and US national team member Chris Armas. Armas was widely considered a controversial selection at the time of his appointment but proceeded to lead the club to their first championship in his first season, doing so by beating Gotham FC and now the Spirit, two sides picked by many as potential league-winners.

“I think from the front to the back we made it a point that every person on this team defends and if somebody is going to make a mistake the other person is going to have their back,” Current defender Izzy Rodriguez remarked. “We try and turn every 1v1 situation into a 1v2 for us, and I think that showed up today. We were winning our duels and second balls and those are things that win games.”.

Recent findings suggest that for the Spirit, the loss is devastating. They become the first American professional club – men’s or women’s – to lose three consecutive finals since the New England Revolution of Major League Soccer, who did so in the mid 2000s. In their five Championship appearances, the Spirit have won just one time, in 2021.

#116569. Industry News: iOS 27.3 Apple Intelligence, Siri AI usage limits: What to know

📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 7m • 📚 Deep Dive (1305 w)
📖 Baca
AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Mashable ↗ Open Full Page

Industry News: iOS 27.3 Apple Intelligence, Siri AI usage limits: What to know

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1305 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Mashable

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • All good things must come to an end implement usage limits.
  • Just a few months after Apple finally launched the long-awaited Siri AI, its upgraded voice assistant powered by Apple Intelligence, the tech giant will now implement daily usage limits.
  • Industry observers note that what does this mean?
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

All good things must come to an end implement usage limits.

Just a few months after Apple finally launched the long-awaited Siri AI, its upgraded voice assistant powered by Apple Intelligence, the tech giant will now implement daily usage limits. These fresh restrictions will be implemented along with the launch of iOS 27.3.

Industry observers note that what does this mean? Basically, if a user hits those limits, they will need to upgrade their paid iCloud+ account or wait for the daily limits to reset. However, not every Siri AI request counts towards users' daily limits.

Sources indicate that so, what counts towards your daily Siri AI limits? How much does it cost to upgrade? Lets break down everything you need to know about the newly introduced Siri AI usage limits.

According to Apple, "Siri AI and Apple Intelligence features are available for free for owners with a supported device set to a supported language." However, "some features rely on powerful server models and have limits.".

Apple says the following features will have daily usage limits:.

Images: Intelligent Photo Editing Tools, which include Clean Up, Extend, and Spatial Reframing, as well as Image Playground.

Workflows and automation: AFM Cloud and AFM Cloud Pro models in Shortcuts.

Third-party apps that use Apple Foundation Models in Private Cloud Compute.

Apple has not published exactly what the daily usage limits are for Apple Intelligence or Siri AI. The company's Support page simply describes it as a "generous daily usage limit.".

Sources indicate that notably, each of those above categories has its own unique daily usage limits. These are not shared between those features, which means a user can hit the daily limit for one but not the others.

Daily usage limits are connected at the Apple account level and are implemented across all Apple devices, including iOS devices, Mac, and Apple TV.

According to recent reports, when a user reaches their daily limit, they will receive a prompt after making a request that counts towards those limits. Advanced requests are paused until the daily limit resets or the user upgrades to an iCloud+ initiative.

"Daily Request Limit Reached," the prompt reads on iOS. "You can continue with basic requests.".

The prompt also includes a button to upgrade to an iCloud+ blueprint to increase those daily limits.

As previously mentioned, Apple isn't sharing exactly what those Apple Intelligence and Siri AI limits are. However, they have shared just how many times those "generous" limits are increased when upgrading to an iCloud+ strategy.

Recent findings suggest that here's an outline of what you get with each iCloud+ strategy: The best tech deal this week The Apple iPhone 18 Pro is free right now with T-Mobile Products available for purchase through affiliate links. If you buy something through links on our site, Mashable may earn an affiliate commission.

The Apple iPhone 18 Pro is free right now with T-Mobile.

200GB: $2.99 per month – Up to 2x daily usage limit.

2TB: $9.99 per month – Up to 5x daily usage limit.

6TB: $29.99 per month – Up to 10x daily usage limit.

12TB: $59.99 per month – Up to 20x daily usage limit.

The 50GB iCloud+ plan, which Apple sells for $0.99 per month, does not include any increase in daily usage limits for Apple Intelligence and Siri AI.

Apple says that all feature categories will have their daily limits reset at approximately midnight in the user's current time zone.

According to recent reports, according to Apple, owners who are travelling internationally will have their limits reset "around midnight in the central time zone of the country or region of your Apple Account." Users who share an iCloud+ blueprint with a Family Sharing group will see their limits reset at around midnight of the time zone of the iCloud+ plan purchaser. Users who aren't signed into their Apple Account will see their limits reset around 24 hours after they first used that feature category that day.

Unused limits from the previous day do not roll over.

Recent findings suggest that starting with iOS 27.3, Siri AI will also receive limits for certain "advanced" tasks. Apple indicates that basic tasks will continue to be unlimited and will work even when the daily usage limits for advanced tasks are reached.

You may be wondering what a "basic" task is and what is an "advanced" task, the latter of which will have daily usage limits.

Apple provided the following examples as a basic task, which customers will be able to utilize without limits:.

"Set a timer for three minutes.".

"Text Mark that Annika's party is at 123 Main Street.”.

As for advanced tasks, Apple provides these examples:.

"Text Mark the address for Annika's party, and tell him what time we need to leave from home to make it on time.".

"Add a summary of my San Francisco trip note to this email draft.".

Based on those examples, it appears advanced tasks involve multi-step requests that require server-side processing.

Industry observers note that beyond Apple's official published examples, Apple leaker pdfu has uncovered Apple's more detailed instructions given to Siri AI telling the assistant how to decide if a user has reached their limits for advanced tasks. In an X post, the leaker explained Siri will take limits into account if a user request:.

uses information from one app, from what is on screen or from a message, in a different app, or needs a result from one step used in a different step or app (such as a looked-up fact typed into a field).

contains two or more separate asks in one sentence, even in the same app (extra details of one action, such as a cc or a time, are still one ask).

asks about or summarizes the content of a photo, a camera view or an attachment (editing, searching and albums are fine).

deletes, archives, junks, moves, marks or changes a set (all, every, these or a whole category) of the user’s emails, notes, reminders, messages, photos, files, contacts or events.

sets a device action or a notification to run on a time or trigger (not alarms, timers, reminders or calendar events), notifies someone when a person arrives or leaves, or builds or edits a Shortcut or automation.

is deep research or a multi-step task done on the user’s behalf.

asks you to compose or create newly introduced content (a story, poem, essay, strategy, recipe, image, or an email or message from a topic rather than wording the user gives), or to rewrite in a tone other than friendly, professional or concise.

A user asking a third-party AI assistant like ChatGPT for an advanced request is never limited, even if a user reaches their daily usage limit for the day.

According to pdfu, tasks like "proofreading, rewriting in a friendly, professional or concise tone, summaries as key points, a list or a table, typing or sending wording the user gives, a single direct operation in any app, even when Siri must look the target up first (the closest bakery, my cousin), 'this' or 'that' within its own app, running a Shortcut by name, a reminder for yourself by time or place, Find My, sharing your ETA or location, and all your home accessories (lights, doors, locks), alarms, timers or device settings" all fall under basic tasks.

Sources indicate that so far, Apple hasn't released much more on these latest daily usage limits for Apple Intelligence and Siri AI. Hopefully, before iOS 27.3 comes out, Apple provides users with more specific information regarding what does and doesn't count towards their daily usage limits.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sharna Burgess believes Dancing With the Stars fans took a wrong turn with the latest elimination.
  • Days after frontrunners Harry Shum Jr.
  • According to recent reports, “Sadly no, I felt it was going to be another shock elimination,” Burgess wrote on her Instagram Stories Nov.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sharna Burgess believes Dancing With the Stars fans took a wrong turn with the latest elimination.

Days after frontrunners Harry Shum Jr. and Jenna Johnson were sent home during the show's semifinals Nov. 17, the DWTS pro detailed her theory behind their exit, accusing viewers of using the voting system to eliminate contestants they don’t like rather than supporting their favorites.

According to recent reports, “Sadly no, I felt it was going to be another shock elimination,” Burgess wrote on her Instagram Stories Nov. 20, replying to a fan who asked if she was surprised Shum and Johnson were sent home. “Not because they deserved it but simply because the online discourse is so wild that [it] was pretty clear who fans were ‘voting off’ and how they have felt about dance experience contestants.”.

It has been revealed that but according to the 41-year-old—who was paired with Bachelor Nation’s Tyler Cameron for season 35 before their Oct. 27 elimination—the issue is much bigger than a single misstep.

Industry observers note that “[It’s] so disappointing to see our voting system is now being used by viewers to vote people off instead of voting for your favorite,” Burgess continued, before pointing to how fans can cast 20 votes per couple. “I say we got [sic] back to yall only have 10 votes total and you have to figure out how to dish them out.”.

As the professional dancer put it, “This voting ppl off thing is so insanely negative and not what we are built on and it's seemingly given fans the chance to manipulate the show. JMO.”.

On the Nov. 17 episode, Shum, 44, and Johnson, 32, were eliminated despite receiving perfect scores on both of their dances. This marked the second week in a row a frontrunner pair—which also featured a celebrity with previous dance experience—was sent home, as Johnson’s husband Val Chmerkovskiy and his partner Jenna Dewan were voted off the week prior.

As for the Grey’s Anatomy star’s thoughts on his elimination?

In a recent development, “I oddly feel at ease. I don't feel sad—it's really weird,” Shum told E! News in an interview after his elimination. “I kind of felt like we accomplished everything we wanted to.”.

As Dancing With the Stars spins into the season 35 finale, keep reading for a closer look at the show’s secrets….

How Much Do the Celebrities Get Paid to Be on Dancing With the Stars?

In a recent development, citing multiple sources, Variety reported in 2019 that Dancing With the Stars contestants make $125,000 for the rehearsal period and first two weeks of the show. If they progress beyond that point, the outlet continued, they earn more money each week. At the time, sources told the publication stars could earn a maximum of $295,000.

However, Bobby Bones said he made more than this when he won season 27 with Sharna Burgess in 2018.

Industry observers note that "That show pays OK," the radio personality stated on a Sept. 2025 episode of Jason Tartick's podcast Trading Secrets. "Like, first episode, no money. Second episode, $10,000. I think it's like, $10,000, $10,000, $20,000, $20,000. It ends up being $50,000 an episode if you last.".

Also receiving a base salary of around $110,000, Bones continued, "I ended up making close to $400,000 from that show.".

ABC has not publicly confirmed any of these figures.

What Do the Pros Get Paid on Dancing With the Stars?

Industry observers note that similarly, little has been shared publicly about how much the pros get paid. But as with the contestants, it seems like the longer they're on the show, the more money they can make.

But even if a pro is eliminated in the first round, they're not leaving the ballroom empty-handed.

"You're guaranteed until a certain amount of weeks," Jenna Johnson mentioned on a June 2025 episode of Kelly Stafford and Hank Winchester's podcast The Morning After. "I think there's different contracts though. I can't speak for everybody.".

Do Pros Get Paid More If They Win Dancing With the Stars?

While Johnson—who won season 26 with Olympic figure skater Adam Rippon, as well as season 33 with The Bachelor's Joey Graziadei—states the pros don't get a larger paycheck if they take home what is now called the Len Goodman Mirrorball Trophy, she noted there's still an incentive to make it to the finale (besides bragging rights, of course).

Sources indicate that "If you make it all the way to the end, you're getting paid the whole season, which is amazing, and you get a bonus on top of that for making it to the finale," she explained on The Morning After. "If you win, it's not like you win a $1 million and split it with your partner. You're just getting a cute trophy together.".

Do the Troupe Members Get Paid as Much as the Pros on Dancing With the Stars?

That doesn't appear to be the case.

On a 2022 episode of Trading Secrets, Lindsay Arnold recalled how her salary was cut "more than in half" when she was demoted from pro to troupe member.

How Are Pros and Celebrities Paired Together on Dancing With the Stars?

The pros get little input when it comes to being matched with a celebrity.

"You get no say," Lindsay stated on a May 2025 episode of Maggie Sellers' Hot Smart Rich podcast. "It's very much just, 'Here's your partner. Make it work.'".

In fact, Jenna mentioned the pairing is often a secret until the last minute.

Sources indicate that "They really want to keep it a secret until you meet them live," Jenna stated on The Morning After. "They want that genuine reaction. So I think people always think we know who we have and we're keeping it a secret. Absolutely not. They do not tell us. They really don't even want us to know the cast. It gets leaked a lot, but they want it very hush-hush until you walk in and meet your partner.".

As for what the Dancing With the Stars team looks for when making these matches?

"It's based on height, build and personality and compatibility," former showrunner Rob Wade told E! News in 2015. "We don't pair people who aren't going to get on. It's too intense. It's not like The Bachelor or something, we couldn't do that. That would just be miserable experience for the celebrity, for us and the viewer. You don't want to see two people who don't like each other and, quite frankly, we have made that mistake pairing people up who didn't get on so well.".

How Often Do the Pros and Celebrities Practice on Dancing With the Stars?

Put simply, a lot."Every day we have four-hour rehearsals," Rylee Arnold, who was partnered with Olympic gymnast Stephen Nedoroscik on season 33, shared on a September 2024 episode of the Lightweights Podcast With Joe Vulpis. "It’s either 9:00 a.m. to 1:00 p.m., 1:00 p.m. to 5:00 p.m. or 5:00 p.m to 9:00 p.m."But the work doesn't stop once the rehearsal wraps. Rylee noted she might then meet with producers or the creative team, work on choreography or study dance videos."Literally my whole life is devoted to it," she continued, "but it's my passion and it's what I love. So, it makes me so happy."Indeed, it's a no-days-off kind of gig."We have our show day on Tuesday and then it's Wednesday to Sunday, straight rehearsals," Rylee added. "And then Monday we have camera blocking and then Tuesday's show day again.".

Do the Pros Get to Pick the Songs Each Week for Their Dance With Their Celebrity Partner?

"Mostly yes," Emma Slater and Britt Stewart revealed in a September 2025 Instagram video, "though it's a collaboration with producers.".

What's the Process Like for Making the Costumes for Dancing With the Stars?

According to recent reports, if you thought the quickstep was fast, just wait until you hear about the pace of the costume department."We meet with the set and lighting designers, dancers and talent and create a story [for each pair]," costume designer Daniela Gschwendtner told TV Insider back in 2017. "Then we sketch out ideas. We have five days, max, to make all the outfits. That’s half a day per costume, not including all the rhinestones. The fitting and trimming we do later. We have about 20 people in our department and then we have a separate tailor shop. It’s a big enterprise."In fact, costume designer Steven Norman Lee mentioned pairs usually try on their costumes for the first time just hours before showtime. And while the department "might use a pair of pants again for the boys," he continued, everything is generally made custom each week.As Gschwendtner added, "We do reuse things for group numbers or promo shoots, but not for the competition. We don’t reuse things unless there’s a specific reason to do so. We try to keep everybody fresh and new in something different every week, so it stays interesting.".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Bruce Willis’ wife, Emma Heming Willis, has celebrated their elder daughter’s birthday with a trip down memory lane.

Mabel Willis turned 11 on Sunday, and her proud mom marked the occasion by sharing a montage of family photos and videos taken over the years, set to the song “Pictures Of You” by The Cure.

“Happy 11th Birthday Mabel Ray!” Heming Willis wrote in the caption.

Emma Heming Willis speaks out about finding community as a caregiver: 'This journey can feel very dark'.

“Your energy is infectious,” she continued, praising her little girl for the way she “can light a whole room with your smile and warmth.”.

In a recent development, “How you love and care for your family and friends is beautiful to witness. Keep shining my love and always remember to #liveitup,” Heming Willis added.

Heming Willis and Willis married in 2009. Along with Mabel, the couple also have an 8-year-old daughter, Evelyn. Willis also has daughters Rumer, Scout and Tallulah with his ex-wife, Demi Moore.

Willis is clearly a doting dad. One picture in Heming Willis’ montage reveals the “Die Hard” star holding baby Mabel while planting a kiss on her forehead, while a more recent image shows a beaming Willis hanging out in nature with his preteen.

Bruce Willis sings with his family in birthday tribute video from ex Demi Moore.

In a recent development, heming Willis penned an equally heartfelt tribute last month when her husband celebrated his 68th birthday. Sharing a video montage on Instagram, she referred to the actor as “pure love.”.

In February, Willis’ family announced that his speaking disorder, aphasia, had progressed into a form of dementia called frontotemporal dementia, or FTD.

“Today there are no treatments for the disease, a reality that we hope can change in the years ahead,” they stated in an update shared online. “As Bruce’s condition advances, we hope that any media attention can be focused on shining a light on this disease that needs far more awareness and research.”.

According to the Alzheimer’s Association, FTD refers to “a group of disorders caused by progressive nerve cell loss in the brain’s frontal lobes (the areas behind your forehead) or its temporal lobes.” These areas of the brain are generally associated with personality, behavior and language.

#116566. ‘Grand Theft Auto 6’ Is a Perfect Game. Rushing Through It Would Be a Mistake

📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (711 w)

‘Grand Theft Auto 6’ Is a Perfect Game. Rushing Through It Would Be a Mistake

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (711 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: WIRED

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that hey, maybe don’t just immediately go to the strip club.
  • Sources indicate that the biggest video game ever has turned out to be one of the very best.
  • It has been revealed that I’ve spent a few hours in the game, and one thing becomes clear right away: This game is a slow burn.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that hey, maybe don’t just immediately go to the strip club. Look, I know that’s what you want to do right away when you start Grand Theft Auto VI. This is a GTA game after all—that sort of outlet for titillation is a common theme in this franchise. But going straight to the good stuff isn’t the best way to play this game.

Sources indicate that the biggest video game ever has turned out to be one of the very best. With near-universally perfect review scores, GTA VI has emerged as an absolute behemoth that has lived up to 13 years of hype.

It has been revealed that I’ve spent a few hours in the game, and one thing becomes clear right away: This game is a slow burn. The GTA franchise has always been high-octane, arcade-style, prioritizing hyperviolence and exaggerated physics that let your character go wild in the digital sandbox. But the latest installation is much more reserved. Vehicles and player movements feel heavier. The characters have deeper, more emotional backstories and motivations. The world has more interactivity and reacts to your actions in much more varied ways.

It has been revealed that it evokes a play style that feels very much in common with Rockstar’s previous title, Red Dead Redemption 2. It was a Western that made the player feel the friction of an often slow, plodding life that didn’t shy away from simulating all the chores of a horse-bound cowboy in the 1800s. GTA VI, set in the modern era, is faster-paced but still carries that intentionality to slow the player down.

According to recent reports, that manifests in ways that might feel like busywork. Instead of having access to all your weapons and outfits, you have to make space for the things you want to bring with you and store everything else in the back of your car. You have to call someone to fix your car and wait for them to arrive. Yeah, you have to paint your house and buy your girlfriend flowers. Get used to it. This can sometimes feel like a chore, but it slows the player down to give them time to examine the world around them.

According to recent reports, once you start looking around and really take everything in, the level of detail is truly unique. Leonida—GTA VI’s mirror version of Miami, Florida—is so varied and splendid it is almost overwhelming. After the game’s on-the-rails introductory missions open up into the first opportunity for an open-world sojourn, the sheer scale of this world becomes apparent. Zooming out on the map and seeing the vast expanse of unexplored territory is dizzying.

It has been revealed that there is just so much Leonida, and none of it feels sparse or unfinished. Every place, person, animal, and environmental asset feels fully fleshed out. Driving down the road, with other cars zooming past, is photorealistic enough to look nearly like real dash-cam footage. This game, as I have muttered to myself over and over again while playing, “is simply insane.”.

If you’ve followed the GTA VI saga, this likely won’t surprise you. Developer Rockstar and its parent organization Take-Two have spent around a billion dollars to develop the game. It’s taken 13 years. The company even delayed the game multiple times to make sure it was polished.

There is massive hype, and at this point I’d say what Rockstar has achieved here has surpassed that hype. The game is likely to be the pinnacle of this era of video games, the final grand blockbuster achieved without the use of generative AI.

I’ve been playing GTA games for a long time. I’ll probably be playing this one for the rest of my life. Like me, you’re probably very excited to dive into this gigantic world. The best way to do that is not to try to see it all at once. Pace yourself. Look out for the small moments, as they may lead to something more profound than you’re expecting. Slow down, and you can really feel how the world reacts.

It has been revealed that nothing else like this game exists. And there probably won’t be for a very long time. Might as well make it last.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that U.S. flights delays eased on Monday as airlines scrambled to get back on track after the Federal Aviation Administration grounded departures nationwide for more than four hours on Friday.

Industry observers note that nearly 300 U.S. flights were canceled and close to 1,000 were delayed Monday, a fraction of Sunday's disruptions, according to FlightAware data.

It has been revealed that transportation Secretary Sean Duffy over the weekend tied the concern that prompted officials to call for the ground stop to a router in southern Arkansas and work to upgrade copper wires to a fiber-optic system overseen by L3Harris Technologies. FAA Administrator Bryan Bedford said the upgrades were part of "routine" maintenance to switch over to fiber optic.

In a recent development, officials ordered the ground stop before 4 p.m. ET on Friday and it lasted until after 8 p.m. ET, marking the longest halt to U.S. flight departures since 9/11.

Hundreds of thousands of travelers were stranded and about 18,000 U.S. flights were canceled from Friday through Monday morning, according to FlightAware.

In a recent development, over that period, American Airlines had the most cancellations with 5,367 flights, close to 22% of its schedule, followed by Delta Air Lines with 3,434 cancellations, or 17% of its schedule, according to aviation data firm Cirium. Southwest Airlines and United Airlines each canceled more than 16% of their schedules. Bad weather on Thursday and Friday had also contributed to disruptions before the ground stop.

On Sunday, disruptions lingered but were starting to improve.

Recent findings suggest that "We slept here," noted Beth Martin, who was trying to travel home to Birmingham, Alabama, from Fresh York's LaGuardia Airport on Sunday at the end of her daughter's birthday trip. The two were booked for Saturday night, and when delay announcements started rolling in from Delta, they decided to make good use of the extra time: After strolling through Central Park, they went window shopping on Fifth Avenue.

According to recent reports, but when the flight was canceled, the standby list for a backup flight looked grim and their original midtown hotel was charging about $700 for an additional night, the two slept at LaGuardia on Saturday. She mentioned they found wheelchairs to sleep in outside security.

Airlines waived change fees and fare differences and offered pilots and flight attendants extra pay to ease the delays.

Customers told CNBC they were booked on several flights before getting on board.

Justine Fritz, who works in sales for a consumer goods firm, was in New York for a business event on Friday. She tried five different flights before getting on one to Houston, then flew four hours out of her way to get back to Minneapolis after her Saturday flight was canceled. Fritz said she had so many boarding passes that the Transportation Security Administration wouldn't let her through security at first.

"It's been bananas," she told CNBC at the gate. Fritz mentioned she made the best of it by shopping and getting a haircut, but she's still disappointed.

"I'm missing the first hour of the Vikings game," she said.

Martin said her trip home with her daughter will take even longer. Delta booked them to Memphis, and her husband will drive the four hours from Birmingham to pick them up.

In a recent development, officials are investigating the root cause that led to what the FAA described as "instability" in data feeds. Duffy noted Sunday that two routers, the original one detected as a problem in southern Arkansas, and another in Amarillo, Texas, are in an L3Harris lab in Florida.

Recent findings suggest that "We are supporting the FAA in its investigation to understand the conditions that led to the Nov. 13 ground stop of our nation's air travel," L3Harris said in a statement Saturday afternoon.

President Donald Trump mentioned Monday he didn't "take any responsibility" for the ground stop.

It has been revealed that shortly after the ground stop, Duffy remarked he was asking Congress for as much as $50 billion for upgrades to the aging U.S. air traffic control system. A day later, Democratic lawmakers pushed back, citing unspent money from existing funding, which includes Congress' approval last year of $12.5 billion for airport and air traffic control improvements over five years.

Sources indicate that "Our committee, on behalf of the flying public, will hold the administration accountable for what happened to make sure this chaos does not happen again," said Reps. Rick Larsen, D.-Wash., ranking member of the House Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure, and Andre Carson, D.-Ind., ranking member of the aviation subcommittee, in a joint statement.

According to recent reports, this sensational saga about a malevolent interstellar society trying to exist within the unpredictable orbital mechanics of a planet and its triple sun system that forms an Earth-bound armada still has us a bit slack-jawed more than two years after debuting in 2024. Now we're admittedly eager for this shortened 6-episode sophomore outing, which is officially arriving on Jan. 14, 2027.

Delivered by Emmy Award-winning "Game of Thrones" team of David Benioff and D.B. Weiss and "True Blood's" Alexander Woo, "3 Body Problem" season 2 revolves around the combined forces of the Planetary Defense Council as they mount a daring deep space counterattack against the San-Ti.

These Trisolarians are not the friendliest of galactic neighbors, and prior to the all-out invasion their primary goal was to thwart humanity’s ability to create advanced defense weaponry in the four centuries it would take for them to enter our solar system. This time it's more about the next phase of ultimate survival and dire actions taken by anti-alien and pro-alien factions.

Season 2 leaps forward 400 years and focuses on the results of the Wallfacer Project, a secret initiative where chosen individuals worked on solutions in isolation as to not attract the attention of the Trisolarian's omnipresent AI surveillance technology called sophons.

While the debut season was based on Liu's Hugo Award-winning 2008 novel, "The Three-Body Problem," this upcoming Netflix offering will adapt the second book, "The Dark Forest." 2010's "Death's End" closed out the acclaimed sci-fi trilogy.

It has been revealed that "So much of season 1 is about the mystery of what's happening," co-creator and co-executive producer David Benioff tells Netflix. "By the time season 2 starts, we have a lot more information. We know there is a hostile alien civilization out there, the San-Ti, and they’re coming our way, and they want our planet for themselves.".

Landing on Jan. 14, 2027, "3 Body Problem" season 2's international cast includes returners Jess Hong, Benedict Wong, Jovan Adepo, Eiza González, Liam Cunningham, Marlo Kelly, Sea Shimooka, Saamer Usmani, Alex Sharp and Josh Brener. Joining them are fresh cast members Claudia Doumit, Ellie de Lange, Alfie Allen, David Yip and Jordan Sunshine.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Messi booked for throwing ball into opponent’s face.

Columbus coach insists Argentine deserved red card.

Defending champions thrashed 3-0 in series opener.

Columbus Crew coach Laurent Courtois noted Lionel Messi should have been sent off after throwing a ball into an opponent’s face as Inter Miami crashed to a 3-0 defeat in the MLS Cup playoffs on Saturday.

Messi’s frustration boiled over on the stroke of half-time when he hurled a throw-in into the face of Columbus forward Gonzalo Tapia, with 10-man Miami trailing 1-0 at the time.

Messi and Tapia were both shown yellow cards for the incident by referee Allen Chapman, but Courtois noted afterwards that the Argentina superstar should have been given a red card.

Sources indicate that “Everybody knows that he deserved more than a yellow card,” Courtois said at a post-game press conference when asked about the incident. “It’s just really sad.”.

Chapman later defended his decision to show Messi only a yellow card.

“The force used was negligible and the offense did not reach the level of violent conduct,” Chapman told a pool reporter.

Miami had already been reduced to 10 men when the incident occurred and were trailing 1-0 after an early penalty from the Chile international Tapia.

The reigning MLS champions went on to suffer a 3-0 defeat, with Taha Habroune doubling Columbus’s lead shortly after half-time before Tapia added his second at Miami’s Nu Stadium.

The result means seventh-seeded Columbus, the 2023 champions, can eliminate Messi and Miami from the playoffs with a victory in Game 2 of the best-of-three series in Ohio next Friday.

“It was a game where nothing went right for us, and we effectively created their chances for them,” Miami coach Kily González noted afterwards.

Sources indicate that “We didn’t produce the great performance we had hoped for. Everything went wrong, but we have to learn from it because next time, if we don’t win, we’re out.

“There’s no better challenge for us as a team than this. It’s a test of character, and I know my team has that character.”.

Joaquín Valiente scored twice in the space of two minutes as FC Dallas beat the Portland Timbers 3-0 in the opening game of their best-of-three Western Conference first-round series.

The 25-year-old Uruguayan midfielder broke the deadlock in the 53rd minute, volleying home a rebound after Daniel Job’s shot was parried by Portland goalkeeper James Pantemis.

Valiente doubled the lead two minutes later, timing his run to meet another pass from Job before redirecting the ball between Pantemis’s legs.

Samuel Sarver completed the scoring in the fourth minute of stoppage time, finishing a cross from Logan Farrington on the counterattack.

Dallas goalkeeper Daniel de Sousa Britto, known simply as Daniel, made four saves, while Pantemis finished with five for Portland.

The Timbers also lost Ariel Lassiter to an apparent injury in the 33rd minute.

Second-seeded Dallas can advance to the Western Conference semi-finals with a victory in Portland next Saturday.

Teenager Peyton Miller scored one goal and helped create another as the New England Revolution beat the Philadelphia Union 2-0 in the opening game of their Eastern Conference first-round series.

The 19-year-old Miller became the fifth-youngest goalscorer in MLS Cup playoffs history when he volleyed home a cross from Jack Harrison in the 73rd minute, his effort bouncing off the crossbar and into the net.

Newly introduced England had taken the lead in the 10th minute when Miller’s shot from the edge of the penalty area deflected off Philadelphia defender Nathan Harriel for an own goal.

Harrison, who came on as a substitute in the 62nd minute, was making his first appearance since 9 September after missing more than two months with a quadriceps injury.

Philadelphia nearly equalized in the 37th minute when Cavan Sullivan turned and fired a shot from outside the penalty area that struck the left post.

The Union fielded the youngest starting lineup in MLS Cup playoffs history, with an average age of 23 years and 207 days, breaking the record set by the Upcoming York Red Bulls in 2022.

Matt Turner made two saves to preserve the shutout for Fresh England, who can advance to the Eastern Conference semi-finals with a victory in Philadelphia next Saturday.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Sources indicate that swastik Chowbey, an astrophysicist at the University of Milan in Italy, spent three and a half months preparing his application for the prestigious Humboldt Research Fellowship.
  • Recent findings suggest that after sending his application to his prospective academic host in Germany for final checks, Chowbey took a break to go hiking.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Research funding opportunities across Europe are receiving record numbers of applications.Credit: Ulrich Baumgarten via Getty.

Sources indicate that swastik Chowbey, an astrophysicist at the University of Milan in Italy, spent three and a half months preparing his application for the prestigious Humboldt Research Fellowship. On 14 November, he stayed up through the night completing the form and coordinating with referees across different time zones.

Recent findings suggest that after sending his application to his prospective academic host in Germany for final checks, Chowbey took a break to go hiking. When he returned to submit it at around 8.50 p.m., applications had closed. The fellowship had reached its limit of 800 applications within 21 hours of opening.

Chowbey is not alone. Many researchers around the world found themselves unable to submit applications last Sunday and took to social media to vent their annoyance.

“It is incredibly frustrating to invest so much time and effort into developing a strong scientific project, only to discover that the timing of the application process may put some researchers at a disadvantage — especially when you open the system on Sunday and close it the same day,” wrote Ida Skubis, an AI researcher at Silesian University of Technology in Gliwice, Poland, on the social-media platform LinkedIn.

Industry observers note that the Humboldt Research Fellowships support researchers from abroad to conduct research in Germany, providing €3,000 (US$3,300) a month for postdoctoral researchers and €3,600 a month for experienced researchers. Fellowships can last for 6–24 months for postdocs and 6–18 months for experienced researchers.

The fellowships and awards are recognized internationally, which is why they are so competitive, claims Marcela Hernández, an environmental microbiologist at the University of Birmingham, UK, and a former fellow. “Being a Humboldtian is a mark of academic distinction. It has an exceptional international network.”.

Recent findings suggest that A spokesperson for the Alexander von Humboldt Foundation in Bonn, Germany, said in a statement to Nature that it had not anticipated that the application cap would be reached within 24 hours of opening. The foundation introduced the cap this year because it has seen a large increase in applications since 2024. It holds application rounds in March, July and November.

In a recent development, the spokesperson stated that as more researchers have used AI to help prepare their applications more quickly, the volume of applications has increased. Humboldt does not prohibit the use of generative AI in applications, nor are applicants required to declare AI use.

In a recent development, simon Hammann, a chemist at the University of Hohenheim in Stuttgart, Germany, supported a research proposal as a prospectiveacademic host for someone who was able to submit their application successfully. He says that opening the call on a Sunday disadvantaged researchers with family and caring responsibilities. “That should definitely be changed.”.

The Humboldt spokesperson noted that the foundation advertises the date when applications will open, but that unfortunately the date fell on a Sunday this time.

“We recognize the impact this had on those who were unable to apply, particularly given the challenges of coordinating availability over a weekend. We sincerely apologize for the disappointment and frustration this has caused,” the spokesperson stated.

They added: “We will take this as an opportunity to continue reflecting on and improving our processes” to “find a transparent and fair solution”.

At a time when Anthropic is vacuuming up stock market money, the AI company has made a pretty grandiose claim about its Claude chatbot's scientific capabilities.

Recent findings suggest that the San Francisco-based artificial intelligence firm published a lengthy blog post this week claiming that its Claude Fable 5.2 model had made some progress on figuring out two long-standing mysteries surrounding black holes. The post goes into an incredible amount of scientific detail that might fly over your head (as much of it did mine), but I'll try my best to summarize it in plain English.

According to Anthropic, the first conundrum Claude was able to solve involved the concept of heating up a hypothetical universe. When the universe reaches a certain temperature, it would form a black hole through a sudden "phase transition," as initially described by Stephen Hawking and Don Page in 1983. Hawking and Page's findings concerned only a vast universe described by general relativity, while this theoretical universe is much smaller and might work differently.

The Apple iPhone 18 Pro is free right now with T-Mobile.

Industry observers note that it turns out, as Claude found, that the phase transition is also abrupt in a smaller universe. As Anthropic explained, this implies that "black hole formation isn’t just a feature of relativity but is actually built into the underlying quantum theory.".

As for the second finding, it revolves around another theoretical universe made up of two dimensions instead of three. In this universe, physicists have spent years trying to figure out how heavy the lightest possible black hole could be using a technique called "bootstrapping," in which the ceiling for the lightest black hole gets lowered each time a theory breaks it. Anthropic claimed that Claude Fable 5.2 was able to notice a pattern that physicists had missed in their calculations and use it to "calculate the precise ceiling for the simplest version of this technique and prove that it could not be lowered.".

As Anthropic was quick to point out in the blog post, these findings do not apply to our universe or have any practical application but could give us an idea of how relativity and quantum mechanics work together. It's also worth noting that these findings were released alongside Anthropic's much-anticipated IPO, AKA a time when Anthropic wants as much public money as possible.

Breaking: El Niño Is Driving a Record Marine Heat Wave Off the California Coast

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (801 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: WIRED

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • For the past 20 years, Daniel Rudnick has been collecting data from below the ocean’s surface.
  • The oceanographer helps to pilot small underwater drones known as gliders that dive thousands of feet below the surface and crawl their way back up, collecting data on salinity, temperature, and other metrics.
  • Industry observers note that A color-coded chart showing temperature anomalies at different depths in the ocean—red for hotter, blue for colder—had to be readjusted because the red shades weren’t intense enough to accurately reflect just how hot things are, even hundreds of meters below the surface.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

For the past 20 years, Daniel Rudnick has been collecting data from below the ocean’s surface. He’s never seen anything like what’s been coming back for the past few months, as a super El Niño fuels record heat off the California coast. The marine heat wave is affecting wildlife and helping to juice the record-setting storms hitting the state at the start of the rainy season.

The oceanographer helps to pilot small underwater drones known as gliders that dive thousands of feet below the surface and crawl their way back up, collecting data on salinity, temperature, and other metrics.

Industry observers note that A color-coded chart showing temperature anomalies at different depths in the ocean—red for hotter, blue for colder—had to be readjusted because the red shades weren’t intense enough to accurately reflect just how hot things are, even hundreds of meters below the surface. Steric height—changes to sea levels driven by heat rather than melting ice—has reached the highest levels Rudnick has ever seen.

“I looked back at our data to make sure that I'm not making a mistake and it's correct—and it is,” Rudnick, who works at the Scripps Institution of Oceanography at UC San Diego, notes.

In a recent development, in Monterey Bay, a station recorded a temperature of 64.72 degrees Fahrenheit (18.18 degrees Celsius) at a depth of 200 feet below the water’s surface in late October, breaking previous records. Other data indicates even hotter water in San Diego at the same depth: 77 degrees Fahrenheit, an anomaly of 21.3 degrees Fahrenheit above normal.

Sources indicate that el Niño “is the biggest source of climate variability” off the California coast, Rudnick indicates. The climate phenomenon is characterized by hotter-than-normal water in the eastern tropical Pacific and affects weather and oceans around the globe. His gliders have captured temperature anomalies across other events, including intense heat during the 2015–2016 super El Niño. But this year’s El Niño is shaping up to be the strongest on record, and its impacts are equally supersized.

“It’s fair to say it’s off the charts,” he says.

Sources indicate that this year’s El Niño is adding heat to an already-simmering ocean. Since January 2025, coastal California waters have been hit by a massive heat wave, with temperatures in some places reaching 8 degrees Fahrenheit above average in August. Add in human-caused climate change—oceans off Southern California have warmed 1.8 degrees Fahrenheit since the 1970s alone—and it makes for unprecedented conditions now.

“This is a bunch of things that have had to come together to make this even physically possible,” Daniel Swain, a climate scientist at the University of California Agriculture and Natural Resources, states. “And even then, it's kind of astonishing.”.

Rudnick agrees. “The heat we get from El Niño stacking on top of the heat we already have, that’s the thing that makes this most unusual,” he claims.

Part of what’s driving the higher ocean temperatures and sea levels off California are what’s known as Kelvin waves. These slow, large waves transport warm water from west to east across the Pacific. They in turn push down the ocean’s thermocline, a transition layer into the deeper ocean where temperatures begin to decrease rapidly.

“It isn't like there's some heater in the deep ocean suddenly,” Swain notes. “It's just that we've turned off the air conditioner and we're allowing the surface waters to warm.”.

Kelvin waves can also help to raise sea levels along the California coast by “keeping the water from moving physically offshore,” Swain says. While Kelvin waves are imperceptible to the average person, their impacts aren’t.

Californians have been living through several weeks of intense coastal flooding and big waves enhanced by these higher sea levels. San Francisco and the surrounding area are under a coastal flood advisory through Friday morning, and waves have reached over 30 feet (9 meters) in height and even set off seismographs. (Another storm is set to hit the Bay Area this weekend.) It’s also contributing to heavier rainfall, with locations from San Francisco to Burbank setting hourly rainfall records in recent days.

But the warmer water itself is also contributing to this temporary sea level rise, thanks to simple physics: Warmer water takes up more space, helping push up sea levels.

The warm water is driving weather even more unprecedented than the intense storms. On Tuesday, two rare twin waterspouts formed over San Francisco Bay, the result of cold storm air moving over unusually warm waters. These phenomena are generally seen off the coast of Florida or the Mediterranean—not in the usually frigid waters of the Pacific.

According to recent reports, “The air temperatures are somewhat winter-like right now, but the water ain't,” Swain says. “It’s an indicator that things aren’t as they usually are in this part of the world.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that the moon shines close to the ringed giant Saturn after sunset tonight (Nov. 20), presenting a spectacular naked-eye display as the stars of the Great Square of Pegasus twinkle nearby.

Saturn's steady light will appear a little over 5 degrees from the 82%-lit moon in the southeastern sky after the sun dips below the horizon for viewers in the U.S. — roughly the width of your three middle fingers held at arm's length.

Moonlight will hide fainter stars from view, though you should be able to spot Algenib, Markab, Alpheratz and Scheat arrayed in a diamond formation above the lunar disk, marking out the asterism of the Great Square of Pegasus in the November sky.

The moon will present a spectacular target through the eyepiece of a 6-inch telescope, as the terminator line separating night from day creeps ever closer to its western edge. It's a great time to explore the 110 km-wide Gassendi Crater on the edge of Mare Humorum as its eastern rim and central peaks throw intense shadows across its interior.

Slewing your telescope over to Saturn will reveal details and subtle variations in the cloud surface of the gas giant, along with its iconic ring system, which is gradually becoming more visible following its ring plane crossing in March 2025.

Depending on viewing conditions, you may also notice a shoal of bright, star-like points of light surrounding Saturn's disk, which represent the large moons Titan, Dione, Tethys, Rhea and Iapetus.

Iran balances ties with China and Russia as Trump ramps up pressure

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (954 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • As Donald Trump, Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin meet in Shenzhen, Washington wants to tighten its blockade of Iran, but China remains Tehran's main oil buyer and Russia offers it political and logistical support.
  • In a recent development, for Iran, relations with both China and Russia are routinely described as strategic.
  • Sources indicate that both countries oppose Washington's efforts to isolate Iran and maintain political and economic ties with Tehran.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

As Donald Trump, Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin meet in Shenzhen, Washington wants to tighten its blockade of Iran, but China remains Tehran's main oil buyer and Russia offers it political and logistical support.

In a recent development, for Iran, relations with both China and Russia are routinely described as strategic. That relationship looks more complicated from Beijing and Moscow.

Sources indicate that both countries oppose Washington's efforts to isolate Iran and maintain political and economic ties with Tehran. But both have broader interests in their relationships with the United States and may see Iran partly through the prism of their own negotiations with Washington.

That raises a central question: Can Trump's strategy of economically isolating Iran succeed if China and Russia refuse to fully cooperate?

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

China is right now the most crucial destination for Iranian oil.

In 2025, it was reported that Chinese buyers took more than 80% of Iran's seaborne crude exports, much of it through independent refiners and at a steep discount because of sanctions.

As China provided Tehran an economic lifeline, Iran also became increasingly dependent on Chinese manufactured goods, machinery and industrial inputs.

Mohsen Solhdoost, an assistant professor of international relations at Xi'an Jiaotong-Liverpool University, claims China is vital to Washington's strategy but not decisive on its own.

"If the objective is to reduce Iranian export earnings, restrict access to equipment and make economic and military recovery more difficult, the United States can achieve substantial results without Chinese cooperation," he told DW.

But forcing Iran to accept Washington's preferred nuclear or regional policies is another matter.

"The ability to interrupt trade is much easier to demonstrate than the ability to determine another government's political choices," Solhdoost stated.

That distinction has become more vital as US sanctions enforcement and maritime blockade efforts have increased pressure on Iranian crude oil exports.

In November, Washington announced Task Force Iron Gate, an initiative aimed at disrupting the movement of sanctioned goods, military equipment and revenue through Iran's land borders and the Caspian Sea.

In a recent development, even so, these trade links have not disappeared. The commercial and security interests of countries including Iraq, Pakistan and Turkey mean that goods continue to move across the region, albeit under greater scrutiny.

As a result, China's role in Iran's economy remains significant, but Solhdoost argues that demand alone cannot sustain Iranian exports. The oil must be able to reach international markets.

"A Chinese buyer cannot keep Iranian export revenues flowing simply by remaining willing to buy if newly loaded tankers cannot reach the market," Solhdoost mentioned.

This economic pressure is shaping Tehran's financial planning. A senior official at Iran's Plan and Budget Organization recently remarked the government was preparing its 2027-2028 budget under several scenarios, including one in which oil revenue falls to zero.

Sources indicate that that does not mean Iran has adopted a zero-oil budget, but considering such a scenario illustrates how seriously Tehran views the situation. At the same time, Chinese trade can preserve critical parts of the Iranian economy even if overall commerce shrinks.

Machinery, electronics, spare parts and industrial components can still reach Iran by rail and road. Such trade cannot replace maritime commerce at comparable scale or cost, but it can keep selected factories and infrastructure operating.

Such Chinese support could help Iran endure pressure without preventing economic deterioration, notes Solhdoost.

But even for Beijing, supporting Iran economically does not mean supporting every Iranian policy.

Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi has maintained support for cooperation with Tehran while calling for negotiations, safe passage through the Strait of Hormuz and stable energy supplies.

In a recent development, A prolonged conflict around Hormuz threatens wider energy supplies and global shipping. China therefore benefits from continued access to Iranian oil but also from regional stability.

Russia creates another obstacle to Iran's isolation. The two countries share access to the Caspian Sea and have expanded military, transport and economic cooperation.

Recent findings suggest that iranian officials have discussed ways of using Russian and northern trade routes to reduce the impact of American restrictions. There has also been speculation about oil swaps and deeper Russian assistance, although these claims remain difficult to verify.

Ahmad Vakhshiteh, director of the Moscow-based Center for Strategic Research on Developing Relations with the Middle East, believes the summit should be viewed within a larger attempt to manage the wars in both Ukraine and the Middle East.

"Russia, China and the United States appear to be seeking constructive dialogue and results that could shape a upcoming security architecture in the international system," Vakhshiteh told DW.

Solhdoost also warns against overstating Russian support for Iran.

The strategic partnership between Moscow and Tehran provides for security cooperation and efforts to counter unilateral sanctions, but it does not require Russia to enter a war on Iran's behalf.

Since Russia is deeply engaged in Ukraine, it likely has its own priorities in negotiations with Washington, notes Solhdoost.

"Russia would prioritize its own national interests in negotiations with the US over Ukraine and Iran," he said.

Moscow could support Iran while simultaneously using its relationship with Tehran as leverage in talks with Trump over Ukraine.

Recent findings suggest that for Iran, ties with China and Russia remain essential. They provide alternative trade routes, export markets and diplomatic support that complicate Washington's efforts to isolate Tehran.

Yet neither Beijing nor Moscow views Iran solely through the lens of strategic partnership. Both weigh support for Tehran against their own economic interests, security concerns and dealings with Washington.

#116548. Musk's Twitter promised a purge of blue check marks. Instead he singled out the Latest York Times

Musk's Twitter promised a purge of blue check marks. Instead he singled out the Latest York Times

📅 03 Apr 2023 | ⏱️ 4 min read (773 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNN

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Some VIP Twitter users woke up on Saturday expecting to have lost their coveted blue verification check marks in a previously announced purge by Elon Musk.
  • Twitter had said it would “begin winding down” blue checks granted under its old verification system — which emphasized protecting high-profile owners at risk of impersonation — on April 1.
  • But one high-profile account did lose its blue check over the weekend: the main account for the New York Times, which had previously told CNN it would not pay for verification.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Some VIP Twitter users woke up on Saturday expecting to have lost their coveted blue verification check marks in a previously announced purge by Elon Musk. Instead, Twitter appeared to target a single account from a major publication Musk dislikes and changed the language on its site in a way that obscures why users are verified.

Twitter had said it would “begin winding down” blue checks granted under its old verification system — which emphasized protecting high-profile owners at risk of impersonation — on April 1. In order to stay verified, Musk said, users would have to pay $8 per month to join the platform’s Twitter Blue subscription service, which has allowed accounts to pay for verification since December.

But one high-profile account did lose its blue check over the weekend: the main account for the New York Times, which had previously told CNN it would not pay for verification.

William Shatner is mad he may have to pay to keep his blue Twitter checkmark. Elon Musk says too bad.

After an account that often engages with Musk posted a meme this weekend about the Times declining to pay for verification, Musk responded in a tweet saying, “Oh ok, we’ll take it off then.” Musk then lashed out at the Times — just the latest instance of the billionaire slamming journalists or media outlets — in a series of tweets that claimed the outlet’s coverage is boring and “propaganda.”.

Recent findings suggest that the weekend moves are just the latest example of Twitter creating confusion and whiplash for users over feature changes — and in this case, not just any users, but many of the most high-profile accounts that have long been a key selling point for the platform. It also highlights how Musk often appears to guide decisions about the platform more by whims than by policy.

Recent findings suggest that although the Fresh York Times’ main account lost its blue check, its other accounts, such as those for its arts, travel and books content, remained verified. (It’s not clear why the New York Times doesn’t have a gold “organizations” check mark, like accounts for other news outlets, including the Associated Press and the Washington Post.) After its blue check was removed, a spokesperson for the New York Times reiterated to CNN that it does not strategy to pay for verification.

Twitter, which laid off most of its public relations staff last fall, did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

According to recent reports, in a separate puzzling move, Twitter’s blue bird logo at the top of the site was replaced on Monday with doge, the meme representing the cryptocurrency dogecoin, which Musk has promoted. The price of dogecoin shot up 20% on Monday.

Musk has been threatening to take away “legacy” blue check marks from people verified under Twitter’s old system since shortly after he bought Twitter last fall.

In early November, Twitter rolled out the option for people paying for its Twitter Blue subscription service to receive blue checks. The program was swiftly put on pause after being plagued by a wave of celebrity and corporate impersonators, and was relaunched in December.

Twitter also rolled out a color-coded verification system with differently colored marks for companies and government entities, but Musk continued to say that individual users would eventually have to pay for blue checks.

In the days leading up to the blue check purge that wasn’t, prominent people such as actor William Shatner and anti-bullying activist Monica Lewinksy pushed back against the idea that, as power users that draw attention to the site, they should have to pay for a feature that keeps them safe from impersonation.

By muddying the reason accounts are verified, the new label could risk making it easier for people to scam or impersonate high-profile users. Experts in inauthentic behavior have also said it’s not clear that reserving verification for paid users will reduce the number of bots on the site, an glitch Musk has raised on and off over the past year.

Musk, for his part, has previously presented changes to Twitter’s verification system as a way of “treating everyone equally.”.

Industry observers note that “There shouldn’t be a different standard for celebrities,” he stated in a tweet last week. The paid feature could also drive revenue, which could help Musk, who is on the hook for significant debt after buying Twitter for $44 billion.

Musk last week also said that starting on April 15, only verified accounts would be recommended in customers’ “For You” feeds alongside the accounts they follow.

–CNN’s Oliver Darcy contributed to this report.

"She’s having fun as a single girl," sister Sarah Jane told Daily Mail that September. "I think it’s as exciting as it possibly could be.".

In a recent development, cast on Dancing With the Stars shortly after her 2024 divorce, Brooks was eyeing more than just the mirrorball trophy. Paired with pro Gleb Savchenko, the two rapidly became partners IRL as well.

But much like their dances, their romance was largely physical. Single for the first time since she was 18, and doing the tango with "the hottest guy I've ever seen in my life," she detailed on Love Thy Nader, meant things escalated quickly.

"All we did was have sex," Brooks shared on the Freeform series, "because I didn't really talk to him that much.".

Perhaps that lack of communication is why he felt blindsided when she confirmed in April 2025 that they were no longer in step.

In a recent development, they weren't even following the same routine, to be honest. "I was surprised to learn through an article published today … that Brooks has ended our relationship," Gleb said in an April 7 statement to Us Weekly. "The last communication I received from her was a text on April 6, asking to speak. I called her today in response, but she has not replied.".

According to recent reports, jimmy Kimmel took a swing at getting Nader to confirm the rumors she was matched up with tennis phenom Jannik Sinner. "Are you dating Italian superstar Jannik Sinner?" he asked during her September 2025 appearance on Jimmy Kimmel Live. Her response? "Is this like an interrogation? I'm so scared right now.".

Though she suggested Stephen Colbert could potentially serve up the truth. "Well, ask Stephen what match we were at," she mentioned of sitting next to the late-night host during her Aug. 31 outing to the U.S. Open. Because, as she noted of Sinner, "I don't think he was at that one. You're close. You're warm, but we weren't at that match.".

What Brooks was trying to hint at in her back-and-forth volley on Kimmel was that she'd found a potential partner in Spanish athlete Carlos Alcaraz. "The rumors are true," sister Grace Ann exclusively told E! News at the Raising Cane's New York Fashion Week Show days later. Still, she cautioned it wasn't exactly love-all just yet. "Dating is such a loose term," she added. "But I do know he’s the man of the hour.".

According to recent reports, and while she was waiting for an introduction, he'd already made the acquaintance of their other sisters. "I'm dying to," Grace Ann said of meeting the seven-time Grand Slam champ. "Such a cutie.".

As for those finding fault with the swimsuit model doubling up with the tennis stars, "I mean, dating is such a loose term these days," she mused during a September 2025 appearance on Watch What Happens Live. "Guys do it all the time. So why can’t I do it?".

According to recent reports, oh, how it felt so real when Rocketman actor Taron Egerton held his tiny dancer close during a March 28, 2026 date night in Los Angeles. Following a three-hour dinner at Capo in Santa Monica, Calif., he and Brooks walked arm-in-arm to nearby Shutters on the Beach to drink each other in.
